he convulsed, unable to think anything, before soon realizing he had done something utterly absurd.

His face turned bright red. As he tried to wrap the blanket around his entire body, he realized it was damp from the liquid he had released and made a tearful face. He was ashamed enough to die; it wouldn't be strange.

Wiping the tears gathered on his chin, Alex slowly raised his head. He pressed his lips together and looked. Nathan, sweeping back his wet hair, let out a shallow sigh.

He also knew that if he were to argue, he'd rather be on the manly, handsome side. At those words, tears streamed down his face again. He was truly upset, but the 'pretty' comment he'd heard before leaving and Nathan's intimate behavior like now were also good. Of course, 'pretty' was absolutely not a word that suited him. He had no memory of ever hearing such a thing in his life, and Alex

As Alex said nothing and bit his lip hard to hold back his tears, Nathan moved his body away. Wondering what he was going to do, Alex cautiously looked, and their eyes met. Then, the blanket was suddenly pulled away. Looking up at Alex, who was flustered after having the blanket snatched away in an instant, Nathan stood up from his spot and said.
"Are you really going?"
"If this happens again later, will you run away then too?"

Alex didn't know whether to be happy or afraid of those words. The premise of a 'next time' from Nathan was good, but the content was terrifying. Would this happen again? Would he show this state again? What kind of adult does such a thing in bed? There probably wasn't anyone besides Alex Yeon. Twenty-seven, a detective, Korean-British, the only one.
"Can't I do it next time?"
Alex suggested a solution. Without changing his expression at all, Nathan flatly refused.
"You got penetrated, felt so much you even pissed yourself, and now you want to top?"

The tears that had paused burst out again. He was so ashamed he wanted to die. Instead of grabbing the snatched blanket, Alex got up hesitantly. Contemplating whether to strip and wash the sheets like this, Alex ultimately chose to run away as Nathan had said.
"I'm really going. Sorry for dirtying the bed."

Why did he always act foolishly in front of Nathan? The first time he'd shown a crying face was also in front of Nathan, the first time he'd acted like an idiot hurting someone was also in front of Nathan, and his experience of dirtying the bed, far from being cool, was also a first in front of Nathan.
The last one was because sex itself was his first time with Nathan, so there was no comparison. He wanted to do everything well, but he hadn't done a single thing properly.

Feeling sorrow rise up, Alex roughly wiped the dripping tears with his arm and quickly walked towards the door. He wanted to run away like this, but his clothes were in the bathroom. Yet he couldn't leave the room. Nathan, who had let out a long sigh, quickly grabbed him. Nathan wrapped his arms around Alex's upper body, a mess and soaked. They became close enough to hear the sound of a heartbeat.
"Alex, don't cry."
It was hard to argue that he wasn't crying when he was clearly crying. Alex bowed his head deeply, his face bright red.
"Really, it wasn't on purpose."
"I know. It's because you felt it a lot. It's not bad at all."
*Please don't hate me, Nathan.*
The words jumped to the tip of his tongue. But he couldn't spit them out. Because Nathan already hated him.

As the fact he had momentarily forgotten surfaced, Alex became genuinely confused. This act they were engaged in was excessively intimate, and Nathan in bed was unbelievably close. Everything, including this moment of being hugged, didn't logically make any sense at all. Even though he had made mistakes multiple times and realized reality repeatedly, Alex kept getting confused like someone who couldn't learn. To avoid getting more hurt, he shouldn't hold onto Nathan, and he shouldn't be embraced like this either. But Alex didn't want to give up this moment.
If he stayed silent like this, he felt he might ask a question he really shouldn't, so Alex said something else.
"Really? It's not disgusting?"
"It's not disgusting."

With a hesitant touch, Nathan stroked Alex's cheek. The temperature and sensation felt good, so Alex unconsciously rubbed his cheek against the hand. The hand stroking his cheek paused for a moment, then began to caress him again. The shame remained, but he had calmed down more than before.
"You should take a neutralizer."
After touching his cheek for a long time, Nathan said softly. Reminded of reality by that statement, Alex finally came to his senses. Awkwardly pulling his body away, Alex nodded.

Nathan firmly separated Alex, who said he would clean the bed, and pushed him into the bathroom to wash up first. When he came out quickly after washing to help with the cleanup, the bedroom was already tidied up. Fortunately, perhaps the mattress hadn't gotten wet; the bedroom, with extra sheets and a blanket laid over it, looked clean. If it weren't for his own pheromones lingering thickly in the air, it would have looked as if nothing had happened.

It was usually difficult to sense one's own pheromones, so this was also the first time he was smelling lingering traces floating in the air. Last time he was too out of it to notice, but he thought it would have been quite dizzying if the other party had been an Omega.

When he said he had no clothes to change into and would just wear what he came in, Nathan answered with a cool expression instead. That's a bit... Awkwardly replying, Alex ended up borrowing Nathan's shirt and pants.

chapters.title: Chapter 78
paragraphs: Nathan went downstairs to the first floor and began boiling black tea, just as he had last time. Alex, who had taken the Neutralizer he’d brought in his bag just in case, along with some water, paced around him, contemplating what to say.

Nathan, wearing a white shirt and black trousers of a similar design to Alex's, brought the tea to the table. After thanking him, Alex checked the time. It seemed significantly shorter than last time, but it was already 10 PM.
"You're going to work tomorrow, right?"
"Yeah."
Nathan, sitting across from him, answered dryly. It wasn't the coaxing, placating voice from before, but the usual Nathan.
"What time are you leaving?"
"6 o'clock."
It was a much earlier time than Alex. With a surge of guilt, Alex apologized softly.
"I'm sorry..."
Nathan, who was rubbing his teacup, answered expressionlessly.
"Stop apologizing. What are you sorry for this time?"
"It's because of me you're overdoing it."
"I chose it, so you don't need to apologize."
"Okay."
It was quiet. The sound of the kitchen appliances running echoed softly, and only the sound of each other's breathing could be heard. Rubbing the hot teacup, Alex searched for something to say.
"Earlier, on the way here, you know."
He struggled to recall the story about Amy Wyning's that Nathan had mentioned in the car. Nathan flinched and raised his head. He, who had slightly furrowed his brow, answered slowly.
"Why?"
"The colleague you were going on a date with...
Wait, you said it wasn't a date."
As Nathan's expression turned cold, Alex hurriedly changed his words. For some reason, he felt a little pleased seeing that expression.
"That, uh, the doctor colleague went to the same school too?"
"Yeah."
So all three of them went to Oxford. It's a prestigious school, and the tuition must have been enormous. A frivolous thought passed through his mind.
"Did you two talk about Mr. Wyning's?"
"Not really."

Nathan picked up his teacup with a skeptical expression. Following suit, Alex also picked up his cup and took a sip of the black tea. The black tea, for which he had never asked to be made sweet, was sweet again today. Still, his insides felt hot and flushed.
"Since I can't contact Amy, there's not much to talk about."

Amy Wyning's was still under the observation of the protection team. Alex had also heard that she got angry when they told her they would proceed in that direction as much as possible until the case was resolved.
That made sense. It wasn't like a resolution date was set, so hiding indefinitely would be unreasonable. The police couldn't keep holding her like that forever either...
"Ms. Wyning's is fine."
"Right."
"And the case... there are more leads showing than before."

Nathan had never pried about the case. It was one of the aspects of Nathan's personality that Alex liked. Most people would be curious or ask, but Nathan was good at maintaining this boundary. Ironically, it was Alex who blurred the boundary. He had brought it up unnecessarily and now wanted to reassure Nathan.

In response to Alex's words, Nathan spoke. The way he called her by her first name and complimented her made it clear they were close. He'd brought it up to reassure Nathan, but Alex felt strange when Nathan actually showed interest and responded. Wyning's had asked Nathan out on a date,
"Amy is a good person."
hadn't she? Of course he'd be curious then.
"She seemed like it."
Even though he hadn't really observed her properly, Alex agreed. His mind was complicated. His insides felt heavy, and strange questions kept coming to mind.
"Were you... very close?"
"Why."
"Just, if she's someone important to you... I want to try harder."
More precisely, he wanted to know if she was important to Nathan.
"She was important."
Nathan answered flatly. That was the moment his heart dropped with a thud. With his eyes wide open, Alex let out an 'Ah,' and unnecessarily averted his gaze to his teacup.
"Not many people specialize in Secondary Gender studies. It's even rarer for Betas. Amy's a rare case."

Although his expression didn't change much, Nathan's voice sounded affectionate. Struck by a sudden sense of loss, Alex stared blankly at Nathan's face. He had to continue speaking. While thinking such things.
"You're... a rare case too, then."
Nathan made eye contact.
"Yeah."
"That's amazing. I knew you were going to be a doctor..."

He stopped talking. He had heard from Tina and Jude in the past that Nathan would go to medical school. The words that flowed out naturally immediately connected to the past. He became a doctor because of David Mac and Alex. The career Nathan had wanted to do was exactly what Alex was doing now. As guilt welled up, Alex closed his mouth. When he bit his lip hard, making a face as if he might cry, Nathan spoke instead.
"Why did you become a detective..."
The sentence was cut off. Nathan furrowed his brow and then shook his head by himself. He sighed and changed his words.
"Let's pretend I didn't say that just now."

Nathan averted his gaze. His throat felt clogged. The question must have been why he became a detective. And the reason Nathan stopped was obvious. Because to answer that, he would have to hear Alex's story. The reason he didn't become a soccer player, the reason he became a detective, were all related to that day.
Nathan didn't want to hear it.
"Nathan, you know."

It was frustrating. He couldn't understand Nathan. He hated hearing my stories, he hated seeing me, so why on earth is he helping me? The question that had been driving him crazy all week finally rolled onto the tip of his tongue.
"Why are you doing so much for me?"
Nathan wasn't looking at Alex. Looking to the side, he quietly remained silent.
"I'm a bastard to you. You hate me so much you don't even want to hear my excuses, so why are you with me... why are you even doing this to me?"
His voice broke.
"Like you said, sex can be done with someone you don't like. But not with someone you hate. I know that much."

Even while wondering what answer he wanted to hear by asking this, Alex couldn't stop. He finally spat out the words that had been gnawing at his soul. While feeling lighter inside, fear also surged simultaneously. Nathan stared expressionlessly at the kitchen window.

The silence lasted a long time. Five minutes, ten minutes, fifteen... Nathan opened his mouth just as Alex, feeling anxious enough for his nerves to burn, was about to speak again. It was after the long silence ended.
Raising his long, white fingers, Nathan swept his hair back. The rustling sound echoed softly. Alex stared, holding his breath, as those thin lips moved.
"You make a face like someone who's been left alone."
His breath caught.
"Like a puppy who doesn't know what to do. Like a lost child."

Nathan's voice grew progressively quieter. Clearing his low, quiet throat once, Nathan slowly turned his head. The green eyes under the orange light were dark. Even though he wasn't making any particular expression, Alex felt an overwhelming, heavy emotion beyond them. Something complex, whether it was sadness, anger, or longing.
"When you make that kind of face, it's hard to leave you be."
Really, his breath caught.
"Alex, I..."
His throat felt constricted. The corners of his eyes stung.
"I liked you a lot."
Very, much.
The moment he heard those words, a hot lump rose from within. It was joy and simultaneously despair.

To be honest, there had been times when he wished he could disappear from the world. But among those times, there had never been a day when he hated himself as much as today. The self who pushed away such a beautiful person, such a precious person, someone who said they liked me even after being subjected to such things—I truly, genuinely wanted to go back to the past and kill myself.
Desperation surged. The past-tense sentence, 'liked,' kept circling in his head. Dizziness washed over him like the time his father had hit him hard on the head.
Now? So not now?
Even though it was an obvious fact that didn't need to be asked, Alex almost ended up asking like that. Taking in a bitter breath, Alex stammered and barely managed to continue speaking.
"Then please, just once... can't you listen to why I did it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 79
paragraphs: Alex pleaded without pride or self-respect. He reached out his arm, as if to touch Nathan's hand holding the teacup. Like someone pushed to the edge of a cliff, he hoped for a miracle. *Maybe if Nathan hears my story, something will change. The urge to confess everything overwhelmed him. These were words he had held in for so long.*
"What I did was..."
But the sentence never reached its end. The moment he saw the painful twist in Nathan's eyes, his mouth shut.
"I don't want to hear it."

Nathan looked hurt. It was the first time Alex had ever seen Nathan make such an expression. Since their reunion, Nathan had shown him many sides he hadn't seen before, but he had never so nakedly revealed a face so wounded like this. The heart that had swelled up like a balloon popped and deflated.
"If I listen to you, I'll probably try to understand you. I always have."
A long, deep anguish seeped from his deeply sunken voice. Even as Alex's insides were torn and boiling, the surroundings were quiet and Nathan was calm. It was so still, it felt unreal.

Like the words 'I liked you once,' Nathan exuded a calmness unique to someone who had sorted out their past. Unlike Alex, who couldn't let go of that brilliant moment, Nathan had made that moment part of the past.

"What would change if I did? So we can be friends again like before? Alex, I believe a broken relationship can never be the same as it was at the start. And I don't want to attempt something where the outcome is already clear."
It was useless before Nathan's logic.

Didn't someone say that everything broken leaves a trace? Like cracks that never disappear even if you glue shattered glass back together. Then Nathan's words were right. Slowly, Alex lowered his head and stared at his own wrist. Excuses bubbled up endlessly only to pop like soap bubbles, repeating the cycle. But all his sophistry was .
"So let's just... focus on making sure you don't get hurt."

*Plink*, water dripped from the kitchen faucet. Droplets gathered and fell, repeating the cycle, slicing through the heavy silence. His chest ached as if bruised. What words would lead to the best conclusion? Alex tried hard to make his mind, which wasn't working, turn. Probably the right thing would be to say he understood, pretend it was nothing, keep his distance, and let them drift apart naturally.

But Alex had always been unable to follow that simple answer. You could call it obsession. If his heart had obeyed his will, he would have done it long ago. Knowing it was the wrong answer, Alex finally asked Nathan.
"Then, after I'm not hurt anymore... can we still be acquaintances?"

With a face that couldn't even cry, Alex tried to make an okay expression. Even though he knew the only feeling Nathan held for him was pity, Alex, far from feeling miserable, was rather relieved to receive even that pity. "I know it's a terribly selfish thing to say, Nathan, but... you've helped me so much, I want to be able to repay you someday, even if it's later. I'm a detective, and maybe having me around could be useful someday..."

If he had to answer Nathan's unfinished question, Alex had chosen to become a detective because he wanted to protect Nathan. Life always takes unpredictable turns, and he thought if David Mac or Jessica Bundy tried something strange again, he could stop it.
Of course, that wasn't the whole reason, but it was the biggest one anyway. So if Nathan used him, even just a little, Alex would have achieved his goal.
"I'm not asking for much... just, maybe, if we happen to run into each other, even if it's just enough for me to say hello to you..."

His voice dwindled like a dying candle. Seeing Nathan, who gave no answer, Alex weakly bowed his head. He saw his own fingers, nicked with small scars. He remained foolishly stretched out toward Nathan. Slowly, Alex withdrew his hand. His arm returned to its place.
"Alright."
Nathan leaned back in his chair. An answer with a meaning different from his indifferent expression flowed from him.
"We'll see each other occasionally anyway because of work, so let's do that. Since we've already come this far."
The sentence granting his request had an unusually long gap between the words. It was a tone akin to a sigh, close to lamentation.

Alex slowly raised his eyes and examined Nathan's pale face. Nathan had returned to his usual expression. The secret facets he had possessed just tens of minutes ago had vanished like smoke. "Thank you."

Nathan silently rubbed the round handle of his cup, then pushed his chair back and stood up. *Screech*, the sound of the chair legs dragging on the floor echoed. A shadow fell over Alex. Nathan, who had been silently staring at him, spat out a single phrase.
"I'll try to forget what you did to me. I was already doing so before I met you."
At the unexpected words, Alex stared wide-eyed at Nathan. Nathan's words sounded as if he were granting forgiveness.
"So you don't have to be bound by that anymore either."

It wasn't a misunderstanding. Nathan was forgiving him. Alex stared at Nathan, dazed, for a long while. *It's strange. It's clearly a good thing, so why don't I feel happy? Can this even be called forgiveness, this one-sided absolution without repentance or confession?*
It must be forgiveness. Because Nathan decided so.
Alex forced the stiff muscles of his face to move. Making even a simple smiling expression was incredibly difficult. Moving his dry tongue, he barely managed to utter a single phrase.
"Thank you, Nathan."
*Please, let those words sound sincere.*

The conversation, which had started unexpectedly, had taken more time than anticipated. Nathan checked the time and told Alex he could stay over. Alex refused. He had already burdened Nathan too much. Forcing out stories of the past, and the neutralizer on top of that.
Having packed his things and come downstairs, Alex stood awkwardly on the first floor to say goodbye to Nathan.
"I'll get going. Can I get the clothes back to you after washing them?"
"Where do you live?"
Nathan answered the question with another question. Alex hesitated briefly before answering.
"Peckham area."
At that, Nathan frowned. His well-shaped lips twisting, he asked in a follow-up question. It was a dry sentence with almost no inflection.
"How are you planning to get there?"
"The bus always runs."
Nathan looked at Alex silently. Perhaps it wasn't the right answer, as Nathan gave a cynical look and walked toward the living room. Then he grabbed his coat and keys. Alex hastily waved his hands.
"You don't have to do that. Driving there and back will take quite a while. You haven't slept much."
"You're going to take a bus to Peckham at this hour?"

It was a known fact among anyone living in London that the area past Elephant & Castle wasn't the safest. But Alex was a police officer, and he was capable of protecting himself. As he nodded, Nathan abruptly turned his body and started walking toward the garage. Unable to do anything else, Alex quickly followed him.
"Really, Nathan. Don't."
Nathan opened the garage door and then turned. Without hiding his displeased expression, he looked straight at him and said.
"I'm not enough of a bastard to let someone I held in my arms just now go home alone. Just get in."

His resolute attitude left Alex with nothing to say. More accurately, it was closer to the dam he had been desperately trying to build crumbling at Nathan's use of the word 'holding.' With feelings he couldn't tell were good or bad, he followed Nathan behind. Like the day he had pushed aside a case with no leads for the new cases flooding in, Alex pretended not to notice his heart growing heavy.

On the road heading home, Alex blankly watched the crimson streetlights spread and vanish like water over the white Mercedes' hood. Quiet classical music flowed in the car, filling the silence. It didn't seem like old classical music. It was calm and sad.

The call from Matthew came just as the car was entering the Elephant & Castle area. Nathan stopped the car at the signal. Alex stole a furtive glance at Nathan's pale hand gripping the steering wheel. Neatly trimmed, pinkish nails came into view.

chapters.title: Chapter 80
paragraphs: Alex flinched, straightening his posture as the image of himself licking those fingers consciously returned to his mind. The phone rang then. Matthew Wayne's name lit up the black screen.
"Matthew, what's up?"
Alex didn't notice the slight hesitation in Nathan's hand resting on the steering wheel.
"Where are you?"
"I was on my way home."
"Are you on the bus? I called because I have something to share briefly."
"No, I'm in a car. You can tell me."
*A car?*
Hearing Matthew's doubtful tone, Alex realized he had rarely ridden in anyone else's car besides Matthew's.
"Yeah."
"Who are you with?"
Alex lowered the call volume, a troubled expression settling on his face. Answering that he was with Nathan felt wrong somehow.
"Just."
*A friend.*

He had been forgiven enough to become something like that, but when he tried to say it, his tongue froze. Alex remained silent. Matthew made a low humming sound, then changed the topic as if it were fine.
"Well, I was looking for the business card and got a description, so I called. After searching all day, I found a lead at a printing shop that's about to go out of business."
Alex rummaged through his bag, pulled out his notepad and pen, and held them. Meanwhile, the traffic light changed. The car only moved a few seconds after it turned green.
"Tell me."

"He's a Caucasian male with brown hair, a little over 6 feet tall. According to the witness, he was wearing a suit like the one on the screen and had a good build. His speech was standard, without any dialect. The witness also mentioned it sounded like a Cockney accent, but they weren't certain. They also said he looked ordinary and was polite. On the CCTV footage,"
his face was hardly visible, so the facial recognition program didn't catch anything.
"It'll be hard to find him."
"After I get the composite sketch from the artist tomorrow, I'll probably have to spend all day searching. Should I come pick you up?"
"Yeah, okay."

The car passed Elephant & Castle and began heading towards Peckham. Just as they passed a gas station and a Marks & Spencer, a distant shout and the sound of glass breaking at a bus stop were heard. Their gazes instantly shifted to the left side of the road.

Nathan turned his eyes first and silently stared at Alex. Alex felt a sudden unease, as if he were being reproached, and gripped his phone tightly. He then glanced at his notepad. A meaningless line was drawn, just like that.
"It's been half a year, so it'll be difficult. I wonder if anyone will remember."
To the obvious statement, an equally obvious reply came back.
"We have to try."
"Get some rest and see you tomorrow."
"You too."
Just as the thought surfaced, Nathan stopped the car. Startled, Alex looked beside him, and Nathan calmly opened his mouth.

He hung up. Nathan continued driving without a word. While a dry melody flowed, Alex, feeling as if sparks were popping, *tap, tap*, inside him, repeatedly clenched and unclenched his notepad. Should he explain why he avoided answering the question about who he was with? Suddenly, that thought...
"We've arrived where you said."
"Ah, thank you."

Hurriedly looking beside him, he saw an old apartment building. Staring blankly out the window, Alex realized he needed to unbuckle his seatbelt. Unusually tense, he couldn't find the seatbelt buckle and lowered his head. A *click* sound rang out. A pale hand covered the back of his hand, which was fumbling around the right side of the seat.
"I'll unbuckle it for you."

The pale fingers slipped between Alex's fingers. He felt a body temperature slightly lower than his own. The pale, long fingers brushed past Alex's hand and released the seatbelt buckle. His body had already grown warm. Dizziness rose up.
"Alright..."
*Do I really want to be friends with you?*
*When just your touch makes me feel like I'm going crazy?*
Frightened by the thought that surged up like a seizure, Alex sharply raised his gaze from looking at the hand. Their eyes met. Green eyes buried in the darkness were staring intently at Alex.
As if time had stopped, he saw Nathan part his lips. His ears rang. Regret rushed in. The realization that his plea to Nathan might not have been the right choice buzzed in his head.
"Enough."
Nathan's hand withdrew. Unable to comprehend those words at once, Alex swallowed dry saliva. His Adam's apple moved noticeably.
"Right."

Slowly returning the seatbelt to its place, Alex gathered his bag. Nathan was watching him. His hesitant hand gripped the car door handle. *Click*, cold air rushed in through the opening gap. The wind was blowing hard. Alex checked the apartment entrance, dark as pitch due to a broken streetlight, looked at Nathan once more, then opened the door.
"Thanks for the ride. Get home safe."
"Yeah."

Nathan said while turning his head. Of course, there were no words to hold him back. Trying to shake off an incomprehensible sense of disappointment, Alex closed the door. Unlike the warm interior of the car, outside was terribly cold. It might snow soon. Smelling the desolate, cold air, he slowly began walking towards the apartment lobby.
But the sound of the car engine starting didn't come. Finding it strange, Alex foolishly looked back. Nathan's car remained as it was.
Not knowing what he was hoping for, Alex stood still. After a few seconds like that, the car door opened. Nathan strode out and stood before him. Like someone who had something to say.
"Alex."
A pale face tinged with a faint purple hue came close. Long eyelashes lowered.
"There's something I want to ask."

Tensed up as if caught in a spider's web, Alex couldn't even answer and just nodded his head. Just as he had felt disappointed for no reason, anticipation welled up for no reason. His hands were trembling to the point they might be shaking. Maybe because it was cold outside.
*What does he want to ask?* Alex's mind raced with anxious possibilities. Though they had no concrete form, the kind of content that simply unsettled a person's heart suffocated him.
"Did Amy ever mention the MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company to you?"
"Ah."

Like someone whose secret had been discovered, Alex raised his hand and brushed his cheek. His eyebrows awkwardly rose and then returned to their place. His skin, which had grown cold in the meantime, felt like ice.
"No."
"I see."
That was the end of Nathan's words. Alex realized it was truly time for him to leave. This place, or...
"I'll ask you sometime. Sleep well, Nathan."
Repeating 'MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company' in his head, Alex took a step back. Nathan looked at him expressionlessly. He was still standing in place.
"Go inside."
"It's cold, you should go."
"Hurry."
*How can I go in when you, saying that, are standing behind me?*

Alex forced a foolish smile like before, then forcibly turned his body. As if persuading his own feet, which didn't understand the newly established situation and wanted to remain in place, he dragged his feet and entered the apartment where a lightbulb was flickering.
He didn't look back.
He couldn't.

Matthew sent a text at 5 AM and rang the doorbell at 8 AM, the time he said he'd come pick him up. It was the exact moment when the phone clock changed from 59 to 00. It was his usual, precise arrival.

Alex opened the door with a piece of toast in his mouth. The bespectacled face standing in the hallway looked particularly weary today. The checkered shirt he always wore had changed fabric to suit the season entering early winter. The navy wool was slightly thicker, a very subtle difference.
"Did you sleep a bit?"

Saying that instead of a greeting, Matthew took off his glasses and rubbed his eyes. He looked tired. When his long fingers swept through his hair, an unfamiliar face was revealed. As a handsome man who could easily be mistaken for someone else appeared before his eyes, Alex felt awkward for no reason and slightly turned his head. "About two hours. You? You didn't stay up again, did you? Are you okay?"

Entering Alex's apartment, Matthew turned the worry back on him. It seemed yesterday's sight of him had been weighing on his mind. Alex thought for a moment. He wasn't feeling particularly good, but he wasn't suffering either. Moreover, strictly speaking, there were positive things too.
He had received forgiveness from Nathan.
"I'm okay. Really."

And if the Neutralizer works well, the pain from the Rut should decrease, so that's like two good things. Despite that, his heart felt numb and indifferent, but anyway, that's how it was. Alex quickly changed the subject.
"Do you want to catch a quick nap? Or some black tea?"

chapters.title: Chapter 81
paragraphs: "We don't have time. The composite sketch artist will be here a little after 9. We can just grab coffee on the way."

Matthew began checking Alex's refrigerator out of habit. Then he lightly complained about why the room was so cold, about how someone wouldn't even know their own arrival time, and grumbled about the composite sketch artist. Alex picked up his laptop and bag. "Let's go."
Matthew hesitated.
"Do you even eat?"
"Yeah."
"You're a good cook. I think you're better than my mom, my grandma, and my great-grandma. How about I do the shopping this holiday and you cook and portion it out? How much would that be?"
Alex refused without thinking.
"Why would we meet on a holiday?"
"We are friends, right?"
Matthew asked, genuinely curious. It was true, but cooking for Matthew was a separate matter. Alex grabbed Matthew's clothes and pulled him to the front door.
"To be precise, colleagues."
"That really hurts."
"I'm kidding. We are friends. You're my only friend."
Nathan suddenly came to mind. Alex desperately tried to shake him from his thoughts as he locked the door. Matthew, still without his glasses, scrunched one eyebrow as if genuinely hurt.

Alex looked away, feeling awkward watching his nicely shaped, smooth eyebrows get all scrunched up. Up close, his face was excessively handsome. It was a different type from Nathan. Of course, Nathan was more beautiful.
"Do you really not think about not wearing your glasses? Anna would like it, and besides, they get in the way."
Probably everyone would like it. Including that person Matthew avoids.
"Anna isn't my type. I like symmetrical people."
Continuing the trivial conversation, they walked toward the elevator.
"Ah, this is under inspection again, apparently."
At Matthew's words, Alex turned his steps toward the stairs. Opening the blue metal door, they descended the apartment stairs that resembled a prison staircase.
"So who is your type then?"
"Guess."
"Illai?"
Matthew made a disgusted expression. It was a rare expression for Matthew, whose default was usually a blank face of boredom or annoyance.
"First, that guy is just a psycho who likes to mess with me, and second, I like women."

Having quickly descended the stairs, they headed toward Matthew's car. Naturally, there was no gesture of opening the passenger door. Alex closed the car door, disgusted with himself for constantly superimposing Nathan over everything.

The composite sketch artist arrived at 9:27. It wasn't that he was trying to check, but Matthew had been timing it down to the seconds, so he found out. With a stopwatch displayed on his computer, he waited for the artist while tracking the numbers on the business cards from the victims' computers and phones.
Anna, who was passing by, whispered in Alex's ear that the artist had a history of being late. Matthew also didn't forget to secretly add that he seemed like a nerd today, too.

While the staff gave statements for the composite sketch, Sergeant Hayden arrived for work. He had gone to check with the bereaved families and people around about the man and the business cards, but there weren't any real results. It seemed the victims had never mentioned him.

The composite sketch by the print shop artist was finished an hour later. After saving the printed face on their respective phones, they split into teams of two. The atmosphere was livelier than before, as a suspected perpetrator had emerged.
After leaving headquarters, Alex told Matthew they should go to the Forensic Science Institute before heading toward Paddington. Matthew made a suspicious face and asked why.
"Isn't there nothing more to come from there yet? Did you find something?"

Alex recalled Nathan mentioning MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company. The mere mention of it sent his thoughts reeling back to the previous night. Nathan talking about Amy and even forgiving words about staying as an acquaintance. A sudden, inexplicable loneliness swept over Alex like a gust of wind. As the silence dragged on, Matthew stared at Alex curiously.
"Ah, sorry. There's something I was thinking about and wanted to check."
"Did you report it?"
"I plan to report it tomorrow if something comes up to support it."
"Okay, let's go."

Shrugging, Matthew took a cigarette from the glove box. Alex easily noticed it was preparation for Illai, who disliked the smell of smoke. As Matthew started the car, Alex asked one thing as if he'd just remembered. It was a tone like someone casually picking up a forgotten item from a warehouse.
"Matthew, how did that thing I asked you about before go?"
Even though it was a question with a lot omitted, Matthew seemed to understand. His hand on the steering wheel paused.
"Still haven't found him."
Hearing his voice lower than usual, Alex quickly changed the mood. Since the content of the question was what it was, he thought Matthew might feel burdened.
"Thought so. Thanks for checking."

It wasn't much. Alex was receiving Matthew's help in finding his father, who was listed as missing. There wasn't much he could do himself, so Matthew's friends, known for their technical skills, circulated his father's photo online or checked the occasionally incoming lists of the deceased. Matthew rubbed his brow and sighed.
"Alex, I wasn't going to ask about this because it's your personal matter... No, actually, I already asked yesterday. So I'll just say it."
"Say it."
"What's going on with you and that doctor?"
It was an unexpected question. With an expression of being caught off guard, Alex looked at Matthew.
"Why?"
"Because I can see you struggling since you saw that guy. I'm your partner, so I think I should know to some extent if something happens to you."
"No. I told you I was wrong. Nathan did nothing wrong. I'm really fine."
Matthew frowned and then bluntly threw out a remark.
"Were you dating?"
"Huh?"
"If it's because of investigation policy, you can tell me; I won't report it. Is there nothing I can do to help?"
Were we dating?
Alex bowed his head with a face that looked like he might cry. He shouldn't be shaken like this while working. Pulling himself together, Alex slowly turned his gaze.
"We were friends."
They weren't even dating. All Alex had to do was just accept the luck that had befallen him, that was it. The situation of painfully digging up what he had lost was overwhelming.
"You and that guy? He didn't look too happy whenever I was next to you?"
"Nathan isn't naturally very sociable. But he's really kind."
"Then why were you so attached at the hospital?"
"Just originally, we were really close..."
Matthew's face showed he didn't believe it at all. With a cynical expression, Matthew stepped on the accelerator and threw out a remark.
"Whatever it is, Alex, I hope you resolve everything that's weighing on your mind."
Alex answered with silence. It was a phrase he had heard sickeningly often from Ian Mac and David Mac.

From the very beginning, Nathan had always seemed out of reach, like someone walking on clouds. Everything that had happened to him had told Alex Yeon that he could never covet Nathan White. As if to confirm the kill, saying someone like you doesn't belong with him. No matter how much he tried, he couldn't improve the situation.
Alex leaned back in his seat with a tired expression. It was vexing how the situation kept reminding him of what he had said yesterday, but now he had to admit it.
There existed an unbridgeable gap between them.

He had to stop mistakenly thinking he could grab hold of what he'd once held again. Nathan would never listen to him, and he wouldn't like him like before. It was even too much for him to be just an 'acquaintance' of Nathan's. That was the proper place for Alex.

Arriving at the Forensic Science Institute, they looked for Illai. Following a researcher's words that he'd be in the autopsy room due to a body that came in last night, they walked down the corridor. Walking under the square panel ceiling, they arrived underground. After scanning the issued visitor pass, the door opened.
"My two favorite people have arrived."
Illai walked out wearing blue surgical scrubs. Following him as he walked to the washbasin to wash his hands, Alex moved his steps.
"Sorry, you're busy. I have something to ask."

chapters.title: Chapter 82
paragraphs: "No. I finished it earlier anyway, since it was an autopsy. You look especially handsome today, Matthew."
Matthew politely ignored him and asked another question.
"What kind of case is it?"
"A crime of passion murder."
Ignoring Matthew, who was ignoring Alex, Illey stood beside him. His ash-blond hair shone palely under the incandescent light.
"It might be your future."
Matthew cursed him nonchalantly, and Ellie laughed.
"Are you jealous? I like anxious people."
"Alex, so what exactly did you want to ask?"
Matthew quickly changed the subject. He seemed reluctant to deal with him. Glancing at his face, Alex saw Matthew mouth 'please.' Alex decided to kindly help his friend.
"Illey, stop joking."
"You're underestimating my sincerity; that hurts."
"You know about the drug side effects in the autopsied bodies, right? By any chance, can you pinpoint when the drugs started causing side effects?"
Ellie wiped the smile off his face and slowly rubbed his chin with his finger.
"I can make an educated guess. I actually found something while checking the Perrin combination formula injected into the victims."
Ellie, who gestured for them to follow, exited the autopsy room. Matthew, who had been listening to their conversation, stuck close to Alex.
"Side effects... So you're thinking about human experimentation now?"
"There's no evidence, and since that angle hasn't been discussed, I thought about it. Plus, I heard something from Nathan."
"Nathan White? What did you hear?"
"He told me to ask Amy Wainings about MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company."
"Don't tell me yesterday, in your car?.."

Looking very suspicious, Matthew tried to interrogate Alex. However, Illey, who was walking ahead, stopped abruptly, cutting Matthew off. They had arrived at Ellie's underground laboratory. Sweeping back his loosely covering bangs, he turned his body.
"You were just talking about Nathan? What a curious coincidence."
Ellie, facing them, reached back and opened the door. Before the sentence 'What nonsense' could even fully leave Matthew's mouth, the meaning of Ellie's words became clear.
"I actually called him here today because I needed help with something."

In the meeting room visible immediately upon entering Illey's lab, two people were seated. Luther Milan in a suit, and Nathan. Alex's eyes widened; he stopped, hesitated, and retreated behind Matthew. He had decided he needed to sort out his feelings and shouldn't see Nathan for at least a few days; he hadn't expected to run into him so soon.
"Good to see you again, detectives."

Luther Milan waved with a friendly smile. Nathan silently looked in the direction where Alex was. His gaze landed on Matthew. Alex saw him slightly furrow his brow and turn his head. Alex followed in the direction Matthew was heading. Matthew, who had sat down, abruptly looked at Nathan and asked a question.
"Something just occurred to me, Mr. White, aren't you a specialist yet? I seem to see you unusually often compared to other researchers. Aren't there others with more seniority?"
Nathan opened his mouth expressionlessly.
"Because I'm good."
Wow. Matthew looked a bit taken aback. Illey smiled, delighted that Matthew had been put in his place. He, sitting next to Alex, chimed in on Nathan's statement.

"That's right. Nathan here is young, but he's the most passionate about Secondary Gender research. Not everyone at the Secondary Gender Research Institute looks at the same things. Nathan is the best at suppressant and neutralizer research. That's separate from the long road to becoming the best internist."
He said.

Nathan still showed no change in expression. He looked like he didn't even care. It was more comfortable that Nathan wasn't looking at him, so Alex also sighed in relief. His heart, failing to grasp the situation, pounded, making him tense. When he reached out to drink his coffee, Matthew asked,
"Illey, you didn't just buy coffee, did you? No mocha or hot chocolate?"
"I naturally prepared some for cute Alex."
At the expression 'cute,' Alex was flustered. Matthew didn't even try to hold back his laughter and agreed with Illey.
"That's right, he is cute."
Luther Milan, caught up in the sudden flow, also joined in.
"You all seem to get along well. I'd rather bet on 'handsome and tall' than 'cute'."

Alex couldn't find words to respond and accepted the hot chocolate Illey offered. His earlobes turned red at the shocking expression of 'cute.' It was Nathan who stopped Illey as he tried to continue. An icy-cold voice cut through their conversation.
"I didn't come here for small talk; I came because of the case. I'd appreciate it if we could start."
Their eyes met. Alex awkwardly averted his gaze.
"That's right, Illey. We were talking about side effects."
While they were talking, Luther Milan smiled with curved eyes and stroked Nathan's hair. Nathan dryly brushed his hand away and opened his mouth.
"The director came to tell you the list of research institutes associated with Perrin. I'll be the one helping you find the combination formula."
Alex, who had been silent, added a word.
"Thank you for your help. But aren't we inconveniencing your work?"
Nathan stared piercingly at him, Alex's use of formal language after so long clearly catching his attention. Alex's pulse quickened, and he quickly looked away.
"Oh, that's fine."
Luther smiled like a grandfather looking at his grandson.

"Since the Royal Institute was the first to identify and extract Perrin, we feel a shred of responsibility for this matter. It started with good intentions, but as things often go in this world, it didn't proceed as expected."
After finishing his words, Luther gestured that they should begin. The lights in the meeting room dimmed, and Luther got to the main point.

"What I've brought is a list of names, hospitals, and companies with the capital and technology to handle Perrin research. It's based on all of Europe, and they are places with a certain level of reputation."
"You must have considerable influence."
Matthew asked, sounding suspicious of Luther for finding this out. Luther lightly brushed off his words.
"Let's just say the people who sponsor me are like that. Anyway, the list is centered on hospitals doing Secondary Gender research. I've separately noted their main areas of focus."
Matthew, looking at the list sorted alphabetically, placed his finger on the name 'MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company.' To Matthew's questioning glance, Alex nodded.
"This pharmaceutical company doesn't seem to have separate Secondary Gender-related products or research institutes."
"Ah, that's correct. They mainly deal with other hormonal agents and tend to collaborate more with hospitals. But there's a rumor."
"A rumor?"
Alex asked. Illey, who had been resting his chin on his hand, responded to that.
"The rumor that they're trying to enter the field of Secondary Gender medications, including suppressants, right? It's not confirmed, but word came from within part of the company?"
Luther affirmed Illey's words.

"Yes. Suppressants are a golden market. The demand isn't like that of cold medicine, but they're expensive and sell steadily. Moreover, it's a field that's become more prominent as the form of lovers who aren't Alpha and Omega increases."
Matthew placed the list down on the table.
"You suspect one of the places on this list."
"That's something for you detectives to find out from now on. This is about all the help I can give."
Luther picked up his coat and rose from his chair. He looked elegant, like an aristocrat.
"I'll lend you Nathan, who will become a capable specialist, for a few days. I hope you'll find him useful."
"I'll remember that."
Ellie winked and looked at Nathan. Following his gaze, Alex looked too. Nathan was staring straight at him, unchanged from when their eyes had met a few minutes ago.

A faint fear washed over him. It seemed like he could see himself, unable to give up on Nathan as he had repeatedly done before, clinging pathetically once more. Alex forced an awkward smile and closed his mouth.

chapters.title: Chapter 83
paragraphs: After Luther Milan left, Alex and Matthew collected the list he had given them. Ellie began discussing this week's schedule with Nathan. While half-turned away and talking to Matthew, Alex couldn't help but overhear their conversation. Honestly, he wasn't trying to listen; it just reached his ears. It seemed Nathan would be coming to the forensic science research institute regularly until the combination formula was uncovered.
"You'll be coming here a lot now, huh."
Matthew crossed his arms and whispered into his ear. Being just a little taller than Alex, he blocked the side of Alex's face.
"What's your angle, saying it like that?"
"Because that doctor is here?"
Lowering his voice further, Matthew moved closer.
"I was serious about what I said. If he ever annoys you, you can tell me, and anyway, if he seems like he won't be helpful, we can deal with it."
"Matthew, that's never happened, and it won't. Thanks, but it's fine."
Hesitating, Alex added one more thing.
"And I won't be coming often. If there's a reason to come, you come."
Matthew raised an eyebrow as if to say he'd see about that. As he was about to step back, he frowned like someone who'd noticed something. His gaze stopped near Alex's ear.
"Alex."

A finger touched the area behind his ear. It wasn't as intense as when Nathan had touched it, but a strange, shiver-inducing sensation shot through him. Instinctively shrugging his shoulders, Alex grabbed Matthew's wrist.
"What, what?"
"Did you get hurt? There's some kind of mark here near your ear..."

Matthew, who had spoken up to that point, widened his eyes with a soft 'ah' sound. Alex couldn't help but realize what he had realized. He stepped back, overwhelmed by shame. After retreating a couple of steps, Alex bumped into someone. A firm body supported his back, and a hand reached out and grasped his shoulder. It was a familiar scent.
"What are you doing?"

Nathan's voice came from right above him. When Alex turned his head slightly backward, he saw Nathan's lips and hurriedly looked forward again. His heart started beating so loud it could be heard outside.
"What do you mean?"
"Why are you touching him like that when he clearly doesn't like it?"
"Oh, I don't think that's something you, Doctor, need to worry about. We're close friends, so we do all sorts of things."
Matthew said with a blatantly sarcastic tone, pushing his glasses up. At the words 'do all sorts of things,' Alex felt pricked and tightly shut his mouth.

He could feel the strength increasing in Nathan's hand gripping his shoulder. To break free, Alex gently tugged at his hand. As if scolding him, Nathan pressed down on his shoulder even harder. His body grew hot. Wanting to keep his resolution not to stick close, Alex awkwardly scanned his surroundings. If he pushed him away now, that would also look strange.
At the sudden standoff, Ellie stood next to them with an interested expression. And then she threw out an utterly inappropriate comment.
"Matthew, are you the one getting tangled up in a love triangle fight? If you happen to die, I'll prettily finish up your corpse for you."
"You psycho bastard."
Matthew was disgusted. However, his hostility toward Ellie couldn't last long, suppressed by his wariness of Nathan at this moment.
"Anyway, give Alex back. We have to go to Paddington. You, Doctor, just do what you need to do here."
Matthew made a gesture. Ellie interjected again.
"But why are you guys like this?"
"No, this guy..."
Matthew stopped speaking there, perhaps realizing the content was extremely sensitive. Ellie made a 'hmm' sound and then spoke as if she'd suddenly remembered something.
"Oh, by the way, Alex, are you dating lately? I meant to ask earlier but forgot. Your pheromones have softened a bit."
Realizing there was no one here to help him, Alex opened his mouth with an instantly tired face.
"Why my pheromones?"
Lately, having only been around Betas, he had even forgotten about the existence of his own pheromones.
"They've always been a nice scent, but they're softer now, like watered-down condensed milk..."
"Is that not sexual harassment?"
Nathan's cold voice cut off Ellie's words. His body pressed even closer.
"Aha-ha, Dr. Nathan seems sensitive today."
"It is sexual harassment."

Alex quickly retorted and pulled away from Nathan to hide his reddened face. Perhaps unable to stop that too, Nathan let him go. Deliberately not looking at Nathan's face, Alex resolutely turned his head and grabbed Matthew.
"Let's go, Matthew Wayne."
And without waiting for an answer, he left Ellie's meeting room.

From late lunch onward, they had a lot of ground to cover, so they grabbed some hamburgers for a quick meal. Recalling the food Alex had tasted during his patrol officer days, Matthew suggested that maybe they should open a restaurant after retiring.

After wandering around in the cold outside for a solid five hours, they achieved one result. Because a club employee said he seemed to remember the situation from that time. The man, a 37-year-old security guard, added that he had been smoking outside that night.
"I think this is the guy. Definitely."
Alex asked one more time for confirmation.
"It's been several months; how can you be sure? You must see hundreds of people a day."
"Damn, wasn't it you detectives who asked?"
Grumbling and spitting, the man swept his thick hand over the back of his neck. The skull tattoo on his nape seemed to writhe.

"Anyway, I remember. Because that day the fight was disgustingly boring, so I was watching something else. Seeing those punks hitting each other like girls, I thought I'd get high blood pressure. Said he was Russian, but he wasn't living up to his nationality."
After listening for a few minutes to the man chuckling and making derogatory remarks, he finally said something that could be helpful.
"Did you hear what they said?"

"It's not that I remembered because the woman was pretty, but I watched because the guy in the suit approached in a weird way. The way he carefully made contact and spoke, like a spy, he was clearly a shady bastard from the get-go. Guys in suits are all like that."

Matthew, suppressing his irritation, asked for the main point. Since there were quite a few citizens who weren't intimidated even by threats, the Commissioner had forced all investigators to be 'friendly detectives.'
"I'm not sure beyond that."
"You seem to have a good memory; please think a little harder."
Alex personally carried out that role. Perhaps pleased by the praise, the man made a show of thinking.
"Ah, well, he said something weird. I think he said not to tell anyone two or three times. Something about not being qualified... or not getting the money..."
After trying for a few more minutes, he gave up there.
"I don't remember anything else."
As the man spoke as if expecting something, Matthew formed a smiling mouth shape.
"Thank you for your trouble. Could we take down your contact and name, just in case?"
"Isn't there any compensation or something?"
"You could come to Scotland Yard yourself and check."
Of course, that was a lie. When Alex looked at him, Matthew shrugged his shoulders. The man, perhaps believing it, obediently wrote his name and contact information in the notebook.
By the time they returned to headquarters, the sun had set. The team gathered in the meeting room for a progress report. Only after Anna arrived late did they synthesize what each had found out.
"So, either a hospital or a pharmaceutical company?"
Inspector Janice scanned the list with a troubled face. Sergeant Hayden next to her agreed.
"If a corporation gets involved, things get more complicated."
"Was it an individual belonging to a corporation who did it, or are we taking the company itself down?"

Recalling her experience with lawsuits, a shadow fell over Inspector Janice's face. If they tried to cover it up at the corporate level, given the nature of the case, it was clear things would get messy.
"Considering the testimony we got today, there seems to be some logic to it. It could even explain the Secondary Gender change itself."
"That makes more sense than a hate crime. I agree with the opinion you've found. The problem is there's no evidence."
Inspector Janice pointed out the most crucial issue.
"It does feel a bit excessive, I have to admit."
Alex also voiced the opinion that had been bothering him. Feeling several pairs of eyes turn toward him, Alex slowly began to speak.

chapters.title: Chapter 84
paragraphs: "The method seems excessive for simple concealment. It's a grim thought, but if the goal was to avoid detection, they could have simply made the bodies disappear and then eliminated the evidence more discreetly."
Ah, Matthew groaned, ruffling his hair.
"There could be a reason beyond mere concealment."
Sergeant Hayden said, tapping the list. Inspector Janice concluded.
"I'll speak with the higher-ups, so you all should gather the evidence. Finding the bastard who contacted the victims comes first. That's where it'll unravel from."
"Alex, would you like to handle the press conference?"

Hayden, who was on the verge of losing his mind from not wanting to deal with reporters, spoke. Alex refused quickly, without even considering it. As the meeting showed signs of breaking up, Anna suddenly raised her hand.
"Ah, your discussion was so interesting I almost forgot. I found something out too."
"Go ahead."
"If the suspect in a suit made contact with the victims, there might have been a standard approach. Although only Rosaline Mayer has been confirmed."
This time, everyone's gaze shifted to Anna.

"First, all the victims were Betas. It's possible the person approaching them had to be an Alpha or Omega to recognize a Beta at first glance, but there might also have been someone who introduced the victims to the suspect."
"We already checked, Anna. None of the identified victims had any acquaintances in common."
"Yes, that's right. But I found something by tracing through the victims' acquaintances' social media."
"Looks like those old skills are still sharp."
Matthew commented, as if praising her. Anna brushed it off, saying, "You're too kind." Noticing the others' confusion, she quickly continued.
"In doing so, I found out they had all attended language exchange meetups at least once."
"Language exchange?"
Sergeant Hayden asked, sounding puzzled.
"You know, those things. Meeting up through apps like Meetup for language learning."
"Isn't that a dating app?"
Matthew pinpointed the essence of language exchange. Anna laughed.
"Anyway, there are people who meet for wholesome purposes too."
"If there was a group they all participated in, we would've found it."
"Yes, of course. But what if they each participated in different meetups? It seems Rosaline Mayer was interested in French, Robert Maine in Chinese, and James Harper in Korean."
"Korean?"
Matthew nudged Alex's shoulder. At the mention of his rarely referenced half-blood heritage, Alex frowned.
"While searching for meetup pages on the app, I spotted someone in a photo."

Anna held out her phone. On it was a well-built man with neatly styled reddish-brown hair. His clean-cut bone structure and fresh smile made him look like a male model. At a glance, he gave the impression of someone working in finance.
"Take a guess."
Sergeant Hayden gave the answer.
"You mean you found this person in all the meetups?"
"Yes. A handsome man participating in three different language meetups, not just two, it's strange, right?"
There was a whisper from Matthew that the word 'handsome' seemed mixed with Anna's personal feelings.

"So, while looking for photos, it was confirmed that this person was present when each of the three victims attended their respective meetups. I think this person is either the contact or the facilitator for the contact."
"He does have a face that would easily attract favor."
"And two or three meetings is enough to learn about someone's personal circumstances to some extent."
"Good. Anna, you investigate with Matthew. You're both good with computers and such. Alex, you said you were going to see Amy Wainings?"
"Yes, I've already contacted the protection team."
"Let's do our best."
Janice slapped the table and stood up. Before leaving the meeting room, avoiding Hayden who was asking about the press conference one more time, Alex practically fled the headquarters.
He had to go. Perhaps because it was the weekend, the train station was crowded with travelers from early on, in addition to commuters.

The next morning, Alex headed to Slough, a suburb, early. The protection team had requested he discuss that issue, saying Amy Wainings was already showing dissatisfaction. Since Matthew was partnered with Anna, he had no choice but to take the train.
It had been a very long time since he'd taken a train. Just as he had long avoided subways, Alex usually chose domestic flights or coaches over trains.

He boarded the crowded train. The stuffy, uniquely British indoor smell permeated the corridor. After a moment's hesitation between the aisle and the window, he settled into the latter. As the train pulled away from the station, he found himself gazing out the window, almost unconsciously. He hadn't even considered looking outside the first time he'd ridden a train. Nathan had been beside him then.

The memories summoned by his subconscious quickly enveloped Alex. As if etched into his genes, the first moments involving Nathan, even after a long time, did not fade but resurfaced sharply like this.
Nathan, sitting next to him holding his hand, said he would prepare something to eat next time. Holding a ticket costing just a few pounds to Brighton, with a tense face.
Even though it was a pale face that didn't show emotions easily, when he quietly reminisced, there was definitely tension there. It was a moment young Alex couldn't have known.
If things had gone as you said, where would our next destination have been?

Alex blankly added to the imagination. Besides things like the chocolate snacks I liked or the juice Nathan liked, what else we would have eaten, where we would have stayed, where we would have gone holding hands, he pictured those moments that never came to pass. Suddenly, his eyes felt dry and gritty, and he rubbed his eyelids.

It would have been different with adult Nathan. We might have traveled together by car on quiet roads, or gone abroad to places we'd never been. Images he couldn't have imagined just a few months ago clearly formed in his mind. Probably because Nathan didn't ignore me or push me away like before.

He remembered Nathan, who held his shoulder and took his side. The sight of him opening the car door and waiting for me, his quiet face comforting me when I cried, all his considerate actions, made my heart burn.
I thought I'd suffer less if he was kind to me now. I thought it would be okay if I received forgiveness. But I, this human, was too greedy, always wanting something bigger from Nathan.

Just as Nathan's memory threatened to overwhelm him, the train screeched to a halt. Hearing his destination announced, Alex hurried off the train, his pace quickening as if fleeing from his deepest desires.

The safe house where Amy Wainings was located was about a twenty-minute walk from the train station. Since Slough itself was a small city near London, there weren't many tall buildings. Arriving at a house with peeling blue paint on the door, Alex made a call. Then Claire, the handler he'd been in contact with, opened the front door and appeared.
"Hi, Alex! Long time no see."
"Have you been well?"
"Hmm."
Claire shrugged her shoulders and gestured. Alex, who had closed the small gate in the fence, quickly went up the front steps.
"Ms. Wainings has a lot of complaints. Thanks to that, I've been getting grilled. I'm a bit worried because I don't know where she might bolt to."
"Is that so?"

Since his first impression of her at the hospital hadn't been like that, Alex made a surprised expression. As if to confirm, Claire opened the door. Amy Wainings was waiting near the entrance with her arms crossed. Unlike when she had fainted in shock, her complexion was healthy. Because her black hair was tied up, her slender, pale face stood out particularly.
"It's the detective I saw then."
She walked over confidently and stood in front of Alex.
"Hello, Ms. Wainings."
He extended his hand for a handshake. Amy's hand, caught in his firm grip, was slender and soft.
"Yes. You said your name was Yeon, right?"

Even though it was something from almost a month ago, Amy remembered even trivial details quite well. As he nodded, Claire guided them to the living room. Amy, who plopped down on the sofa and, with a pointed glare at Claire, got straight to the point:
"Why can't I make phone calls?"

chapters.title: Chapter 85
paragraphs: "We're handling any necessary contacts on your behalf."
When Claire pointed this out, Amy immediately countered.
"What kind of contact is that?"
Amy made no attempt to hide her irritation.

"I could accept it for about two weeks. But it's already been a month. I know I was in a dangerous situation. But this isn't something involving the mafia like you see in movies, and there's no guarantee they'll come after me again, right? What is this about moving me to the Midlands? Tell me! Detective, when on earth are you going to catch this culprit?"

Questions poured out one after another. It was a natural reaction from someone who had been living an ordinary life and was then forcibly separated from their daily routine. Alex wanted to calm her down first.
"Ms. Wainings, please calm down first. The investigation is ongoing. The reason I visited today is related to that."
"So when can I return to London?"
"We are also trying to catch the perpetrator as quickly as possible for the victims' sake. However, I'd appreciate it if you could understand that we cannot give you a definitive timeline yet."
Amy stared intently at Alex. With her gentle, large eyes that could be called puppy-like and her calm voice, she didn't seem like the type to intimidate others even when she was irritable.
"What do you want to ask me?"
"Have you heard the name MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company?"
As if the question was unexpected, Amy tilted her head slightly.
"Yes, I have."
"How do you know about it?"
Amy spoke in a tone suggesting it was no big deal.
"It's a place I interviewed at. It didn't seem like a good fit for me, so I declined their offer."
"You didn't mention it in your resume or during the statement process."
"Right, because I never worked there. I thought it was an unrelated matter. Besides, it happened over half a year ago."
Amy genuinely seemed not to know. Soon, as if she remembered something, she leaned forward.
"But who did you hear that from? Nathan's the only one close to me who knew I applied to MacMilan. Did Nathan tell you?"
Alex flinched at the familiar way she called him 'Nathan'. The tone was overly affectionate. As Nathan's name came up, Amy's face brightened even more.
"Is that Nathan? Is he doing well? Ah, Claire! Please, just let me use my phone. I don't even know how Nathan is doing."
Then Claire firmly intervened.
"Unless that person is your lover or husband, there's no real reason to contact him."
Amy glanced sharply at Alex, then reached out and grabbed his arm. Stopping Claire, who was about to step in, Alex met Amy's gaze.

"I was just about to gather my courage and ask Nathan out on a date when this happened. We just needed to set a date. Given this situation, Nathan must be worried about me, right? What do you think, Detective?"

It was something Alex had heard Nathan say during his statement. He had thought about it since then. The image of Nathan, who had called Amy's name fondly and praised her, overlapped in his mind. Feeling as if the ground beneath his feet was giving way, Alex slowly opened his mouth.
"Mr. White seemed to be doing fine."
"You know Nathan?"

His words caught in his throat. Alex painted an awkward smile as he tried to think of an answer. *We were high school classmates. We almost dated, and I screwed that up royally. Oh, and recently, Nathan slept with me to help me out... twice, no less.*
These were things he couldn't say at all. He felt a churning, crumpling sensation inside. Alex was silent for a few seconds before finally managing to produce a usable answer.
"Yes. I've seen him a few times during the investigation."
"Will you be seeing him again by any chance? Since I can't contact him directly, there's something I'd really like you to tell him."
Not forgetting to shoot a brief glare at Claire, Amy made her request. Claire looked at Alex with an exasperated expression.
"Please, I'm begging you."

Her voice was earnest. A cool sweat faintly trickled down his spine. He felt stifled. The feeling of being an interloper, which he had felt before, enveloped his entire body. Guilt also surged, wondering if he was the one obstructing the relationship between Amy and Nathan.
Although the two weren't dating yet, even Alex, who barely knew, could clearly tell that Amy liked Nathan. And if he hadn't interfered, Nathan wouldn't have had sex with him either.
"Is it not possible?"

A look of disappointment appeared on her face. Her pitiful expression, as if any request should be granted, amplified Alex's guilt. He could understand the Amy before him. More than anyone else. Alex had had a crush on Nathan for a long time. He couldn't not know the feeling of harboring affection for someone. He also knew well how painful and difficult it was. An answer came from his hesitating lips.
"Yes, if you tell me, I'll pass it on."
"Thank you!"
Amy's face lit up with joy as she tightened her grip on his arm.

"Since you said you're trying, Detective, I want to believe I can return to London within at least two or three months. So, could you tell Nathan that I really like him a lot, and to please wait a little? I wanted to say it myself, but it's taking too long."

With a smile that didn't dare doubt rejection, Amy spoke shyly. She even showed a confidence that couldn't exist unless something had been mutually discussed. Alex silently stared at her face. Amy was someone who knew Nathan's twenties, which Alex didn't.
*She must be a precious person in a position incomparable to mine.*

The moment he thought that, Alex realized his own hidden feelings, which he had tried to avoid. He, foolishly, had been thinking about the seat next to Nathan. Holding onto the words 'I liked you once' as hope, clinging to the kindness Nathan showed him as lingering affection, believing there might still be a possibility...
Alex quietly removed Amy's hand, which was still holding him. At Alex's gentle action of letting go, Amy blinked.
"I'm sorry, Ms. Wainings, but I don't think I can fulfill that kind of request."
"Huh? Why?"
If Amy was that confident, then perhaps Nathan would accept her, even if it took a little time. That was between the two of them, and Alex had no right to interfere.
"That was between the two of them."
"But you promised just now."
Amy's expression instantly filled with disappointment. Guilt welled up. Amy was undoubtedly earnest too.
"Mr. White would be happier to hear it directly."
But Alex wasn't such a good person that he could connect the person he liked with someone else. That much he couldn't do.
"So please trust us, hold on a little longer, and tell him yourself."

Alex stepped back. Amy wore an expression as if she had something more to say, hesitated for a moment, shrugged her shoulders, and said she understood. Claire looked at him with suspicious eyes, but Amy, as if having collected her emotions, suggested moving on to the next matter. Alex followed her lead.

That day, Alex obtained as detailed a statement as possible from Amy about the day she had gone to the MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company. Leaving a request for her to contact Claire if she remembered anything more, he left Slough. Before parting, Amy added one more thing, as if she had just remembered.
"Oh, come to think of it, there was a senior who recommended I apply to MacMilan. I haven't heard from her in a while, could she be involved?"
"Could you tell me her name?"
"Sera Ots."
"I'll look into it."
"Okay. Take care."

Amy saw him off. Her attitude was as if she had completely forgotten about the confession she had asked him to deliver. Was it because she was so sure it would naturally work out with Nathan? Suppressing the vulgar jealousy trying to burst forth and pry open his heart, Alex turned all his attention towards 'Sera Ots'. Focusing only on the work like a person who felt nothing made him feel a little more alive.

chapters.title: Chapter 86
paragraphs: Over the two days since returning from Slough, the investigation had made considerable progress. Anna and Matthew had uncovered the identity of the man who had appeared at the language exchange meetings.

It wasn't his exact identity. He had used different names at each meeting: Marty, Cameron, Philip. He had consistently said he was in his early thirties and was indeed British. Compared to tracking the man in the suit, there was a fair amount of information exposed, and by the third day, they had discovered the man's definitive identity.
Patrick Shore.

Having majored in marketing, he had continued his career in sales before starting a headhunting company about a year and a half ago. His exact age was 32, and he was unmarried. A check revealed his company was a shell company, existing only online.

They went to the address on record, but a different tenant was living in the house. After securing testimony that he, who had sublet the place, hadn't been seen for several months, the team allocated more investigative personnel. Hayden made an optimistic statement that since his face and identity were confirmed, they should be able to find him soon.

Matthew worked with the technical team to secure the shell company's electronic transaction records. Meanwhile, Anna sought out and obtained testimony from people in Patrick Shore's circle. Among them, several had heard Patrick Shore bragging about receiving an incredible offer, and the timing coincided with when he started the shell company. And coincidentally, the place that made him the offer was a pharmaceutical company. He hadn't told his friends the company's name, but this added one more piece of circumstantial evidence. The fact that he suddenly started a headhunting company right after being offered a position at a pharmaceutical company was suspicious in itself.

While the team members were each handling their assigned tasks, Alex began investigating Sera Otsu from Monday afternoon. To gather basic information, Alex worked at headquarters for the first time in a while. Matthew was busy with the technical team, making him hard to see even in the same building. After sitting for hours meticulously recording Sera Otsu's personal details, his throat went dry and he paused his work for a moment.

Scanning the interior of the investigation team, filled with the sound of keyboard tapping and phone calls, Alex pushed his chair back and stood up. Sergeant Hayden raised his voice while on a call with a reporter. Glancing at his back, Alex thought it would be better to buy his share of drinks too.

Unlike the inside of the investigation team headquarters, which felt quiet despite the noise, the corridor was chaotic. Voices could be heard from the passageway leading to the elevator. Since it was also near the break room with the vending machine, Alex walked there slowly and checked the date. It was Monday. A new week had already begun.
Then he remembered he hadn't discussed this week's medication with Nathan. Should he contact him? Whoever contacted first, it was a topic that would inevitably be mentioned.

But he didn't feel at ease. After meeting Amy, her relationship with Nathan weighed on his mind. Moreover, if his body touched Nathan's again, it seemed like the desire he'd struggled to suppress for the past three days would be reawakened.

There were three or four people in front of the elevator. Intending to pass by without a thought and head to the break room, Alex saw a blond man among the people and opened his eyes wide. His height, significantly taller than others, made the man stand out. It was Nathan.
"Are you heading to the administrative office? Do you have a visitor's pass?"

A woman who appeared to be a police officer was speaking kindly to Nathan. Alex slowly stepped back. An instinctive desire to greet him and acknowledge their acquaintance surged, but reason suppressed it.

Increasing the frequency of meeting Nathan wouldn't do any good. He'd said they should stay as acquaintances, but if they kept running into each other like this, giving up on his feelings would be impossible.

Nathan, who had been about to answer the officer, much shorter than him, with his head slightly bowed, suddenly looked up. Nathan's eyes met Alex's, who was stepping back while looking at him. The green eyes frowned as if in disbelief, and soon he was seen excusing himself to the officer. Alex hurriedly turned and started walking back the way he came. Running seemed a bit much, so he quickened his pace.
"Stop right there, Alex."

Avoidance was useless. Nathan quickly caught up with him. At the voice coming from behind, Alex firmly closed his mouth and stopped. Turning his head slowly, Nathan came into view. As always, his face today was cruelly beautiful.
"Hi. Nathan, did you have a good weekend? What brings you here?"
Alex greeted him, looking for cues. Nathan was wearing a white lab coat under his coat. It seemed he'd come straight from the lab.
"To register as a research consultant."

Nathan answered Alex's question curtly. Wanting to leave, Alex took a step back and nodded. Even though they had agreed to be acquaintances, he honestly didn't know how to interact with Nathan to maintain that level of familiarity.
"I see. The administrative office is the other way, just go straight down that hall."
"Where are you going?"
Seeing him retreat, Nathan asked with an unpleasant expression.
"I was going back..."
"Why are you running away."
The lowered voice brought up the uncomfortable topic all at once. Alex quickly shook his head.
"Me? I wasn't."
"Is that what you're asking me to believe?"
It hit the mark. Unable to find words and hesitating, Nathan continued speaking.
"I clearly told you there's no need to avoid me, and we agreed to stay as acquaintances. As you wanted. So why are you running away? Don't say you didn't know; it was obvious at the institute too."
If they were to remain acquaintances, a greeting would have been appropriate. Interrogating why he avoided him didn't suit that relationship.

It was confusing. It was naturally good that he was acknowledging him, but Alex needed to isolate himself from Nathan's attitude. If their relationship progressed beyond greeting-level acquaintances, he would definitely get confused. As long as the memories of kissing and mixing bodies remained, that would happen.
"What else is the problem?"
Perhaps the continuing silence was frustrating, Nathan asked in a lowered voice. The expression rising on his pale face was mixed with concern. Like last time, Alex still couldn't understand Nathan.

*How can Nathan be like this? After going through such a thing, how can he forgive me and be gentle enough to keep me by his side? I like you like this, but sometimes I wish you were truly a bad person. If that were the case, then I wouldn't keep wanting you.*
"Don't be so nice to me, Nathan."

With limp, dejected hands, he quietly looked up at Nathan. He examined the brilliant gold flecks within the vivid green eyes. He loved those beautiful orbs that shattered into dozens of colors under sunlight. The straight bridge of the nose beneath them, the pretty and soft lips, all of it.

He loved everything: leaving his slightly disheveled hair alone after just waking up and drinking water, his personality that hated dirty things, his tendency to maintain a cool silence for long periods. And among all these beautiful aspects, Alex liked the kind Nathan the most.
But at the same time, that kindness was also resentful.
Nathan's eyes opened slightly wider, like someone who had heard something unexpected. A small sigh escaped from between his well-shaped lips.
"What?"
"I mean worrying about me like this. If you keep looking after me, I might get the wrong idea."

Looking back, it had always been like that. While it's clearly the mistaken person's fault, whenever he tried to create distance to somehow drive it from his heart, Nathan came to him. As if trying to prevent Alex from resigning himself.

With a slight frown, Nathan stared quietly at Alex. Not avoiding the meeting gaze, Alex waited for an answer. Once he'd spoken his true feelings, his heart felt like it was about to overflow.
