If Nathan wouldn't accept his reason, he even wanted to confess. At the very least, he wanted to tell him how much he liked Nathan. Then he could explain everything.
"What are you mistaking?"
*That I like you so much, that I'm afraid of mistakenly thinking you might accept me,* he could say that.
"I, toward you..."

chapters.title: Chapter 87
paragraphs: I just wanted to say it. Nathan was looking at Alex with deepened eyes. At the last moment, Alex suppressed what rose to the back of his throat. The situation wasn't right. Confessing out of the blue right in the middle of a corridor where everyone could see was rude in itself. It was also a feeling that wouldn't do any good to reveal. To remain just acquaintances, he had to endure it.
"Why are you acting so familiar?"

A long silence stretched between them. Nathan, looking down at me with tightened lips, seemed troubled. He looked like someone faced with an unsolvable problem. Only when someone glanced at them as they passed by in the middle of the corridor did Nathan finally speak.
"Is that what you want?"
He forced a nod. A relationship where we greet each other when we meet, and help each other out a little if something big happens, just enough to care. I thought I could give up with that much.
"Yeah. But if something happens to you, please tell me. I'll help you as much as I can."
Nathan let out a faint sigh and straightened his upper body. A blunt remark was thrown.
"If you're openly avoiding me, how can I talk to you?"
"Sorry."
The apology seemed to trouble Nathan even more. Nathan, who had squeezed his eyes shut, swept back his hair and spoke as if it was settled.
"I'll do as you wish, so get on with what you need to do."
Their gazes tangled. In the meantime, a few more people passed by them. Nathan's shoes turned direction to the side.
"I'm going."
"Take care. Have a good day."

Nathan turned his back. Watching him turn his body without a word, Alex wondered if he should have walked him to the administrative office. Come to think of it, he hadn't talked about the Neutralizer yet either.
But Nathan was already far away in the distance. Alex, who had been staring at his straight, broad back for a moment before slowly turning around.
I did well. I did well.
If I just keep this up, we'll really become just acquaintances someday.

Thinking like that, Alex lost his appetite and decided to just go back to his seat. The scene at the returned headquarters was no different from before he left. Looking at that sight, Alex wished he too would appear that way.

It was a Friday with the whole team gathered for the first time in a while, so lunch continued in the meeting room. Although it hadn't rained for some time, London, which had shown cloudy skies, was bright that day. Sunlight seeping through the window dyed the tabletop.

Since that Monday, Alex hadn't seen Nathan. He deliberately cut off his visits to the research institute and didn't really contact him either. Even though it was time to take the Neutralizer, Nathan also hadn't called or texted. Considering he had only called once a week at most, the sense of emptiness was quite substantial.
Stop thinking about it.

Alex erased the thought. He'd taken the Neutralizer twice, so it should be fine, and if he left things like this, they would naturally drift apart for sure. Since he had even been forgiven, there was nothing more weighing on his mind. He comforted himself that this current situation was the best for them.
"When is Supplies Support going to replace these chairs? Feels like they'll be like this forever."

Anna, who had leaned back putting weight on the creaking chair, spoke. She had been eating chicken breast recently for strength training, and while complaining it tasted bad, she eyed Alex's lunch. As Anna reached out her hand, Matthew picked up Alex's sandwich.
"This is mine."
"Ah, Senior! Why did you only make it for Matthew, Senior?"
"Well, because I paid for it!"

Whether his earlier words were sincere, Matthew had begged Alex, giving him £30, to please make him a sandwich. Since it was money that would cover the ingredient cost and more, when Alex tried to refuse, Matthew insisted stubbornly, so Alex ended up making two portions of chicken sandwiches. He didn't know if they were that delicious, but Matthew was satisfied. Sergeant Hayden, who was eating soup bought from Pret A Manger, chimed in.
"Alex's homemade lasagna was legendary though."
Matthew nodded, taking a big bite of his sandwich. Anna's words, tinged with regret, followed.
"I'm jealous. I wasn't here then, so I don't know."
"There was a certain charm to newbies freezing stiff in their stiff uniforms. The investigation team was happy because a cute face had joined after a long time."

As Hayden spoke, lost in reminiscence, Anna giggled in agreement. Having forcibly stuffed the chicken breast into her mouth, she was examining the notes compiled on Patrick Shore's whereabouts and spoke as if she'd just remembered.

"That makes sense. Ah, hearing that reminds me, there's been a fuss about a new scientific researcher lately. A colleague who went there the other day for another case was excited, saying a really handsome doctor had newly joined and showed me a photo."
"That's illegal."
Matthew pointed out.
"He said it was legitimate photography..."
Alex, who had been examining Sera Ots while eating his sandwich, stopped moving. His body reacted automatically to the word 'doctor.'
"Ah, I heard too. The fuss reached even here. There's this grand talk going around inside the institute that a new light has entered a place where there was no hope except for Ilai."
Sergeant Hayden also nodded as if he knew. Matthew made a face and said.
"You're talking about Nathan White, right? That's a bit much, isn't it?"
Then Sergeant Hayden turned his head slightly and patted Matthew's shoulder with an understanding expression. As Matthew showed clear signs of his mood souring rapidly, he changed the subject.
"Instead of meaningless talk, let's get back to discussing the case. Did you find anything about Sera Ots, Alex?"

Alex was a beat late in understanding the question directed at him. Making an 'Ah' sound, Alex quickly pulled his laptop forward. Having forced himself to focus solely on the case for the past few days, he had found quite a bit.
"It seems she really is missing. They say she went to Germany for a few months for corporate training, but her family said they couldn't contact her for a while."
"Why didn't they file a missing person report?"
"Seems her relationship with her parents isn't that good. She's adopted, and it seems the gap widened after the couple had a second child."

It didn't feel like someone else's story, and Alex couldn't feel at ease throughout the investigation. Rapid ripples spread across the calm surface of his mind, which had been drawing a level line for a while. The forced composure he had maintained by trying not to feel or think anything quickly crumbled.
"Information's slowly coming together. Sera Ots is a big link."
Hayden said to Alex as if praising him. It was something anyone could have found out, but since the structure was such that the first to find out gets praised, Alex silently agreed.
"It's scary that so many people disappeared in half a year and no one knew."
Anna, having finished her lunchbox, got up from her seat while packing it. Hayden nodded and followed her out.
"The circumstantial evidence is roughly gathered, so if we catch Patrick Shore, we can somehow take it to the prosecutor. We'll go dig a bit more, so you guys hang in there too."
"See you later."
Matthew waved his hand half-heartedly. Then he looked at Alex.
"I'm going to the research institute now to check on progress related to the compound formula, want to come?"
Nathan's name came to mind first. Before lingering feelings could rise, Alex forcibly cut them off.
"No, I'll stay and look into Sera Ots more."
This is all I need to do. He encouraged himself.
"Alright."
As if understanding, Matthew patted Alex's back. Pointing with his chin to the desk they shared, he added.
"If you're curious about the research content reported up to yesterday, check my computer. I left it unlocked."
"Got it."

Once even Matthew left the meeting room, silence descended. Alex, who had been looking at the empty meeting room, also slowly rose from his seat. Even though nothing bad had happened, his heart felt heavy.

Melancholy washed over him. Afraid of the helplessness that had suddenly rushed in, Alex tried to think of the cause. Perhaps Sera Ots's family situation was the cause. The story of a child abandoned by their parents was one I knew all too well.

When handling cases, it was hard to avoid feeling a sense of kinship, being human. Usually, he pretended not to feel any emotion like a machine and moved on, but occasionally there were days when his heart was shaken like this. Today seemed to be that day.

chapters.title: Chapter 88
paragraphs: The best course of action would be to avoid seeing such things, but this was Alex's profession. Having spent half of his twenties like this, he no longer desired to seek out another job. He couldn't become a soccer coach either. Two years of experience without a single debut did not qualify as a career.

Sitting in Matthew's usual spot, Alex's hand tightened around the mouse. As he gazed at the meticulously organized A-Z folders, Alex recalled Matthew's advice. The thought that he should consider seeking counseling if these feelings persisted gradually began to surface. There was only one reason he hadn't pursued therapy despite hearing that counsel. Even if he were to confide in someone, his circumstances would remain unchanged.

A person named Alex would likely continue to be plagued by financial worries like this. After paying the rent and settling his monthly debts, his salary would vanish in an instant, leaving him with no means to save any money. His only mother would never love him again, and the probability of his father returning was...
Continuing his somber reflections while scanning the screen, Alex blinked. While browsing through Matthew's folders, he had discovered a folder labeled 'Yeon' within the Y section.

Then, he remembered their previous conversation in the car, when he had asked about the progress of the search for his father. Back then, Matthew had explicitly stated that he hadn't found anything yet. There was no conceivable reason for Matthew, of all people, to lie to him.
It must be a coincidence.

With that thought, Alex slowly moved the mouse cursor over the folder. It could simply be an abbreviation. Or perhaps it was a file pertaining to a victim with a similar surname. His throat felt parched. Swallowing dryly, Alex held his breath and double-clicked the folder.

Inside, several photos were stored. They were displayed as small thumbnails, so the details were not clearly discernible. His hand, trembling slightly, clicked on one of the photos. The sound of his own heartbeat thrummed loudly in his ears.

The first photo opened. It revealed a middle-aged man with a smile. The man, who appeared to be in his mid-fifties, was of East Asian descent. More precisely, he was Korean. Alex knew this at a glance. It was a face he absolutely could not fail to recognize.

Alex stared blankly at the monitor, his eyes wide. Believing he might be hallucinating, he even pressed his eyelids firmly with the hand not holding the mouse. But no matter how intently he looked, the man in the photograph was undeniably someone he knew.
"He's gotten old."

The words escaped his lips in a soft murmur. Forgetting even to blink, Alex gazed at the photo for a long time. The middle-aged man's eye area was etched with fine wrinkles, and he had a considerable amount of white hair. Yet, his face seemed brighter than Alex remembered. His complexion was vastly different from his past self, who was perpetually soaked in alcohol and often drunk. He looked younger now.

His chest felt heavy, as if he had been anesthetized. In a state where he couldn't identify the emotion overwhelming him, Alex moved to the next photo. The same man was present there as well. This time, however, he was accompanied by other people.

Beside his father stood a young woman and a boy who couldn't have been more than ten years old. The photograph appeared to have been excerpted from a website. In what seemed to be a classroom setting, there were children of the same age and their parents. It seemed Matthew had enlarged a photo taken there. That Matthew fellow is quite skilled. How did he manage to find this? An inappropriate thought flickered through his mind.
A sharp pang in his stomach made Alex momentarily withdraw his hand from the mouse. It didn't seem like a wise decision to view more photos. But then, why?
Isn't it actually a good thing to know that father is alive?

Alex's rational mind posed the question. It was true. It was incredibly joyous news that the father he had believed dead after being missing for nearly ten years was, in fact, alive. Until this moment, Alex had lived with the conviction that he had lost his father. In such a situation, seeing him smiling so happily was undeniably a positive development. The decision was made. It was alright to see more.

Alex scrolled through the photos. The solo photograph of his father was both the first and the last. Whether he had unearthed pictures from his daily life, the photographs featured individuals who appeared to be his father's new family. Their well-kept attire and smiling faces showed no signs of hardship or weariness from life's struggles.

Observing the unfamiliar background, it seemed to be Korea. That must have made the search difficult. With substantial debts, fleeing abroad was likely the more practical option. Returning to his home country and reapplying for citizenship would have allowed him to reclaim his nationality. In many respects, it was a logical choice.
Because his father looked happy with his new son.

It had been an eternity since Alex had last seen his father's smiling face. As far as Alex could recall, his father had always been unhappy and dissatisfied with Alex's accomplishments. He had tried his utmost. Alex had thought perhaps he had done enough, but it seemed he was mistaken.

Scrolling through the photos to the very end, Alex examined the face of the child who, unlike himself, bore strong East Asian features. Whether he excelled at soccer, was obedient to his father, or was simply more charming, his father seemed to favor his new son. It was the complete opposite of Alex's experience.
I am still here, alone. Clinging to everything you left behind, waiting for you, with no idea when you might return.

Without even realizing what he was doing, Alex raised his hand and touched his lips. The fingers brushing against the corner of his mouth grew increasingly restless. Labored breaths escaped him. It felt as though something had lodged in his throat, something he couldn't bring himself to expel.
Feeling his airway constricting, Alex rose from his seat. It's okay. It's okay. Let's think of something else.
But the image before his eyes persistently interrupted his thoughts. The desperate plan he forced himself to conceive was to leave this place immediately. So, where should he go?
Matthew. It would be better to go and see Matthew.

It seemed appropriate to inquire why he had kept this information secret, even after finding details about his father. It was not good conduct for partners to deceive each other. The discomfort in his heart was likely due to that very reason. Once he understood the rationale behind Matthew's actions, things would surely improve.

Lacking the mental fortitude to take a bus or the subway, Alex hailed a taxi. As he entered the taxi with a pale complexion, the driver inquired if he was alright. Replying that he was fine, Alex rubbed his phone.

He almost called Matthew but refrained, thinking he might vent his anger on an innocent person if he heard his voice immediately. It wasn't too late to go to the institute and ask calmly. Matthew hadn't done anything wrong. The reason he hadn't disclosed the information was probably out of concern for Alex. If Alex became unstable, it would hinder the case, and there would be no positive outcomes. In fact, Matthew had handled the situation judiciously.
Because Alex was regretting having seen the photos.

A profound sense of utter aloneness washed over him. Loneliness spread like a venom, much like when he had been left alone to guard the house. Unable to grasp what to do, Alex prayed for the taxi to arrive quickly. Anything would suffice; he longed to see a familiar face. Otherwise, he felt he might descend into madness. As if sensing his desperate wish, the taxi reached its destination in just fifteen minutes. Upon seeing the fare exceed £20 on the meter, he briefly felt it was a waste, then, disgusted with himself for such a thought, he exited the vehicle without even waiting for his change. Presenting his ID, he entered the institute. With unsteady steps, Alex stopped in the middle of the institute's main hall. He felt utterly lost.
Where should he look for Matthew?

Unable to conjure the simple solution of stopping a passerby and asking for directions, Alex opted for a route he remembered. He walked down the corridor leading to the underground area where Ilai was stationed. Since he couldn't access the autopsy room with his card, he changed his destination to Ilai's meeting room instead.

The door to the meeting room was ajar. Matthew was not present. As if in the midst of his work, the board was densely covered with what appeared to be formulas. Gazing at the cold, stark lighting of the meeting room, Alex turned to leave. Now that he had come all this way, it felt like a pointless endeavor. If he had simply continued with his own work, Matthew would have eventually come to check on his progress anyway.
"Alex."

Just as he was regaining his senses and about to exit the meeting room, his name was called. He was closer to a state of having his eyes open but not truly seeing anything, so Alex belatedly recognized the figure that came into his view. Standing there was the person he least wanted to see at that very moment.
"Ah, hello, Nathan."

chapters.title: Chapter 89
paragraphs: It felt like a wall made of sawdust was collapsing, leaving me hollow and broken inside. Seeing the pale face staring straight at me, I felt tears welling up. Clenching the rising emotions, I averted my gaze. That was the best I could do.
"What are you doing here?"
Nathan asked, his voice devoid of any emotion. I struggled to grasp his question. My head wasn't functioning properly.
"Have you seen Matthew, by any chance?"
"He's not here."
"I see."
Feeling as though I was blocking the doorway, I stepped aside. Seeing me like that, Nathan slowly entered. The files tucked under his arm were packed densely.
"I should get going. Good luck with your research."

That was the limit. Without a word, Nathan placed the files on the meeting room table. Seeing him turn his head, I also headed silently toward the meeting room door. I thought it was fortunate I hadn't heard anything from Nathan. Until Nathan quietly uttered a single phrase.
"Why do you look like that?"
My feet, which had been staggering forward, stopped abruptly. I slowly turned back, my eyes shaking messily. Nathan was asking with his back turned.
"Huh?"
"I said, why do you look like you're about to cry?"
My words caught in my throat, and I bit my lip hard. Was it because no answer came? Nathan turned his body and strode over. He was looking at me with his mouth set firm.
"What's wrong?"
"Nothing, it-it's nothing."
My voice trembled, making me stumble over my words. Clutching my heart, which was on the verge of collapse, I tried to feign composure.

But the moment Nathan's finger touched the corner of my eye, I was overwhelmed with sorrow. I had no way to endure any longer. On another day, it might have been okay. If it had been a few days later, after I had somehow managed to accept the reality that my father had abandoned me, I might have withstood Nathan's kindness.
But not today. It was a day of truly, disgustingly bad luck.

The finger stroking my burning eyelid was painfully warm. Like a beast starved for warmth, I crumbled rapidly at that small contact. I wanted to act spoiled. Because I knew Nathan had been kindly accepting me all this time.
"Tell me."

His thumb swept under my eye. I grabbed Nathan's wrist that was touching me. The flimsy boundary my reason had built shattered into pieces after just a few touches. The heart I had been suppressing since meeting Nathan again threw a tantrum. Why today, of all days. Why, at this very moment, did I have to see you.
I couldn't bear it.
I simply couldn't give up on Nathan.

While telling him my father had abandoned me, I wanted to hug Nathan tight. I wanted to bury my face in his nape, which carried a refreshing scent, and feel his warmth. I wanted to kiss him, I wanted Nathan to hold me. I wanted him to tell me he'd stay by my side. But as mere acquaintances, I couldn't do such things.
"I told you... not to be too good to me, Nathan."
So I don't want to act like we're just acquaintances.
"If you keep being so good to me..."
I've always wished you were my lover. I don't want to be friends with you. I don't want to be acquaintances, or friends, none of it.
"It makes it hard to give up on you."

Nathan was by my side during every moment of my deepest loneliness. Loneliness makes a person vulnerable. In my weakest moments, when I had no way to protect myself and was weathering the storm alone, Nathan was the only one who sheltered me.

Because he was that kind of presence, the person I wanted to lean on and the person I wanted to like was always Nathan. Faced with unbearable loneliness, I ended up clinging to Nathan. The inner thoughts I had been holding back firmly came pouring out. I collapsed wretchedly. I wanted to feel that I wasn't alone.
"I like you."
Putting strength into the hand holding Nathan's wrist, I moved closer to him. With a face desperate as if wishing he would hold me, I whispered.
"I like you so much."

I tried to endure it. I tried to distance myself too, and actually did so. But as if trapped in an endless loop, I always returned to this starting point. This was the last method I could attempt. Confessing my heart, which was rotting and disintegrating.
"I just don't know how to like you a little."

Moisture mixed into my calmly uttered voice. If Nathan wouldn't listen to my excuses, I wished he would at least understand a little more of my true feelings, so I put strength into my voice. I took one more step closer. Don't push me away, Nathan.
Don't push me away...

Nathan said nothing. Instead, he made an indescribable expression. His eyes were contorted and his pretty lips were slightly raised, like someone smiling while crying. A dreadful silence stretched on for a long time. Like a soundless scream, after a long quiet, Nathan opened his mouth.
"Alex, I..."
I quietly took in Nathan's expression. To search for joy on Nathan's face after hearing my words, because if Nathan liked me just a little, maybe somewhere deep down he'd be happy.
"You're making such a terrible face, it's driving me crazy. Yes, I care about you. To the point where I think forgiving you is better, despite what you did to me. I admit it."

But no matter how I searched, I couldn't find any joy in Nathan. What I found were eyes contorting as if in agony and lips trembling slightly. Nowhere in those confused green eyes was there happiness.
"But I don't trust you."
Nathan's face, which had been collapsing wretchedly, slowly returned. As if facing reality.
"I can't trust you."
"Because of what I said to you?"
Drawing in a breath that was scattered into a mess, I asked back. Nathan asked quietly with a shadowed face.
"No. Because you didn't trust me."
I couldn't answer that.
"Whatever your circumstances were, you should have told me you trusted me and asked for my help."
I stared blankly at Nathan. Nathan was also silent. I had to answer, but no appropriate words came to mind. Nathan was right. It wasn't anything new; it was always like that.
"What do you want to do with me? Do you want to date?"

Finding it more painful than death to spit out that short phrase, I gritted my teeth. On the premise that I couldn't even find words to soothe the wounds Nathan had received, I wasn't selfish enough to suggest dating. I'd have felt better if I had. But I couldn't even do that.
"There's no trust between you and me, is that possible?"
Like an empty-headed person, I couldn't say anything. But I couldn't just stay like this forever. I let go of Nathan's wrist that I had been holding and slowly lowered my arm.
"Right."

That was all I could say. Since I had no way of knowing what answer would look okay when rejected, all I knew was that the moment of rejection hurt more than anything I had imagined in the past. It hurt.
It really hurt.
"Of course that would be the case."

Almost crying, I scrunched up my face and bit my lip. I raised my empty hand and rubbed my cheek. Slowly exhaling the breath that felt ready to burst inside, I took a deep breath. My senses gradually returned.
Like someone discovering their own reflection on television, I only thought, *Why did it turn out like this?* What I wanted was just simple comfort, but foolishly, I messed it up.
If I had just left it alone, it's clear things would have been okay in the middle.
"I'm sorry. I shouldn't have said anything. Um, so..."
Nathan remained silent with an expressionless face. A chilling silence filled the room before dissipating.
"About what I just said... can we just pretend it never happened?"
I asked in a voice devoid of inflection, sunken low. Even though it was a stupid question, Nathan lowered his gaze and gave an answer.
"Yeah."
"That would be good."
"Yeah."

Nathan gave the same answer. Hearing the consecutive words of affirmation, I almost let my expression crumble. Using every ounce of strength, I maintained my expression. Letting my eyebrows droop, I slowly moved my legs. I considered saying 'Have a good day' but gave up.

chapters.title: Chapter 90
paragraphs: The timing was all wrong. Alex quietly walked past Nathan, who stood frozen in place. Each step was slow, deliberate, as he moved further away. Nathan didn't reach out to stop him. It felt like pieces of Alex's heart were being torn away.
Finally, just before completely leaving the conference room, Alex paused. Without looking back, he softly said to Nathan.
"I'm sorry."

After offering an apology that would now sound tedious to Nathan, he closed the door. Alex continued forward, gaze fixed straight ahead. It wasn't as if something major had happened, but his body refused to cooperate, so Alex kept murmuring to himself that it was okay.
*It's okay, it's okay, it's okay, it's okay, it's okay, it's okay, it's okay, it's okay, it's okay, no—*
In truth, it was far from okay.
He had never experienced anything like this before.

Alex slowly stopped. Like someone who had lost their drive, he stood rooted to the spot, staring ahead. The institute was filled with people. People with clear destinations. People with purpose, people who undeniably had somewhere to return to. He knew there were many in the world unhappier than him, but
Right now, he couldn't bring himself to say it was okay.
Because now, Alex Yeon had no one left whom he could love.
Please cross the yellow line.
He had learned about the brain before.

The human brain eliminates circuits it doesn't use. To remember something, one must repeatedly engage those circuits to strengthen them. Times, faces, and places not recalled fade like fine dust and eventually disappear. Like forgotten objects left to languish in a basement.
Nathan wanted to forget Alex like that.
From the age of seventeen, when he transferred schools to Oxford, Nathan slept only four hours a day. On days when the medication didn't work properly, he sometimes slept only three hours.

The reasons he couldn't sleep were plentiful. The boy who had switched schools ahead of university entrance had a mountain of work to catch up on. He had to study several subjects he hadn't taken before and familiarize himself with new faces. The changed uniform felt uncomfortable, and the quiet town where he knew no one was irritating. Consequently, there was no time for sleep.

His mother, Nora, noticed Nathan's abnormality one night, a month after they moved to Oxford. She encountered her son, who had gone to bed early, in the kitchen at 3 a.m. Nathan held a carton of chocolate milk. His mother, recalling how her son used to buy it often in the past, had purchased chocolate milk at the supermarket that evening.

Nathan was opening the refrigerator door, gripping the milk carton so tightly that his hand turned white. Only after a frightened Nora carefully touched his shoulder did he turn his head. The face of her always-beautiful son was pale.

To her question about what was wrong, Nathan asked if he could throw away the milk she had bought today. In Nora's memory, Nathan was always a calm and rational child. Not a boy who spoke such incomprehensible words. Nathan ended up discarding all the milk that day.

That wasn't the only strange behavior. Before long, Nora realized Nathan wasn't sleeping. The light in his room was rarely off, and even then, for no more than four hours. Seeing the persistent nosebleed Nathan suffered as he was getting ready for school,
She took her son to the hospital, tears streaming down her face.

The doctor diagnosed it as insomnia due to stress. Worried about the condition afflicting her quiet son who had grown up without any apparent troubles, she took a leave of absence. Then, she stayed by her son's side, filling his empty time. As the time spent with her own son grew longer, Nora realized Nathan was no longer the same as before. Her son didn't bring friends home. And he didn't smile, not even a little.

Finally, Nora asked Nathan one thing. To his mother's question about why he found it hard to sleep, Nathan didn't answer. There were simply too many reasons he couldn't sleep. It was better to study a bit more during the time he should be sleeping, and by doing so, he could catch up on the curriculum.
And he could shut out the image of Alex that haunted him whenever he closed his eyes.

The moment his consciousness was about to sink into slumber, Nathan's head, as if following a set routine, etched Alex's face before his eyes. When that frustrated face, holding back tears, surfaced, his heart boiled like a blaze, driving Nathan to the brink of madness. He didn't even know if that emotion was anger.

Nathan wanted to erase Alex from himself. That's why he couldn't sleep. Because if he kept seeing that kid in his dreams, he'd never be able to erase him. To not remember, he had to avoid thinking of Alex in any situation.

The first emotion he had labeled 'liking' was tenacious like a weed. Even after the insomnia improved very slowly and time passed to the point where he no longer pushed away approaching people, Nathan discovered traces of Alex in the vast world.
He didn't even look at soccer matches.

Disliking everything he once loved, Nathan tried to forget the being he had cherished the most. Then, surely, he could also stop flinching and looking every time he saw black hair walking down the street on a rainy day.
The subway was dirty, so he didn't want to ride it.

And clearly, it was effective. The year he graduated university, Nathan finally stopped dreaming. He buried deep in his subconscious the memory of that dark, narrow alley, the day he first experienced proper violence. The smell of blood-soaked earth, the back of his hand reddened and bruised from striking skin, the cruel and disgusting words, the sound of sirens... All of that disappeared.

The instances of waking up gasping from a light sleep also ceased. Rainy days still made him feel uneasy, and he still couldn't sleep soundly, but this level was no longer uncomfortable. The existence named Alex Yeon was clearly disappearing like that within Nathan White.
Until five weeks ago, before reuniting with Alex.

On that night at the hospital where he saw Alex again, Nathan thought he had done well. His head was cold, as if rewarding the effort he had made over long years to forget. Even seeing the physique that had changed little since childhood, and the faint joy frosting in the eyes that had grown wide as if startled, Nathan believed he was someone who had nothing to do with him. He ignored him like that.

However, the moment he 'looked down' at Alex, whom he encountered in the hallway, he felt a fine crack forming in his reason. The eyes he always had to look up at now required him to slightly lower his head to see properly. Were the dark brown eyes that stared so squarely at only him like this? Like this...

A cross-section of deeply buried memory flared up like a flame. He remembered the boy he used to be, the one who truly believed he would grow tall, and Alex, laughing brilliantly at that very thought, flashed before his eyes. To extinguish the embers that kept trying to spread inside, he recalled the rule. The rule he had established while cutting off Alex.
Forget Alex.
Forget the wound he gave, the words he said, the outcome he chose.

Only then did it seem he could live. The memory of that day was terrifyingly unbearable, and Nathan learned for the first time that he could be that weak. Hitting an ordinary person, not a sparring partner, was a completely different dimension. Even though he wanted to forget and was actually forgetting, the sensation of that time, along with memories of Alex, often visited Nathan at night.
The words his instructor at the time, Yona, had said didn't even remain in his head. Something about not using force on someone who wasn't properly trained.

The moment he heard Alex had driven him to this, his body was no longer his own. The thought of his fist crushing living flesh, of seeing terror bloom on the faces that had sneered at him, was utterly horrifying. The sensation of blood bursting and slicking his hands was sickening.
The rational Nathan White ceased to exist. He only came to his senses after breaking the teeth of the person who tried to attack him. Blood was everywhere.
*How dare I want to be a police officer after injuring someone like this.*

Faced with the result he had created, Nathan was paralyzed. For him, who had always lived rationally and logically, it was an unforeseen event. The hatred directed at himself consumed his soul like a flame. This too was an emotion Nathan had never felt toward himself before.

chapters.title: Chapter 91
paragraphs: Everything that followed was unprecedented for Nathan. He had never experienced his own reaction to the cruel words Alex spat out with a pale face, nor the suffocating despair that felt like being strangled.
That wasn't the end.
Even hurt by Alex's words about secondary genders—words Nathan couldn't comprehend—he found himself recalling Alex's face. He couldn't forget it: that face, tearful-eyed, lips pressed tight.
*Could there be a reason?*

That thought surfaced from somewhere deep within his heart. *Perhaps it wasn't his true feeling after all?* The anxious behavior Alex had shown, and the phone call asking if he would be forgiven even for a mistake, kept overlapping in his mind. His brain refused to accept reality and continued to fabricate reasons. Reasons to keep liking Alex.

Reason and emotion clashed, shattering him. Reason couldn't comprehend a heart that defied its judgment. At times, he felt like he was losing his mind. The solid foundation that supported Nathan was visibly crumbling. Sleepless, his memories kept returning to that day.
To survive, Nathan had to forget Alex.

Returning to the present, Nathan tried to adhere to this rule. He ignored Alex and even became hostile towards him. But it was futile. His mind urged him to pay him no mind, yet when he came to his senses, he found himself gripping Alex's wrist. His body moved before reason could make a judgment.

Whenever he became entangled with Alex, the standards and rules he had established always lost their meaning. It was Alex who made him, who detested uncertainty, contemplate meeting a different secondary gender, and Alex was the only one who could make him retract his words. The boy who held the sole place in his life, even as he matured into a young man, still held sway over him.
"Nathan, isn't that your phone ringing right now?"

His gaze, which had been fixed on empty space, refocused. As he slowly turned his head, he saw his mother's face. His mother, who had come up after cleaning the basement, was observing him with a puzzled expression. He straightened his body, which had been loosely leaning against the sofa, and reached out his arm. The phone on the table was vibrating noisily. He quietly glanced at the name displayed on the screen. It was Jude Lawrence.
"This is Nathan White."
Even though he knew the name, Nathan answered with a curt, formal introduction. Then, a bright voice echoed from the other end of the phone.
"Nathan, hi! How have you been?"

The moment he heard the question about his well-being, his expressionless face faltered slightly. Alex, with his eyebrows drooping weakly and his lips pressed tight to suppress his emotions, immediately sprang to mind. That was an uncontrollable territory, beyond the reach of Nathan's reason or consciousness.
"Yeah. What's up?"
Unlike his initial hesitation to answer readily, Nathan affirmed Jude's words. Despite the bleak reply, Jude responded in his good-natured voice.
"You're coming to the alumni reunion tonight, right? You promised last time."

It was more bothersome to answer, so Nathan simply replied that he understood. It had only been a few months since he reconnected with Jude. After naturally losing contact when he transferred schools, he hadn't heard any news until they coincidentally met at a medical conference in London a few months ago and re-established contact. Back then, Jude had inquired about the alumni reunion he had been preparing for a year, and Nathan had initially declined...
Slowly raising his hand, he rubbed between his eyebrows. Tracing his neat brow bone firmly with his fingertips, he spoke in a low voice.
"I'm sorry, but I don't think I can make it."

Perhaps at another time, but attending the alumni reunion in his current state wasn't a wise choice. His mood was low, and he hadn't slept for three days. Ever since refusing Alex, his old insomnia had flared up severely. Attending a gathering that would inevitably remind him of Alex in this condition was foolish.
"Please, Nathan! Tina said she's coming too, even though she wasn't in our class. It's been so long since we've seen each other. Please, please, please, okay?"
"Jude."
When Nathan called his name firmly, Jude replied in a noticeably dejected tone.
"Really not? Tina and I were really looking forward to it."

Even though the tone of voice bore no resemblance to Alex's, Nathan hesitated simply because it sounded disheartened. His mind became instantly complicated. Wiping his tired complexion, he opened his mouth after a long silence.
"Okay, fine. You said 7 o'clock tonight, right?"
"You remembered! Thank you. Then we'll see you tonight, okay?"
Jude, after reiterating his point, hung up after saying goodbye.

Nathan placed the phone back on the table and stood up. Today was the weekend, and he had adjusted his hospital schedule in advance to assist his mother with her move. He had also postponed his collaboration with Ilai Walker at the research institute today due to the case. Despite it being a long-awaited day off, he didn't feel rested. He was exhausted.
"Nathan, is this yours?"
Nora, who had brought up another box from the basement while he was on the phone, asked him. He tilted his head slightly. Nora pointed at the doll placed on top of the box.

"You really liked it when you brought it home, remember. I still recall you bringing home a doll, which was so unlike you. I remember you placing it on your desk and looking at it, but I suppose you packed it away when you moved and forgot about it. Are you throwing it away?"

The doll was shaped like a puppy. It was a white husky with slightly upturned eyes that, strangely enough, looked gentle and cute. Aside from the accumulated dust, there were hardly any traces of time evident. Except for the top of its head, its body was surprisingly clean. Nathan blinked slowly. Letting out a soft sigh, he stood up. Stopping in front of his mother, whom he now had to look down at as he had grown so tall, he reached out his long arm and took the doll.
*Alek.*
He repeated the doll's name in his heart. As if responding, its black eyes stared intently at Nathan. He could see his own reflection in them.

Unlike the young boy he once was, he wasn't happy. He wasn't tense with the excitement of a first date, nor did the calm demeanor of someone who had never been hurt remain. Even though so much time had passed that the Nathan White of the past seemed to no longer exist in this world...
He could find the him who received the doll that day within his own reflection in the doll's black pupils.
Then and now, Nathan was hopelessly drawn to the person named Alex.
"Nathan, are you okay?"
At the sound of his name being called, his thoughts scattered.
"You haven't looked well lately. Are you sleeping okay?"
Worry etched itself onto his mother's face.
"Yes."
He lied nonchalantly. Nora scrutinized him as if trying to gauge the truth, then asked with a sigh.
"Should I throw that doll away for you?"
Strength entered the hand holding the doll. There was only one answer. There was no reason to keep such a doll. Hadn't he lived forgetting about it all this time? It was unnecessary trash.
"No."
Yet, Nathan's mouth uttered a different answer.
"I'll take it with me."

As if afraid someone would snatch the doll away, he lowered his arm. The doll was so small it would still fit comfortably in his large hand. *I should throw it away,* he thought, but Nathan also wondered where he should put it.
"That's unusual."
Nora looked at him strangely, shrugged, and then patted Nathan's arm.
"Alright then. We're almost done cleaning, so can you help a little more?"
"Yes."
The desk.
Yes, on the desk would be good.
Because Alex might see it if he visits again. He'd probably like it. While failing to hide it properly, putting on that foolish expression where he can't even openly show his liking.
Nathan closed his mouth. His lips stiffened and slowly twisted. A hot lump welled up inside him. He had a foolish thought.
*He'll never come again.*
*Because I refused.*
*You, who said you liked me... I refused.*
His body grew heavy. A headache began to throb, so Nathan raised his hand and pressed his eyelids. The shallow breath beneath his pale lips was slightly damp.

chapters.title: Chapter 92
paragraphs: As Nathan drove to the reunion venue Jude had arranged, he replayed his actions. What he had said to Alex wasn't wrong. At least, according to his reason, it wasn't. It was a defensive response, a final line of defense restraining the impulses his traitorous body had committed. He wished he could have feigned ignorance and let it pass, but circumstances kept entangling them. After Alex, who had taken his words at face value, had nearly ended up in danger, Nathan could no longer do even that. He had grabbed Alex under the flimsy pretext that he was an eyesore. Retreating step by step, Nathan had hit a wall.
The wall erected by the wounded young boy signified only one thing.

He didn't want to get hurt again. Even though the wound that had utterly demolished and shaken him was too intense and sharp to bear a second time, he felt as if the wall would crumble if he let his guard down even slightly. He feared he would lose his way, stepping into a world where neither reason nor intellect held sway.
That was why he had refused the confession.

Even though he was already foolishly concerned about Alex, he deemed it impossible to overcome the single obstacle of simply trusting Alex. There were times when Alex revealed his thoughts even less than Nathan himself. What was Alex thinking when he said that? Why did he have to push him away like that? Why did he say he liked him when he wouldn't trust him... Nathan couldn't understand a single one of Alex’s actions.
A person’s fundamental nature doesn't change much, and a lifetime of behavior doesn't alter easily. There's a disposition, much like inertia, that tries to return to its original state.

This wasn't solely Alex's problem. Nathan would likely never understand Alex's actions. Therefore, this decision was right. Just as Alex couldn't trust him, he couldn't trust Alex either. They simply didn't fit. It must have been fate.

Suppressing the bitter aftertaste of emotion, Nathan turned off the ignition. It was 6:55 PM. After parking in the restaurant lot Jude had reserved for the reunion, he stood before the elevator. Someone stood beside him, staring straight ahead with an expressionless face. Nathan paid no mind to the clicking sound of their shoes.

He saw the other person's face when the elevator door opened and they stepped inside. It wasn't intentional; ingrained etiquette moved him. The moment he pressed the button and waited for the other person to enter, their eyes met. After a brief bow of his head, he noticed striking curly hair.
The wide-open, round eyes were vaguely familiar. After a few seconds, Nathan slowly recalled the other person's name.
Jessica Bundy, was it?
That was the name. With eyes that held not a shred of interest, he stepped into the elevator. There was no nostalgia whatsoever for a face he hadn't seen in a long time.

However, Jessica Bundy seemed to feel differently. She looked up at him, her eyes wide with alarm, and her lips parted as if to speak. Then, as if struck by a sudden memory, she flinched, recoiled, and pressed herself against the elevator wall. Silence descended. Nathan averted his cool gaze from her and watched the closing door.

Jessica Bundy continued to act strangely. She kept glancing at him repeatedly, as if overly mindful of his presence. As soon as the doors opened, she disappeared as if fleeing, her shoes quickly tapping away. Her retreating back might have been objectively quite attractive, but Nathan stared ahead with eyes as cold as if looking at a lump of mineral.

Wearing a navy casual suit, he walked down the corridor with an impassive expression. Following the noisy sounds, a sign appeared: Clairewood School Class A Reunion. As the school's name entered his vision, his throat felt tight. Even though he wasn't wearing a tie, he felt a constriction in his nape. He raised a long finger, lightly rubbed his Adam's apple, and lowered his arm.

The restaurant, arranged in a hall format, had a high ceiling. A huge chandelier dyed the interior crimson, and in the spacious hall were several large oval tables. Over twenty people had already arrived and were drinking wine at the bar. Amidst the lively atmosphere, Nathan alone remained expressionless.
*Would it have been more enjoyable if Alex were here?*

While having this meaningless thought, Nathan spotted Jude. His face hadn't changed much since Nathan had last seen him at the academic conference. Jude also spotted him a few seconds later. A smile rose on his fair face, dotted with faint freckles, and Nathan watched him wave cheerfully, beaming. Beside Jude stood a woman with long blonde hair. That was likely Tina.
"Nathan, you're right on time!"
Jude, who had hurried over, clasped his hand. Tina, who had walked over slowly, looked up at him with a curious expression, then smiled.
"Long time no see."
"See? I told you he really grew a lot, didn't I?"
They were still best friends, as Jude linked arms with Tina and whispered.
"That's right. He must be even more popular now, Nathan."
"Right!"

Jude giggled as if something was immensely amusing. Looking down at them with a dry expression, Nathan opened his mouth. Even though they were friends he'd had by his side longer than Alex, no emotional turbulence stirred within Nathan. A faint sense of gladness barely raised its head.
"Hi."

However, perhaps satisfied even with that brief reply, Jude's eyes crinkled as he smiled. This time, for some reason, a feeling of longing arose, and he stared into space, not even knowing what he was longing for.

The party was predictably dull. People exchanged perfunctory introductions about their jobs, trying to leverage old acquaintances into new connections. When they learned he was a doctor, he was immediately surrounded, but mentioning his specialization in Secondary Gender quickly thinned the crowd. Never one for small talk, he knew from experience that silence was usually enough to make them drift away.
Jessica Bundy was sitting at the farthest spot from his table. He knew this because Jude had whispered into his ear.
"Nathan, Jessica keeps looking at you. Seeing you after so long, maybe her feelings are resurfacing?"
"Doesn't look like it to me?"

Tina cautiously objected. Without even turning his head, Nathan took a sip of his martini. Time passed sluggishly. For no reason, he felt restless. It was a feeling that had come intermittently since refusing Alex.
"Jessica has a lot of pride. I don't think she'd do that, especially after Nathan rejected her."
"Yeah, that's true. Because of Alex..."
Jude, who was responding to Tina's words, suddenly clamped his mouth shut. Seeing him hurriedly checking his expression as if apologetic, Nathan smoothed his brow.
"It's fine to talk about it. I've seen him recently."
Not intending to make the atmosphere more awkward, he offered a short answer. Startled expressions simultaneously appeared on both their faces.
"What?!"
Jude leaned his upper body low and let out a sharp squeal. Tina went straight to the point.
"Oh, really? That's good. After that incident, neither you nor Alex told us anything and just stopped seeing each other, so it felt really lonely."
Jude, blinking his eyes as if still not believing it, stuck close to Nathan's side.
"So, you two made up? Can I ask what happened?"

It was an ambiguous question. He couldn't readily answer the question of whether they had made up. "Made up" implied resolution, but their relationship was still stagnant. Even though he had forgiven Alex, it remained so.
"You don't have to tell us if you don't want to, of course!"
Jude hastily added. Tina nodded.
"Alex said he was wrong to you, but I was just curious because it's hard to believe. You know too, but Alex really liked you, didn't he?"

Looking at Tina's face, which smiled gently as if reminiscing about the past, Nathan fell silent. The moment he had been worried about had arrived. Hearing talk about Alex was more bothersome than he had thought. Indistinguishable feelings—whether guilt, regret, or lingering attachment—began to stain his insides black. After taking another sip of his martini, he excused himself.
"Sorry for cutting the conversation short, but I'll step out for a moment."
"Okay, see you later."
Jude waved cautiously. Pushing his chair back quietly, Nathan got up and left his seat. His long legs gradually widened their stride.

chapters.title: Chapter 93
paragraphs: I came out of the restroom. At the end of the hallway, opening the wooden door with its creaking old hinges revealed another restroom. I slowly moved my feet and stood before the sink in front of the mirror. My ghostly complexion looked utterly ridiculous. I washed my hands for a long time in the cold water. Only after making my hands so cold that no thoughts could surface did I finally calm down.

And by an unpleasant coincidence, I ran into Jessica Bundy again. Her face was flushed, perhaps from having drunk quite a bit. She seemed even more startled and showed a more nervous reaction than when we had met in the elevator, stepping backwards. It was an overly sensitive reaction, like someone who had something to feel guilty about.
"Why?"

Suddenly, she threw out a sharp question. I silently looked down at her. The restroom was structured so that upon opening the door and entering, one would go through different doors depending on gender, and Jessica Bundy was blocking the door leading to the hallway.
"Stop looking at me like that."

A hysterical voice rang through the air, and then Jessica Bundy quickly opened the door and left. Her behavior, which seemed inexplicable, was a bit bothersome, so I stared in the direction she had disappeared.

Just then, the women's restroom door opened again. A woman with black short hair popped out abruptly. I had seen her hanging out with Jessica Bundy at school a few times. I had never asked her name. "Jessica! You left your phone!"

She was holding two phones in her hand. As if she hadn't expected anyone to be there, the woman looked up with a startled face, then immediately wore an expression of fright. The way her face turned pale was visibly noticeable.
"Yes, Nathan."

Given the series of strange behaviors I had witnessed, I finally reacted. It wasn't so much that I was annoyed, but more because the situation was suspicious. It was definitely odd that even a woman whose name I didn't know was acting as if she'd seen a ghost. As I looked down at her with cold eyes, she noticeably avoided my gaze and spoke. "I heard you were here. So, how have you been?"

Her voice trembled miserably. Her attempt to feign composure was so pathetic it was embarrassing to even call it acting. I found this situation bothersome, but I concluded that getting involved in something might help take my mind off Alex. With a weary expression, I asked in return.
"Well. How do you think I've been?"

Instead of showing the courtesy of asking her name, I posed a question. The woman seemed flustered by my flat, lifeless voice. Gaping her mouth, she grabbed the handle of the door leading to the hallway and spat out a sentence.
"D-David, I really had no idea he'd use the photo like that! I'm sorry. Jessica never specifically said not to show it!"
Photo?

Nothing came to mind from Jessica Bundy's name and the word 'photo,' so I furrowed my brow. It seemed there was something. Thinking of her previous, obviously faked laughter, something felt off. With a bad premonition, I hardened my expression and then extended my hand to the woman. "Give it."
"W-what?"
"I said give me the phone. I'll hand it over."
Instead of urging her, I just quietly watched, and the woman hesitated but then placed the phone on my palm. An emotion—whether guilt or self-consolation—washed over her face.
"Should I say thank you?"

At the question in my dry voice, the woman shook her head, then pushed the door she was holding and quickly slipped out of there. Listening to the clatter of high heels filling the hallway, I took my time before coming out into the hallway.

When I returned to the dining hall, Jessica Bundy had moved to another seat. Seeing her putting on her outerwear, it seemed she was about to leave. After apologizing to Jude and Tina, I slowly walked over to Jessica.

Jessica was talking with another man. Standing in front of her as she was pouring out words with a flushed face, the gazes of both people simultaneously focused on me. A lazy smile played on my pale face as I leaned my elbows on the table, lowering my upper body.
"It seems we have something to talk about."
As if she hadn't expected me to smile, Jessica widened her eyes and looked at me.
"Oh, it's Nathan. Was I interrupting something?"
The man, who hadn't grasped the situation, said that. Without wiping the smile from my face, I spoke.
"I'd appreciate it if you'd step aside."

Jessica, who belatedly came to her senses, tried to grab me, saying "Wait a minute," but the man moved out of the way first. Watching Jessica, who looked flustered and tried to follow me, I said quietly.
"You should take your phone."
"What?"

She sharply retorted and spun her body around. Her sharply raised eyes glared at me. I slowly wiped the smile from my face and shook the phone. Only then, as if realizing, Jessica gritted her teeth hard. As I stared indifferently at her lipstick getting smeared, she opened her mouth.
"It's all over, so why do you keep doing this?"
"What's all over."
Even though it was a statement I couldn't understand at all, I patiently asked quietly. Then Jessica raised her voice irritably.
"The photos are all deleted, and it wasn't even your photo to begin with! Alex Yeon came and checked everything, so why are you making a fuss now?"
Alex?
At the name I never expected to hear in this situation, my eyes widened.

I knew Jessica was vain and that she considered our relationship something to boast about. When I heard the word 'photo,' I had just thought she'd probably used some photo I didn't know about in an annoying way, that was all.
But I hadn't anticipated Alex's name coming up.
The faint, twisted smile remaining on my face froze coldly. With eyes that had turned cold and icy green, I looked down at her.
"Say that again."
"W-what, who do you think you are, ordering me around? I didn't do anything wrong. It's Alex Yeon or David Mac who are wrong for believing a photo they found somewhere was of you!"

My heart began to beat rapidly. My body heated up instantly. Feeling my throat constrict again, I rubbed my Adam's apple with my finger. Alex's face, pleading 'Please, just once, listen to why I did it,' surged up. My fingertips tingled.
"Properly."
I didn't raise my voice. The low, subdued voice merely urged her to tell the truth. But Jessica, unable to contain her anger, huffed with a flushed face. She even looked quite aggrieved.
"What photo they found, and how Alex believed it."
I had a bad feeling about this.
"What Alex checked, tell me everything properly."
Very.
"No!"
Jessica spat out viciously. I asked quietly in return.
"No?"
"Yeah, th-this!.."
Jessica trembled and raised her eyes sharply. I smiled coldly.
"Alright, then. If you did nothing wrong and don't want to talk, I'll find out myself. Didn't you say you work at a modeling agency? Should I just do to you what you did?"
"Are you crazy?"
Jessica screamed. As the sound grew louder, the surrounding gazes converged on them.
"Why is this?"
"What are you trying to do to me?"
"Well, I'll have to find out from now on. Why? You said you didn't do anything wrong. Then there's nothing to worry about, right?"
Slowly leaning my hunched body closer to her, I spoke without even blinking.
"Isn't that so?"

Jessica's face turned pale. Jude and Tina, who had approached at some point, were looking at me worriedly. I heard someone say I was scaring Jessica, but I didn't move. More accurately, it was truer to say nothing was entering my vision right now. In the feeling of my nerves burning out, I endured.
As people's gazes gathered and words of concern for her seemed to be heard, Jessica changed her attitude.
"Stop harassing me and get away!"
Whispers increased around them. A voice telling me to stop came from somewhere. I maintained my stance.

Jessica even started crying. The man who had stepped aside earlier because of me came back to her side and glared at me. Twisting my lips, I silently stared at Jessica. Jude and Tina grabbed my arm as if to say we should leave now. It was then that someone stepped forward.
"Nathan didn't do anything wrong."
It was the short-haired woman I had encountered in the restroom. Jessica whipped her head around.

chapters.title: Chapter 94
paragraphs: "Nathan's transfer was because of a photo Jessica showed."
"Kate, shut your mouth!"
Jessica rose as if she were about to rush at her.
"What kind of photo was it?"
Nathan asked with strained patience. The woman wore a mortified expression. Traces of a fierce internal struggle flickered across her face before she soon ground her teeth and spoke.

"It's... a nude photo. I- I mean... To be precise, it was a photo of someone else who looked like you. We only found out later. We didn't know David Mac might have shown it to the Alphas. We only learned about it after Alex came and told us to delete it."
A sharp intake of breath, the sound of someone sucking in air, came from Jude. A different kind of commotion than before spread loudly, and then all eyes turned toward Jessica.
But Nathan couldn't take in any of it. The moment Alex's name came up again, his breath hitched.

His head throbbed as if it had been slammed against the floor; his mind was numb. Unable to process what he had just heard, he had to chew over the sentences for several agonizing seconds. Alex did what?
What?
"Jessica, you should have some conscience. You heard everything David Mac said. What he demanded from Alex using that photo..."
"What's the big deal? Getting to date a pretty Omega, isn't that good for him, an Alpha?"
"Are you saying that now?!"
"Are you pretending to be good now, you crazy bitch!"

The fight soon degenerated into a heated argument between the two. The noisy clamor of the hall, now a battlefield, echoed dully in his ears. He couldn't think of anything. Nothing except replaying the words he had just heard in his head.
The words about dating an Omega, about making him delete the photo... The photo.
A nude photo?

A raw, bloody emotion surged up violently. His fingers trembled. The words from Jessica and Kate's mouths weren't neatly organized, but the main outline had been pieced together. Jessica had shown her friends a nude photo that looked like him. It had gotten into the hands of a man named David, and Alex had wanted it deleted.
Instead of me.
In the story he couldn't have guessed, this was what surfaced in Nathan's mind.
*Why did you hide it, Alex?*
The answer came immediately. Alex had wanted to give the explanation he'd tried to give. The one who hadn't listened was Nathan himself. Nathan White, that very person.
"Then please, just once... won't you listen to why I did it?"

What had he said to Alex, who had clung to him with a desperate face? He'd said, what difference would that make? He hadn't tried to hear the reason. Because what was done was done. Because Alex had chosen and brought it upon himself. On the very first day he brought Alex into his home, Nathan had even said this.
"I don't care what circumstances you had."
*I don't care.*
*Whatever you went through, I don't care.*
He'd said that.
Truly, rationally speaking, what had happened to Alex was already a past event. Knowing the reason wouldn't make the past disappear. Alex had chosen the method of pushing him away while hurting him.

Nathan thought that was the extent of Alex's feelings. That was also the reason he had tried to forget him. He was afraid of his own heart trying to find any reason to like Alex again. He hated that he was only someone Alex could trust that much, hated that their feelings weren't mutual. Because Alex's reaction to the first confession he'd ever made was different from what he'd expected, so he thought that was the extent of Alex's feelings.
But in all those moments, had he ever tried to understand Alex?
*Why you did it, why you showed that reaction, had he ever tried to understand more about the environment that shaped you and the thoughts you were having?*

At the very least, he should have tried harder. On the subject that Alex Yeon considered most important, Nathan had never properly tried to grasp Alex. He knew the kid was clumsy, but he didn't know why a clumsy kid like him had acted like that. If he couldn't figure it out, he should have asked, and if he didn't get an answer even when he asked, then at least,
*Because I had never forgotten Alex.*
In every moment he was trying to forget Alex, he was thinking of Alex. There was no way he could forget Alex.

From the moment he first saw him, he couldn't leave Alex alone. Like a riverbed where all the water had dried up, leaving only traces behind, the memories with Alex existed somewhere in his chest like that. Nathan didn't want that river to flow again and wished it would just weather away and disappear in the wind.
He believed then the scars Alex left would also disappear.

But Nathan revived that river with just the smallest fragment of Alex. In the blink of an eye, the revived stream of water became a flooding tsunami and was engulfing him. His body didn't follow reason. He hated seeing his back turned, so he grabbed him. The face that looked like he was all alone irritated him madly, so he grabbed him again.
*I still like him.*
He had only covered up the memories, not erased them. Despite that, whenever he saw Alex, he was shaken, and as always, he tried to act rationally. He wanted to maintain balance that way.
*What good was that.*
*If I ultimately couldn't forget, if I liked you more than the wounds I received, then I shouldn't have treated you that way. You were truly never not my priority.*
*I didn't know that.*
*Me, of all people.*

His insides were stained completely black. His mind was painted black, and he felt as if his soul had been pierced. The lips that would float a shy, fluttering smile when they saw him came to mind. The well-shaped eyebrows that curved gently unlike his sharp eyes, the round earlobes, the neck and face that flushed so easily... they were all unbearably lovely.

He couldn't even begin to grasp what Alex must have endured without telling him. His heart felt as if it were being torn apart, ground to dust. That foolish kid said he'd protect me, tried to delete the photo, pushed me away, said he did things I hadn't done. Even if the method was wrong, the one Alex had tried to protect was Nathan.

He didn't know, and for a long time, he didn't know. Too many things were crashing down on him at once, and Nathan barely suppressed the nausea rising in his throat. Guilt stabbed his entire body like an awl.
"Nate."

The moment he even pictured the face that would happily smile, calling him by that nickname, as if something was so good, Nathan crumbled. Feeling as if he would die, he slowly turned his body. He didn't want to be here. He had to see Alex. Alex...

Suddenly, Nathan painfully recalled the fact that he had rejected Alex's confession. He had rejected Alex, who had clung to him desperately with a face about to cry, talking about trust. Even though it wasn't a wrong thing to say, Nathan couldn't possibly forgive himself for what he had said. If even I am like this, could Alex have trusted me?

With the sudden deluge of past stories, the room was in an uproar. As the story of David Mac, who had been a rising star as a soccer player, was added, many people took out their phones. Passing by Jude and Tina, who were looking around the hall with faces full of shock and anger, Nathan slipped out of there like a ghost.
Jude, who had been watching him leave, opened his mouth, looking at Jessica and Kate.
"You know neither of you ever properly apologized to Nathan? To Alex, and to Nathan."
The two who had been arguing shut their mouths. Tina finished with a cold look in her eyes.
"You'll definitely get back what you've lived like. You guys who make a spectacle out of bad things that happen to others."
Silence fell. As Jude and Tina also left their seats, the hall where the alumni reunion had been continuing soon became disorderly, and people left one by one.
People do not die from loneliness. So, it couldn't be said that it was a direct cause of death.

Therefore, Alex did not die. He still breathed, ate, slept, woke up, and went to work. Having many things to do became a reason to live and moved Alex. But he couldn't help feeling hollow, as if he were left all alone. Even smiling was too much effort, so he remained silent and immersed himself in his work.

chapters.title: Chapter 95
paragraphs: The day Sergeant Hayden recommended counseling to him was the fifth day since the incident with Nathan. Sergeant Hayden placed a single sheet of paper in front of Alex, who had been working consecutive night shifts without rest. *Thud*. At the sound of the paper slapping the desk, Alex raised his eyes.
"I've booked it for today. Go get it."
"Huh?"
"You look terrible. Whatever's going on, just take it."

Alex blinked. Sergeant Hayden was looking at him, an unlit cigarette in his hand. His face was scrunched up as if everything in the world was a bother. Alex glanced away to check the time; it was lunch hour. Stroking the file where he had compiled everything about Sera Oates, Alex subtly expressed his intention to refuse.
"I don't think I have time for that."
"Of course, we're busy. We have to catch these bastards. But this is more important for you."

The paper had the counselor's name and a time written on it. Katrina Bell. 4 PM. It was almost time for him to leave. Looking between the file and Sergeant Hayden, Alex asked, wanting to confirm just one thing.
"It was Matthew, right?"
"I don't know that."
"I had a feeling."

It was almost certain that Matthew had spoken to Sergeant Hayden. He'd been urging Alex to get counseling for a while, and when Alex didn't listen, he probably resorted to getting Hayden to order it. Since it was a direct order, Alex had no choice but to pick up the paper with a reluctant expression.
"Understood."
"We're going to go talk to the magistrate with the evidence from the research institute, so contact me when you're done."
"Will we get a search warrant?"
"That depends on how solid what Ilai and that doctor found is. I think we will."

The situation had become clearer over the past few days. First, the suspects in the victims' murders were determined to be either the man in the suit or Patrick Shore. The criterion was who had direct contact with the victims.

To identify the man in the suit, they needed to find Patrick Shore. Anna had gone undercover at various language exchange meetups to confirm this. Patrick Shore hadn't appeared at the meetups since the initial contact period with the victims, but fortunately, they'd obtained some useful testimonies. Perhaps because he'd been memorable, quite a few people remembered him.

According to acquaintances of [Corrected Name], the victims had innocent personalities and were tight-lipped. It was suggested that Patrick likely selected those who were also in need of money. In other words, he chose individuals who were naive and steadfast enough to participate in an experiment and adhere to a confidentiality agreement. That was probably why nothing had leaked.
Next was the mastermind behind these two suspects. There were other candidates, but MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company, where Amy Wainings had interviewed, was designated as the likely source.

The problem was which group within the company had made this decision. To dig into that, they now needed to start contacting people inside the company and investigate the research institute, because they needed evidence. What they had so far was only circumstantial evidence.
If they could just find definitive proof that the 'Perrin' injected into the victims came from their research institute, that part would be somewhat resolved.

After that, what remained was the reason why Amy Wainings had become a target and why Sera Oates had gone missing. These two were clearly connected. This was precisely the part Alex was investigating.
"Yes."
"Well then, get going."
At the urging to get out, Alex packed his belongings and stood up.

London was now fully adorned in winter colors. In preparation for Christmas a few weeks away, markets overflowed with Christmas-related goods and food. Everything from packaged turkeys to roast beef was available ready-made, and small trees and cute trinkets were on display.

Strings of light decorations lined the streets in central London. Double-decker buses passed perilously close beneath them, and on the South Bank, Christmas markets were beginning to open. Passing nearby, the sweet smell of mulled wine warmly pricked the nose. Even though he had some time to spare, London was entirely in the mood for an upcoming festival.

The sun now began to set very early, and it would start getting dark after 3 PM. By the time he arrived at the counseling office, it was already pitch black outside. The cold, windy scent clinging to his coat felt hollow in his nostrils. Unable to join in the festive spirit, he acutely felt his loneliness, and his heart ached with a solitude that was hard to bear.

Dr. Katrina Bell's townhouse was on Great Smith Street. The clinic, which had no sign or marker, was a place for the police, and Dr. Bell had long served here as a specialist counselor. It was convenient that it was only about a ten-minute walk from the police station, so he didn't have to walk far.

The clinic he was visiting for the first time was austere and calm. The wood-dominated space, lit by a soft yellow light, naturally evoked a serene atmosphere. After proving his identity at the reception desk with a receptionist, he entered the consultation room. Dr. Bell was sitting in a chair by the high-set window. With her pale blonde hair tied up in a single bundle, she looked to be roughly in her fifties.
"Hello. I'm Katrina Bell."
Dr. Bell rose from her seat, extending her hand to greet him. As they shook hands lightly, she smiled. The pheromones that brushed against him slightly let him know she was an Alpha.
"Hello. I'm Alex Yeon."
"Good, very good. Ah, if it's not too forward, may I call you Alex?"
"Please do."
"Then please call me Katrina too, Alex."
Dr. Bell gestured to the chair opposite. Sitting awkwardly on the plush leather sofa, she interlaced her fingers and placed them on her knee. Her smiling eyes made him feel more at ease.
"How did you come to be here, Alex?"
Alex told the truth.
"I was ordered to come."
"Many people start that way. Welcome."
"But I have nothing to talk about."
Dr. Bell just smiled. Rising from her seat, she walked over to where a kettle and tea were, then asked Alex.
"How about some black tea?"
Alex, who was about to refuse, just answered okay.
"How many spoons of sugar would you like?"
"Four spoons."
"You like it sweet."
Those words stirred something deep within him. A sudden wave threatened to overwhelm him, and Alex bit down hard on his lip to keep it at bay.

Even after all this time, Nathan had known his preference exactly. The thought that he had ruined that relationship, which was gradually accepting him, with his own foolish actions, surged forward, and agony burst forth. The festered and ruptured wound now hurt even at the slightest touch; it was painful just to think of the name Nathan.
"You look like you're holding in a lot."

Dr. Bell, having put the kettle water on, sat across from him. Alex raised his reddened eyes. Since finding his father's whereabouts and being rejected by Nathan, he hadn't had a proper conversation with anyone.
Even when Matthew came to see him the other day, Alex had avoided the topic. Matthew seemed convinced that Alex had seen it, having discovered the folder's open time.
"You saw it, right?"
"What?"
"The photo of your father I found. I checked the folder. Alex, damn it, I'm sorry."
To the apologizing Matthew, Alex put on a face that said it was nothing. He turned his head, said 'ah,' and told him it was okay.
"I wasn't sure you'd be okay seeing that. That's why I hid it. I'm truly sorry."
"It's fine. He's alive, so it's all good. I know you did it thinking of me."
"No, you're not okay."
Matthew wore an angry expression, as if on Alex's behalf. With a look of exasperation, he swept his hair back. Unconcerned about his face being visible from outside, he sighed and spoke.
"No one can be okay after seeing something like that."

Alex did not answer. The moment he admitted he wasn't okay, he didn't trust himself to hold his crumbling self together. He had no family, lover, or sibling to rely on. In a situation where he was barely getting through each day, it was clear life would become more miserable if he acknowledged his own weakness. Briefly crumbling,

chapters.title: Chapter 96
paragraphs: Alex laughed, pretending to have forgotten that day, and brushed off the conversation with Matthew.
"Do I look like that?"
Returning to reality, Alex asked. Dr. Bell answered with a question.
"Alex, you tell me. Any story is fine. I am someone who listens. Sometimes, just telling your story to someone who knows nothing about you can be a great comfort. I am not someone who judges you."
The suggestion to speak only made him feel more numb. He didn't know what to say. After contemplating for a few minutes, Alex voiced a feeling he'd had recently, or rather, all his life.
"I'm lonely."
"Why are you lonely, Alex?"
"Because... I'm alone."
The kettle made a loud boiling sound. Dr. Bell, with her fingers interlaced, looked at him quietly and asked.
"Is there no one around you, Alex? Family, colleagues, friends? My first impression was that you seemed like a very charming person."
Just as he was about to say there was no one, Alex thought of Matthew. Anna, who always spoke to him in a friendly manner, and... Nathan too.
"I have colleagues."
"People who care about you, Alex?"
"Yes."
"But why are you lonely, Alex?"
This was a question he had never properly considered. It took him a long time to produce an answer.
"Because the people who care about me can't solve my problems for me."
"What kind of problems?"
"Just, that kind of thing. Money or..."

"Of course, you're right about that, Alex. Those are problems they can't solve. But Alex, you can talk about the problems. You might get advice you hadn't thought of alone, from a different perspective. And if that doesn't work, well, just venting your difficult feelings and relying on someone a little might be possible, right? Because they're friends."
At the word 'relying on,' Alex frowned. It was an unfamiliar word to the point of feeling repulsive.
"You don't seem to like that idea."
Dr. Bell said softly with a smile. Alex rubbed his cheek lightly and admitted with a sigh.
"Yes."
"What part makes you uncomfortable, Alex?"
"The part about relying on the people around me."
"What's wrong with that?"
"It burdens the other person."

He had no memory of ever having relied on anyone. The parents Alex could have relied on were always busy with their own affairs. His mother didn't like him, and his father had high expectations of him. In that situation, the only person Alex could rely on was himself. That was
natural.
"Is Alex overly dependent?"
"No."
"Have you ever thought about this? That by not relying on them, the other person might feel hurt."

That was something he had truly never considered. Alex recalled Nathan's words. Nathan had said that he didn't trust him. It was also something he had always regretted. He thought many times that if they had just talked together and explored options, it wouldn't have led to this outcome. Though he couldn't even offer that as an excuse in front of Nathan.
"You don't have to do it with everyone. But if it's a precious person in a proper relationship, they won't dislike it if you trust and rely on them, Alex. Because that's a matter of trust."
Alex looked confused. The people Alex had trusted and followed had always left him. His father was like that, and his mother was too.
"The people I trusted... never stayed by my side."
"What kind of people were they?"
Dr. Bell asked calmly. Alex opened his mouth with a miserable feeling.
"My parents."
"They sound like bad people."
"Huh?"
Dr. Bell shrugged her shoulders. Alex blinked.
"My remark was inappropriate. I apologize. But Alex, I think they were bad. It wasn't wrong for you to rely on them. It's only natural."
No one had ever said that to him. Because it was a story he had never brought up before. He hadn't even told Nathan.
