It's okay to rely on someone you feel cares for you, Alex. Scholars have differing opinions, but I believe humans are social animals. A life where you can't trust anyone – how lonely must that be?

Dr. Bell got up from her seat. She slowly headed to the kettle, put in a teabag, poured a little milk, then added four spoons of sugar. After stirring the black tea briskly with a muddler, the doctor returned to her seat. A porcelain teacup was placed before him.
"Try it."
"Thank you."
Alex slowly reached out and took the teacup. He took a sip of the black tea, now a soft brown. It was sweet. Sweet enough to improve his mood.
"It's delicious."
"I'm glad."
Dr. Bell smiled. Then, she also began to drink her share of the tea. And so, the two drank their tea quietly.

The counseling session continued for another 20 minutes after that. Dr. Bell was a comfortable conversation partner. This kind of question-and-answer conversational style was the first he'd had with someone other than Nathan. Alex suddenly recalled that Nathan had always tried to understand the reason. He thought fleetingly that Nathan's method, which sometimes felt like pressing him for answers, might have been his way of trying to understand him.

Nothing had changed immediately just by spilling out his story. But his head felt a little clearer. He couldn't do something right away, but once his thoughts were sorted, he wanted to talk to Nathan one more time. If that wasn't possible, he now had things he wanted to convey, even if it meant using the old-fashioned method of a letter. As evening fell, the rain began to fall again. People so accustomed to the frequent rain were seen walking down the street without umbrellas. This was a very common sight in London. Mixed among them, Alex returned to headquarters. Inside, members of other investigation teams were each working on their assigned cases. His team was nowhere to be seen.
It was then that his phone rang. There were several missed calls on the screen. The caller ID showed the name Anna Lionel.
"Senior, something terrible has happened!"
"What's wrong?"
Anna's voice was extremely startled. The faint sound of a curse, *damn it*, was audible.
"Amy Wainings has disappeared. While one of the team members went out to buy groceries, she slipped out. Through a second-floor window!"
Alex recalled the structure of the house. The backyard was dirt with dry grass, and it wasn't that high. It was a plausible scenario.
"Any leads on her whereabouts?"
Alex quickly left the investigation headquarters and went down to the temporary vehicle usage recording area.

"They said a call came in that Wainings's mother had passed away. Clara heard the content of the call and after that, she couldn't calm down, and it seems she slipped out during that time. It happened two hours ago. Since she took her wallet, they tracked her card usage, and she bought a train ticket to London. Departure at 3:30 PM, arriving at Paddington."

After recording the vehicle issuance details, Alex took the car key and went down to the basement. Checking his wristwatch, it was 5:10 PM. He got into an unmarked black Ford and started the engine. It takes 40 minutes from Slough to Paddington. She would have arrived and left quite some time ago.
"She must have arrived and slipped away already. Did you send vehicle support to Wainings's family home too?"
"Yes. They said she hasn't arrived home yet. Her house is near Clapham Junction. Given the timing, she should have already arrived, but she hasn't shown up..."
"What about Matthew?"

"He's checking CCTV footage at the train station. The sergeant and I are at the house of the friend Wainings called. She said she was threatened by some man. Actually, Wainings's mother is perfectly fine. She said his face was covered by a hoodie so she couldn't see it well, but he was tall."
"Probably Patrick Shore. Fortunately, Wainings's friend remembered the vehicle license plate, so we're tracking it now."
"The sergeant must have requested additional support. I'll head to Wainings's house."
"Be careful, Senior!"
Driving the car toward Clapham Junction, Alex called Matthew. The Bluetooth speaker emitted a few rings, then Matthew answered the call.
"Alex, did you get the news?"
"Yeah. Did you check the footage?"

chapters.title: Chapter 97
paragraphs: "Yeah. Not good. Someone similar to the suspect was caught on camera. The face isn't visible, but we have footage of a man in a suit following Wainings. It looks like he chased after her outside the station when she took a taxi."
"Damn. It was a decoy. The taxi's license plate?"
"I couldn't see the full number, but I contacted the taxi company for a trace. Ah, I'm getting a call now. Hold on."

After pressing the hold button, Alex increased his speed a little more. Turning on the emergency lights, he swerved onto the shoulder and headed toward Clapham Junction as fast as possible. The fact that they were trying to approach Amy Wainings again, even after a month in hiding, meant she was still a threat.
Why now? Why?
Alex pondered what had changed. There was one thing: Sera Ots. After hearing about Sera Ots from Amy Wainings, and Alex starting to investigate her, things escalated.

Since Amy Wainings's body showed no trace of ever having been administered Perrin, and she wasn't involved in the experiment, that kind of cover-up wasn't likely. Was there some information she herself didn't know? What if it was related to Sera Ots, who worked for the pharmaceutical company?
"Alex, are you listening? I got in touch with the driver who picked up Amy Wainings. He said she got off near Whitechapel ten minutes ago."

Alex scanned the road. The car was just about to pass Lambeth Bridge. Whitechapel was in the opposite direction. He had to cross the bridge and loop back around. He could get there faster than Matthew, who would have to start from Paddington. Hearing the location Whitechapel, something came to mind. The Royal Hospital was there. Where Nathan worked.
"She's trying to go to the hospital. Because there's someone she can rely on there."
The moment he uttered 'someone to rely on,' his heart ached.
"She's going to the hospital to see Nathan. Since I'm closer, I'll go there first. Let's meet there."
"Got it. I'll request a support vehicle to the area immediately. I'll get there fast too."
"We have to catch him today."
"Be careful, Alex. Seriously."
"See you soon. You be careful too."

He drove faster than usual. Thanks to the cars yielding, Alex entered the hospital area around 20 minutes, earlier than the average 30 minutes it usually took. The uniformed patrol officers who had been patrolling nearby were already gathered.
Running to the reception, Alex showed Amy's photo and asked first.
"Have you seen this woman?"
"No."
"Please take another look. If you happen to see her, please call this number immediately."

After showing his badge and handing over his business card, Alex gave orders to the constables. After sending them Amy's photo and the suspect's composite sketch, he told them to search every nook and cranny around the hospital. He had one member of the tech team check the hospital's security cameras just in case. Returning to the reception, Alex asked one more thing.
"Is Mr. Nathan White in today?"
"No, he's off until today."
Coming to the crowded hospital was the right call. If she intentionally chose a crowded place, she wouldn't have needed to hide further within the hospital. So Amy didn't come here.

If she changed her destination to here without heading straight home, it was likely Amy had also realized she was being followed. If she chose this place even after hearing her mother had passed away, it was clear. But she didn't show up at the hospital.
Then it was one of two things. Either she was caught on the way, or she changed her destination midway.

The possibility that Amy had been caught couldn't be ignored either. If the suspect in the suit chasing Amy was the one who had done that to the victims, something serious might have happened by now. And if by any chance Amy was on the run, there was a chance she went to Shoreditch Highline, where Nathan's house was.
Telling them to radio him if any new information came in, Alex got back in the car. The local police station would contact him immediately if Amy appeared.

The escape attempt, despite her mother's situation, suggested Amy trusted someone she depended on more than the police. Moreover, Nathan had a record of saving Amy. Alex decided to follow his intuition.

The distance from Whitechapel to Shoreditch was less than a 20-minute walk. Having one backup vehicle follow him, Alex got out of the car when narrow alleys where vehicle entry was difficult began to appear. Although the area itself had become relatively quiet since the Beta Tester incident, Shoreditch, with Brick Lane nearby, had a moderate bustle of people. It would be hard to carry out business right away in such a place.

"John, Leonard, you each spread out to Buxton Street and Humberry Street respectively. If it seems dangerous, request support immediately, and don't follow recklessly. I'll go up toward Cheshire Street."
"Yes."

After giving orders to the constables who followed him, Alex started running. Within the police department, Alex was the best at running. He could cut the time by about half compared to others. Although his dress shoes slowed him down a little.

Moving his long legs in big strides, Alex gradually increased his speed. He showed Amy's photo to every person he encountered. Among them, luckily, he met three university students who thought they might have seen a back view similar to Amy's. They said they remembered because it was strange, someone dressed as if they'd rushed out, running anxiously.
*Please, please, be alive.*

Sweat soaked his back in an instant. Like in his soccer days, he ran at full speed. Alleys flashed by, swish, whoosh, appearing and disappearing beside him repeatedly. People looked at him running at an absurd speed, surprised, and made way for him.
The moment he entered Chiltern Street, not far from Nathan's house, Alex heard a scream. *Kyaaaak,* the high-pitched tone was familiar.
"Get away!"

He pushed off the wall to change direction. The sound was just one block behind. He turned the corner. There was no one in the sparsely populated residential area. There, a woman with her hair pulled high was being grabbed, and a man with a physique that overwhelmingly overpowered her.

It was a man in a suit with a face almost identical to the composite sketch. He was much bigger than he appeared on the grainy screen. His height was similar to Alex's, but his body was very thick. That type of physique was often more threatening than a muscular one.
"Police, stop!"

When he shouted loudly, the man turned his head toward Alex. A menacingly contorted face was visible. Using that brief moment, Amy struggled. Then she raised her knee and slammed it hard upward into the man's groin.
"Fuck!"
A low curse was heard as the man released her hair. *Kyak,* screaming, Amy started running toward Alex's direction.

Despite what must have been a painful blow, the man regained his senses within seconds. He immediately chased after the running Amy. It seemed he thought, since his face was completely exposed, he should finish it here. The man pulled a knife from his waist. The blade, which looked like a military knife, was sharpened menacingly.

For a very brief moment, Alex made a judgment. There was no time to take out the Taser, assemble the cartridge, and aim the probes. The distance between Amy and the suspect was too close. There was no guarantee he could hit the suspect with the single-use probes in this fleeting moment either.

Having reached a conclusion, Alex stomped on the ground. The man's running speed was far superior to Amy's. Just before she could reach him, her long, flowing hair was about to be caught in the man's hand.
Alex ran toward the man as if leaping, pushing off the ground. Putting his full weight into it, like when he used to win tackles, he shoved the man hard with his shoulder.
A heavy impact hit his shoulder, and then the two of them fell to the ground. They tumbled once. Even during the ensuing struggle, the man didn't let go of the knife. His strength was tremendous.

chapters.title: Chapter 98
paragraphs: Judging by his movements and the tools he wielded, he was likely a former soldier. If Alex had faltered even slightly, he would undoubtedly have been overpowered, leaving no opportunity to draw his Taser gun. After tumbling over several times, they landed hard on the road.

Alex, now on top, brought his elbow down hard on the man's wrist. With a grunt of pain, the man dropped the knife. It clattered away across the ground. From behind, Amy's sobbing voice could be heard. Alex continued to press down on the man's wrist and shouted at Amy.
"Amy, run! The place you were trying to reach is nearby, isn't it? Go now and call the police immediately!"
"B-b-but!.."
"Staying here won't help!"

Shouting fiercely, Amy nodded her head, tears streaming down her face. Wiping her tears with trembling hands, she began to run around them. Even though most people would have frozen in fear, she assessed the situation quickly enough.
"You're way too fucking relaxed!"

The man didn't miss the opening while Alex was talking to Amy. In that very brief moment of loosened strength, he pushed Alex away. Alex's head slammed against the cement floor, and his neck was gripped. *Gasp*, he couldn't breathe. Blood rushed to his face, increasing the pressure. Raising his arm, Alex pushed the man's face. The moment the choking force intensified, he pressed his thumb hard against the man's eye socket.
"Agh!"

With a pained groan, the man momentarily recoiled. The hand choking his neck loosened. Oxygen rushed violently into his lungs, triggering a cough. Coughing, he pushed against the ground with his legs to get away from the man. The palms of his hands, braced against the ground, were already scraped raw and covered in abrasions.
"Backup has already been deployed around here. You can't escape."

As Alex whispered with a strained voice, the man opened one narrowed eye. A vicious smile appeared at the corner of his mouth. Seeing that sent a chill down his spine. Alex's gaze and the man's gaze simultaneously moved toward the military knife that had fallen right beside them. Damn it! Widening his eyes, Alex reached for the knife.

But the man was a bit faster. He pinned Alex down with his body and grabbed the knife. *Scrape*, the sound of metal scraping against stone echoed, and the man's fist slammed into Alex's face. The back of his head hit the ground hard.

He felt blood bursting inside his nose. A stinging shock surged up, followed by a metallic taste. Instinctively, he raised his hand and grabbed the man's arm. The knife blade aiming for his nape was slowly descending. He strained to hold him back, but his strength was gradually being pushed aside. The blade, meant for his heart, stabbed Alex right then.
When he barely managed to push the arm past to his abdomen, his strength gave out. It was because the stab-proof vest worn on duty didn't cover that area.
*Thud.*

With a faint sound, cold steel split his flesh. He felt a sensation of being stabbed from below. Alex looked down. The blade wasn't visible. Only the large hand violently forcing the knife in came into view.

The knife was embedded in his lower abdomen, an area the stab-proof vest didn't cover. In that moment, he felt nothing. Staggering, Alex grabbed the man's wrist. It was to stop him from driving the knife deeper into his stomach. He didn't know how deep the knife had gone, but moments later, his abdomen felt like it was contracting violently.
Ah, damn.

Starting from his lips, his whole body trembled violently. *Huhk*, a ragged breath was expelled. Not even a pained groan came out. Alex somehow endured the sensation of strength draining rapidly from his body. He desperately tried to recall his training, but being properly stabbed with a knife was a first for him today.
"Killing a runt like you is nothing."

The man whispered without erasing his vicious smile. Pressing his body close, he drove the knife deeper. A coppery, bloody smell could be detected from somewhere. The strength drained from the hand gripping the man's wrist. The man rose up. Gripping the knife handle, he smiled while making eye contact with Alex.
"Go well."

Inside, the blade twisted slightly. The man pulled the knife that had torn through his abdomen straight out. The fingers that had been feebly moving to block it slipped away. Alex stared at the man's face as much as possible with his eyes open.

His mind, which had been a void, slowly began to clear. No matter how fast Amy ran, the distance to Nathan's house was still within the man's catching range. Even if backup arrived, the man had time to do his deed.
*I can't let him go like this.*

That thought filled his head. Since he had pulled the knife out, proper hemostasis was impossible. By then, the man had gotten up. Wiping the blood from the blade onto Alex's clothes as he lay there, he sheathed the knife. His dress shoe *tapped* Alex's face, and then he stood by his head, looking down.
"This is more fun than just killing you."

The shoe heel pressed harder against his cheek than before. Gasping weakly, Alex lowered his hand and pressed on his stomach. Unless deployed for a special operation, he couldn't carry a gun. The only weapon he had was the Taser gun.

He couldn't tell which organ the blade had pierced. A burning pain was slowly spreading, making it difficult to judge anything beyond it being unbearably painful. Alex pulled the Taser gun from his waistband with trembling hands. The man, leaving him behind, was already moving quickly in the direction Amy had run.

Staying still like this would be the wise thing. Moving even a little would make the bleeding uncontrollable. He should stay put and perform hemostasis as he'd been taught. But if he did that, Amy might die. Protecting a citizen was his duty, and Amy... Amy, she was important to Nathan, so...

*I can't let him go.* Putting all his remaining strength into his limp legs, he stood up. A feeling that he might die right then swept over him. Alex stumbled and followed him as if about to fall. Hearing footsteps from behind, the man stopped walking and turned his body. "Well, well."

As if praising him, the man smiled and drew his knife. But before he could swing the knife, Alex collapsed forward first. He couldn't put any strength into his legs at all. Cold sweat ran down his forehead, wetting his eyes. Sitting down before the fallen Alex at his feet, the man drew his knife. Then he grabbed a fistful of his hair. His face, pale from blood loss, looked up as Alex lifted his eyelids. His strength kept failing.
"I'll kill you outright for your tenacity."

The man showed no hesitation. As his words ended, the blade moved toward his throat. As muscle strength failed, making his mouth form a strange shape, Alex shrugged his shoulders. The moment the tip of the blade was about to pierce his skin, Alex moved. Aiming just below the man's exposed ankle, he pressed the button on the Taser gun.

*Zap, zap, zap!* The sound of sparking crackled. Gripping the yellow handle marked with the number X26 tightly, Alex kept his finger on the button. *Aghh!* With a short groan, the man's body crumpled. The man trembled and twisted his body. Holding onto his ankle, Alex let out a rough breath. He vividly felt blood draining from his body. Dizziness washed over him.
Even as he felt his strength fading, Alex fumbled and crawled along the ground. A person with a robust physique had a chance of shaking off the shock.
After pulling out the handcuffs, Alex grabbed the man's wrist. Watching him twitch reflexively, Alex opened his mouth.
"You are under arrest for the attempted kidnapping of Amy Wyning. You have the right to remain silent, and..."

He could feel the blood staining his white shirt soaking through and seeping out. His body grew so cold it was shaking. As Alex felt the fallen man twitching, he let out a long sigh and cuffed the suspect's left wrist.
"Any statement you make without exercising your right to remain silent can be used as evidence against you in a court of..."
Law.
The last word was small, like a dying ember. Staggering, barely raising only his upper body, he fastened the remaining cuff onto his own wrist.

chapters.title: Chapter 99
paragraphs: There was no strength left. A chill ran through me. I slowly collapsed onto the ground. I needed to call for backup and stop the bleeding from my wound, but I no longer had the energy to even move my hand.

Just in case the man woke up in the meantime, I tased his leg once more. I could feel the muscles twitching in response. Thoughts of excessive force swirled pointlessly in my head before disappearing. What did it matter? My stomach was punctured. My whole body felt powerless. I lay down beside the man and stared blankly at the black sky. I pressed down with what little strength I could muster on the palm of my hand against my stomach. The fine raindrops that had been falling incessantly since earlier landed on my face. The thick, gushing blood soaking my fingers and flowing out felt almost warm.
There were reasons I wanted to become a detective.

I thought that if I became someone Nathan wanted to be, maybe he would like me a little more, and I thought it might help me find my father. I wanted to help people. In case Nathan ever got into trouble again, I could help him, and even if not... I wanted to help someone in a situation like me and Nathan.
But sometimes, when I descended deep into the recesses of my consciousness, I would think that perhaps there was one more hidden reason.
I never thought I was unhappy enough to die.
But I also never thought I was happy enough to live.
*I wonder if I wanted to die like this.*

Facing a moment that might be the end of my life, I wondered if the final reason I chose to be a detective was for this very moment. My eyelids grew heavy. My consciousness, like sand slipping through my fingers, slowly flowed and sank into the black darkness.
*Did you want to die, Alex?*

The voice in my head asked. I quietly watched the days of the past flitting before my blackening vision. There were definitely times I was happy. In childhood, family outings holding my father's hand, and all the trivial days of the past when I met Nathan... The small moments at the police station where Matthew made me smile...
No answer came.
My lips, which had twitched as if to say something, turned pale and cold. My eyes closed.

On the night he returned from the alumni gathering, Nathan asked his older brother, Nicholas, to look into Alex's affairs. At the time of the incident, Nicholas had wanted to say something, but since Nathan hadn't wanted to hear it, he knew nothing about the related matters. He hadn't heard much during the plea bargain process either.
But.
Knowing that his brother's husband was in a position to find out a great deal if his brother wished, Nathan asked him to find out as much as he could. About Alex, too.

Although puzzled by his younger brother's unusual request, Nicholas agreed, and the next afternoon, he delivered the results. A fairly thick dossier was delivered via his brother's secretary, quite substantial for an investigation conducted overnight.
The first thing he read was about everything connected to the photo Jessica Bundy had mentioned. The documents were meticulously organized.
Since the source of the photo, which everyone said had been deleted, wasn't Jessica, a hacker had found an old original. It was a photo of an amateur porn actor, long-forgotten and not well-known.

The face was completely different, but in the photo Jessica had, the face was obscured by shadow. The explicit pose with genitals exposed, the slender body, the blond hair—if you just glanced at it, you could believe it. It was actually completely different from Nathan's physique at the time.

Next, he checked on the three Alphas who had come to gang-rape him. One was the younger brother of an East End mafia member with multiple arrests for drug offenses, and the other two were on the soccer team.

The nexus connecting them was David Mac, the person Jessica and Kate had mentioned. An investigation revealed he had been a professional soccer player active in the First Division until a year and a half ago, but after a major ACL injury, he had quit his playing career.

Looking further, he was a guy with many dirty corners. He was overly protective of his younger brother and had a history of terrible deeds against those who crossed him since his school days. It seemed many incidents had been buried during his soccer career as well. Now, it appeared he had secured a position at a pharmaceutical company using his father's background.

Throughout reading the summary of the incident, he barely breathed. Increasing force entered his pale fingers as they turned the pages. He paused his reading at the part detailing what that bastard from the same soccer club had demanded from Alex.
*Appears to have trauma regarding Omegas.*

That added personal opinion burned into his mind. The moment Nathan read that one line, he felt a self-loathing so intense it was hard to bear. A trembling breath escaped him as he covered his mouth. Blue veins stood out on the back of his hand. The doubts he had felt while observing Jed and Alex's medical consultation at the hospital suddenly made sense.
It was true that he had never had relations.

The face looking up at me, saying it was his first time too, and the moment he accepted me, stopping so obediently at those words—those weren't things to be dismissed. I shouldn't have brushed it off with a simple "I see." I shouldn't have left Alex holding me in the bathtub either.
Enduring his Rut with medication until his body reached that state, and not meeting an Omega—it was all intertwined with me.
*All of it.*

In a state of mind bordering on madness, Nathan put the documents down for a moment and splashed cold water on his face. He dug his fingers into his skin. Going mad might have been preferable. His head felt like it would explode.

*What have I done to you, Alex?* The past wasn't the problem. What Nathan couldn't bear was the certainty within himself that the outcome wouldn't change. He had believed that, for whatever reason, their relationship couldn't be altered. If that belief had been true, Nathan shouldn't be feeling any remorse or regret now.
But what filled his chest was an endless, infinite agony. The words he had spat at the lovely face that haunted him kept swirling.

They were words he wouldn't have said if he had listened to Alex even once. There was only one reason he hadn't wanted to listen. He was foolishly afraid of loving again and getting hurt again. Even though you mustered the courage to approach me again.

Enduring the poisonously spreading self-loathing, Nathan finished reading the documents. This time, it was the section with Alex's brief personal details. It stated his mother had remarried and started a new family, and his father was missing. There was even debt.

It said that from the time he was forcibly dating Ian Mac, Alex had left home, drifted around, and after becoming a police officer, ended up living alone in his current apartment. The image of the shabby apartment, where he didn't even properly change the lightbulb in the entrance, came to mind.
Reading one more line, there was a comment.
*Presumed to be repaying debts incurred by his father to relatives.*
His fingers gripping the paper tightened.
So, Alex had no one by his side. According to Tina and Jude, after he transferred schools, Alex had deliberately distanced himself from them.

*He's not one to keep people close.* Imagining the scene of him drifting alone for a year, Nathan could no longer bear it. His chest tightened painfully, and he stood up, taking a deep breath. Clenching his teeth, he stared at the Alex in the documents. Alex wasn't smiling. He was looking ahead with an expressionless face. *Was this always your face when you weren't in front of me? Living this kind of life, did you still give me shy smiles?* The life Alex had lived, which he couldn't fathom—no, which he hadn't tried to hear and thus didn't know—kept painting itself in his mind.
*How lonely must you have been?*

The image of the face that had tearfully blurted out that he liked me came to mind. If he had said yes when I asked to date him, Nathan probably would have gone along, pretending to resent him, led by his stubbornness. But Alex didn't do that. He was never selfish, not even for a moment. Seeing me in pain, Alex forced a smile, then lowered his head and apologized again.
I kept making him apologize.
To the guy who endured alone, doing nonsensical things for me, the human named Nathan White only kept instilling guilt. Even though I wanted to treat him well. Even though I said I cherished him.

chapters.title: Chapter 100
paragraphs: Nathan was the one who had noticed Alex always looked like someone utterly alone, and he was right about that, at least. Alex had no family by his side. Without parents to lean on, Alex had stayed with people he didn't even like, all to erase that worthless photograph. He endured all of it alone, until the trauma took root. An Alpha traumatized by an Omega...
*And I didn't even see it. What did I think I knew?*
He couldn't bear it any longer. Nathan put down the document he was reading and picked up his phone. He dialed a number he had never forgotten. The dial tone rang, but no one answered.
Even though he thought it was a natural consequence of his own decision to end the relationship, Nathan, his face pale, called again and again.
*Please, please, please answer me.*

But there was no answer from Alex on the second, third, or any subsequent calls. Clutching his phone tightly with his pale hand, he agonized in silence. It felt like his mind would explode. Nathan wondered if going to find Alex was the right thing to do. Would Alex want that? Was it right for him to approach Alex?
And selfishly, Nathan was sure of it.

*I know Alex likes me. I can't be sure of the exact beginning or duration, but Alex's actions up to now were things an ordinary person could never do. Alex had protected me, even to the point of being angry that I dared to judge him.*
*So, I wanted to believe he wouldn't push me away. If he didn't push me away, I wanted to have a proper conversation.*

*What we had done until now wasn't a conversation. Nathan hadn't tried to fully listen to what Alex said. Alex had never properly said what he wanted to say. I wanted to hear, from start to finish, what he had wanted to share. I wanted to clear away the debris between us and build a new space on those ruins.*

He had forgiven Alex, yet he hadn't truly forgiven him. It was a mere one-sided pardon, not a true resolution. A relationship couldn't heal that way. Because he believed that, he convinced himself the relationship was doomed.

The conclusion was reached. Whatever outcome awaited, Nathan now had to go find Alex and confront him. Even if it meant giving back more than Alex had done, he wanted to be by his side. It wasn't time to stay still.
He left the living room and grabbed his coat. He hurried straight to the front door. As soon as he opened the door to leave, Nathan discovered a woman standing in front of him.
"Nathan!"
It was Amy.
Her face deathly pale, Amy threw herself into his arms. He could feel the sound of her sobbing and her cold, wet body. Her black hair was a tangled mess.
"Amy?"
"What happened?"
Amy was trembling all over. Yet, she somehow answered Nathan's question.
"I, I got a call saying my mother died, and I was tricked. *Sob, sob*, that's not the problem. Nathan, you have to go help. Detective Alex is still there, he's there."
Amy's words tumbled out, fragmented and panicked. Her voice was choked with sobs, punctuated by hiccup-like gasps. She pointed frantically to the right, gesturing wildly towards the street.
"Alex?"
Anxiety gripped his throat. The unease that had been smoldering for days tightened around his entire body. His eyes narrowing, Nathan peeled Amy off of him and spoke.
"Tell me exactly where, Amy."
"If you go out to the main road and turn onto Chiltern Street, there's a small alley around there."
"Did you call the police?"
Amy nodded. As soon as she finished speaking, sirens could be heard in the distance. Nathan bowed his head, met her eyes, and whispered.
"Lock the door and stay inside here. Call the police again and tell them to come to my house and the place you mentioned, both locations. Definitely call an ambulance too. I'm going there."
"Okay."

Making an effort to stop crying, Amy said. After smoothing her wet hair, Nathan immediately rushed out of the house. Trying to comfort himself that it probably wasn't that serious was no help. When he came to his senses, he was running like a madman. He had never run like this in his life. Barely breathing, he ran to the destination.

Entering the Chiltern Street Amy mentioned, Nathan looked for a small alley. Nothing could be heard except the quiet sound of falling rain. The rain gradually intensified. When he finally stepped into the small alley, the first thing Nathan discovered was the fishy, metallic scent lingering in the damp air.
*It can't be.*
Dazedly, that thought came first. This was a bad omen. This shouldn't be happening. The smell of blood coming from the place where Amy said Alex would be was something that shouldn't happen.

Nathan took two more steps. Two people came into view. It was dark, but he could tell at a glance. Alex was lying motionless. The moment he saw a figure collapsed beside someone else without moving a muscle, his vision went dark.
"Alex!"

Stumbling forward, he ran and knelt down. His pulse throbbed violently as if it would burst, and blood seemed to rush to his head. For a moment, he even felt like he was going insane. A sharp, ragged breath escaped. He almost vomited on the spot. The shock was too great.
"No, no, no..."

His voice cracked as he whispered. *No, no, it's okay. I have to calm down. Panicking won't help.* Not caring that his knees were scraping hard against the ground, Nathan first checked Alex's consciousness.
"Alex, come to your senses. It's me, Nathan. Okay?"
Even to his own ears, his voice sounded strange. He scanned Alex's body with his eyes to find the wound. Judging by the white shirt soaked red, it seemed to be the abdomen. His hands were shaking.

Although he hadn't chosen surgery, Nathan had rarely been nervous in any practical. But his excellent grades and calm personality were of no use now. The soaring anxiety felt like poison that would kill him. His heart began to beat madly fast.

Overcoming the brief panic that had seized him, Nathan took a deep breath. Separate from his mind being eaten away by anxiety and about to explode, his reason screamed that he had to do what needed to be done. *Ambulance, I have to call an ambulance.* Amy would have given the location by now, so the ambulance would come with the police car. Then...

With trembling hands, Nathan quickly assessed Alex's condition. Judging by the location, it was around the small intestine. If this much blood was lost, there was a high possibility of arterial damage. If the abdominal aorta was damaged, there would be intestinal perforation, and surgery would have to start immediately upon arrival. All measures had to be taken within the next 45 minutes.
*"It hurts, Alex, I know. But I'm here now, so you'll be alright."*
Muttering like a madman, he shielded Alex from the pouring rain with his body. It didn't seem like he had vomited.

To relieve tension in the injured area, he supported Alex's knees with his arm and bent them, then pulled out his phone. Meanwhile, he took off his coat and tore the lower part of his shirt roughly. It was slightly better for stopping the bleeding than clothes soaked in blood and rain. He used the coat to shield Alex's body from the rain as much as possible.

The rain-soaked screen didn't respond well to touch. Applying appropriate pressure to the abdomen, Nathan called Luther. The nearest hospital was the Royal Hospital where he worked, and as soon as the patient was transported by ambulance, all measures had to be taken in the shortest time possible. Including starting surgery.
"Nathan, good afternoon. What's the matter?"
A gentle voice answered the phone. The voice, so detached from the unbelievable hell he was witnessing, almost made Nathan break down. He wanted to scream.
"Mr. Milan, it's me. Lower abdominal stab wound patient. The patient will be transported within 20 minutes. Surgery, surgery, prep..."

His voice shaking badly, Nathan took a deep breath for a moment. Holding the phone with his shoulder, he tilted Alex's head back. Securing the airway, he checked the carotid pulse with his right hand while pressing Alex's forehead.
Putting the phone down for a moment, Nathan leaned closer. Even though it was raining, he could feel cold sweat forming on his own body.

chapters.title: Chapter 101
paragraphs: He pressed his left cheek against Alex's face, checking his breathing. Though unconscious, Alex was still breathing. His chest continued to rise and fall. *You can live, Alex. I won't let you die.*
Picking up his phone again, Nathan gritted his teeth and spoke to Luther.

"I know this isn't my jurisdiction. But we have to save him, no matter what. Tell my brother, tell Mr. Frost, get everything ready. The aorta seems to be damaged, so prepare for a blood transfusion and proceed directly to surgery. Luther, please!"

He couldn't even comprehend the words spilling from his own mouth. As if desperately denying the horrific scenarios relentlessly flooding his mind, Nathan raised his voice. Damn it, the sound came out like a sob. It made no sense. Time seemed to be accelerating with terrifying speed.
At the voice that was almost a scream, Luther immediately replied in a grave tone.
"I'll have the Frost family's medical specialists on standby immediately. Calm down, Nathan. What's the patient's blood type?"

Blood type, blood type, what was his blood type? Nathan dug through old memories. What had Alex said back then when Jude and Tina, making idle conversation, had asked about blood types? It was probably O-type. What was certain was that it wasn't a rare type.
"It's not confirmed. Prepare for a transfusion with O-type blood for now."
"Understood. You're doing well. Nathan, it'll be okay. When you arrive, I'll have them go straight to the operating room."

After removing his belt, Nathan pressed the torn piece of his shirt against the wound area. Tightening the belt around Alex's abdomen for compression to stop the bleeding, he grabbed Alex's wrist. The skin that was always warm was cold from the rain. Alex was unbelievably cold, and he was faced with uncontrollable terror.
It was a fear incomparable to any wound he had ever received from Alex. The terrifying fear of a loss so immense he'd never dared to imagine it was enough to kill Nathan right then and there.
"I'm here, so it's okay, Alex. You're not cold, are you?"
Squeezing out a voice that wouldn't come, he whispered. Alex's face, devoid of any color unlike usual, looked like a corpse. His black, soaked hair was plastered to his forehead.
"He can live."
Muttering like a madman, he shielded Alex from the pouring rain with his own body.
*He can live.*

Even in the years Nathan had lived pretending to forget Alex, cutting himself off, he had never imagined a world without Alex. When longing welled up in the gaps of time, he had often wished for Alex to be living well. Because the boy in his memory was cruel, yet he couldn't just leave him alone; his heart ached for him.

*I always wanted to make you smile, to see you like that, and I took you being by my side for granted. That's why I liked the sound of your neat footsteps following me even when I walked ahead first. Because I liked you so much, I thought, at least live well somewhere in the world. And then I'd pretend not to know anything and erase you again and again.*
In all those countless years, he had never once assumed a world without Alex.
It just didn't make sense.
Holding Alex's wrist, bending over to cover his body, Nathan whispered.
"I'm sorry, Alex. I'm sorry. I, I understand now... Please let me apologize to you..."
He absolutely had to live.
There was too much left undone. He wanted to hear every single word Alex wanted to say, and after that, he wanted to say the words he should have given back.
*That I like you too.*
No, *you.*
"Let me say, I love you..."
A long, deep sigh fell heavily.

Yes, I love you. This feeling, so tenacious, agonizing, and capable of making him not himself, couldn't be described by any other word. Saying 'like' fell far short. This long-lasting emotion, far from fading faintly, only carved itself deeper, becoming bottomless.
*I love Alex.*

The agony of finally voicing such an obvious emotion was excruciating. Endless self-loathing spread darkly. If Alex were to die like this, it wouldn't be strange if he killed those who caused it and ended his own life.
At the moment when the smoldering, blooming emotion was about to consume him, rising darkly, a siren blared loudly. With a face drained of color, Nathan turned his head.

Red and blue lights spread across the dark alley. Into the alley, which had been terribly quiet, came the clamor of radios and the footsteps of police officers. Every second felt like an eternity. *Had they arrived too late?*
But less than five minutes had passed.

Medical personnel rushed to Nathan's side. Even seeing people coming, he couldn't get up from his spot. His hand pressing on the abdomen tensed, then, at the touch of hands pulling him away, Nathan momentarily regained his senses. Letting go of Alex, Nathan staggered to his feet. His clothes had been ruined long ago.
"If you're not involved, please step back."

At the words spoken by the medical staff with serious expressions, Nathan's eyes narrowed. It was a reasonable thing to say, considering it was a crime scene, yet he felt burning hostility. It felt like Alex would die the moment he was taken away from his sight. His throat tightened unbearably, making it hard to breathe. It seemed dying would hurt less.
But he had to do what needed to be done.

"I'm a doctor from the Royal Hospital. The patient has a lower abdominal stab wound, is unconscious, but pulse and breathing are maintained. Please give me IV fluids and a line for securing access first. I'll move to the spot to establish the line."
Pulling away, the man spoke to the medical team.

At his words, the medical staff, who were about to move immediately, looked behind Nathan as if for confirmation. Turning his head, he saw a familiar face. A man with shaggy hair, glasses pushed down to his forehead—Matthew Wayne. A person he hadn't liked from the first time he saw him. With his glasses fogged from the rain,
"Do as this man says. Move him, now, hurry!"
"The Royal Hospital is the closest, so we'll go there. Surgical preparations are complete, and a blood request for emergency transfusion has already been made to the hospital."

Though looking dubious, the medical team quickly followed their instructions. Without taking his eyes off the figures carefully approaching to move Alex onto a stretcher, Nathan smelled the scent of blood permeating the damp air.
"Detective, you'll need to remove the handcuffs."

Another rescue worker, who had also checked the condition of the man beside Alex, said to Matthew Wayne. The man still didn't seem to have regained consciousness. Alex, lying on the stretcher, was sharing a pair of handcuffs with him.

Matthew Wayne pressed his lips together tightly and approached Alex. Looking at the bruised face and blood-soaked clothes, he clenched and then unclenched his fist, took out a key, and unlocked the handcuff on Alex's wrist. Then he re-cuffed the man's wrists together.
The air was heavy. After staring down at Alex's face for a few seconds, Matthew Wayne turned his body. Signaling to the waiting officers, he shouted.
"Begin securing the scene! This individual will be transported separately."
Alex was loaded into the ambulance. Nathan, watching with a pale face, turned his head. Matthew Wayne was looking at him. Nathan opened his mouth.
"I'm riding in the ambulance too. You can take my statement later."

His voice was firm, with no intention of backing down. Before getting into the ambulance, Nathan, looking down at his blood-stained hands, looked elsewhere to calm himself. He turned his gaze to the officers beginning to set up the police line. Clenching his trembling fist, he repeated internally. *Alex will live. So he can see with his own eyes what Alex has accomplished, I will save him, no matter the cost.*
"Alright."
Matthew Wayne said. Nathan looked at him with surprise. The raindrops streaming down his cheek felt lukewarm.
"The most important people are Amy Wainings and that suspect, so your statement isn't urgently needed right now. I can go to the hospital and take it there."
He opened his mouth but no sound came out. It was too much to force a sound from his tightly closed throat.
"You two aren't just ordinary acquaintances."
Matthew Wayne's words continued. At the words about not being ordinary, Nathan, turning his body toward the ambulance, asked with eyes darkened to pitch black.

chapters.title: Chapter 102
paragraphs: "Did Alex... say anything?"
"No."
Matthew shook his head. Raising his arm to sweep his hair back, he spoke calmly.
"Is there a need to say it? Anyone can see that guy likes you."
He simply couldn't respond to that.
The evidence was everywhere. His face, which would tighten and hold back hurt at every word I said, and his eyes, which would brighten and smile at the slightest kindness, were proof.
His face would flush at the slightest touch, he'd hold his breath just because our lips met, and he'd lose himself in my embrace and then cry after his Rut.
In every moment the two of them were together, Alex always showed it. Even with words that pushed him away, he'd linger around, trying to say it. How much he liked me.
For a very long time, Nathan had wanted to return the feelings of someone who loved only him.
The person he had waited for his whole life had been by his side from the start.
Nathan had simply refused to look back.

He heard it. The warm drops flowing down his cheek pooled along his jaw. The fine trembling that shook his body soon became a soundless sob, seeping hotly beneath his lips. Raising his cold, chilled hand, he covered his eyes. Tears flowed quietly beneath the palms covering his eyes.

Matthew placed a hand on his shoulder once, then let go and headed towards the police car, leaving him behind. The intensifying rain washed all the blood away. Treading on the flowing blood, Nathan quickly walked towards the ambulance with a pale, ashen face.
He had a long dream.
It was a strange world. The sky was tinged a pale purple, and cumulus clouds floated low, pink like cotton candy. Endless green grass stretched across the ground.

In the middle of the plain was a large carousel, surrounded by tall dandelions blooming white and yellow with their seeds. A single girl was riding the carousel. The girl had black hair similar to Alex's, and strangely enough, Alex immediately recognized her as Amy.

Seeing Alex, Amy waved her hand. Her face, smiling brightly, was as lovely as candy, a smile that would make anyone watching unable to resist running to her. Alex pointed a finger at himself with a puzzled look, then realized Amy wasn't looking at him. He turned around. Then, a blond boy was standing behind Alex.
"Nathan?"
Alex called Nathan. But Nathan, as if he hadn't heard, passed by with an expressionless face. Amy waved her hand even more vigorously. Nathan didn't look back. As always.

Maybe his mind had regressed as much as his body had, because in the dream, Alex thought riding the carousel would be much more fun. It would definitely be more fun than standing in a field full of dandelions and playing with me, who had no amusement rides.

Yet, resenting Nathan for leaving without even a backward glance, Alex stood helplessly, staring only at his retreating back. Of course, thinking that Amy suited Nathan better than he did, he suddenly felt wronged.
*I liked you longer.*

It didn't matter if it was childish. From the distant past, he had liked Nathan. Nathan was the only one in the world he'd ever even thought of being greedy for. He didn't mind if it was called obsession. He was happy when he was with Nathan, and he liked Nathan the most.
*Can't I be greedy for you? Is that such a bad thing?*

There were many obstacles. His Secondary Gender made him hesitate to dare to be greedy for Nathan, and the wrong choices he had made hindered them. Whenever he tried to get closer to Nathan, something always got in their way.
But Alex always did his best. Even if the methods weren't completely right, he sincerely cared for Nathan.

Contemplating this, Alex started to run. Stretching his legs long, he parted the grassy field. He stopped before Nathan, who had reached the carousel and was in front of Amy with her arms spread wide. Alex desperately grabbed Nathan's clothes.
"Stay with me."

Looking back, Alex had always let Nathan go at the most crucial moments. Even in the days when he secretly liked Nathan, he thought they wouldn't work out. Even when Nathan trusted him and approached, even when he was asked if he wanted to date, he had never dared to be shameless.
"I may not be a great person."
So, just this once, let's be honest. Let's say what we truly want.
"I like you the most in the world."
If there's a feeling this painful, sad, happy, and affectionate.
"I love you, Nathan."
Then that must be love.
"I'll do really well. I'll try harder from now on, just trust me this once."

Done. The pale face quietly looked at him. The delicately curled eyelashes blinked softly. Eyes like leaves holding the midday sun held Alex. Looking at his own face reflected in those pupils, Alex wished he could have said these words to Nathan before falling asleep, hoped...
The dream ended there. The fairy-tale world swirled and flew away like the wind, and soon the surroundings darkened.

In his unconscious state, Alex occasionally saw visions. Through flickering vision, he saw golden hair that looked like Nathan appear and disappear. He felt what seemed like a cool hand touching his forehead. He also heard a whisper of 'Alex.' An unknown, soft warmth touched his cheek. It was a tickling sensation that made him feel good without even trying.

Alex's consciousness properly returned on the third day after being transported to the hospital. Pushing open his eyelids, heavy with the effects of medication, he saw a white ceiling. The ceiling bathed in the soft, pearlescent glow of the lights was unfamiliar.

Slowly, like stagnant time flowing, memories came flooding in. Opening his eyes wide, Alex raised his upper body. Then he slowly looked down. Ugh, a heavy pain was felt in his lower abdomen. The pain mixed with a foreign sensation announced the presence of the injury.
"Stay still."

A low whisper was heard. With a sound of 'Huh?', Alex turned his head. He saw Nathan holding his wrist where no IV was inserted. A large, pale hand was covering his wrist. It was the scarred area. "...Nathan?"

Wondering if it was still a dream, Alex carefully called his name. His voice, unused for a while, came out low and cracked. Nathan didn't answer. Instead, with his other hand that wasn't holding the wrist, he pushed Alex's shoulder to make him lie down. Still unable to grasp the situation, Alex just stared at Nathan's face.

First, what came to mind was sending Amy away and wrestling with the suspect. He'd been stabbed in the abdomen, and honestly, after that, he thought he was going to die. Because he bled so much. After that, he must have lost consciousness, as no scenes came to mind. Only the dream involving Nathan remained.
Was it not a real dream?

He had told Amy to go to Nathan's house, but he'd never imagined seeing Nathan when he opened his eyes. Of course, it wasn't that he disliked it. It was just that, since the end of their last conversation hadn't been good, he felt awkward.

Their gazes tangled directly. His mind had been too scattered to notice, but upon closer look, Nathan's complexion was terribly bad. Dark fatigue was draped over his eyes, and his hair was disheveled. It might be a trick of the light, but his jawline seemed sharper than before. No, he'd definitely lost weight.
"Are you hurt somewhere?"
Forgetting that he was the one who'd been stabbed, Alex suddenly felt scared. If he wasn't sick, there was no way he'd have lost weight like that.

Nathan, who had been quietly watching his face, narrowed his eyes at the question and tightened his lips. Clenching his teeth, he stared piercingly at Alex. It was like someone confirming something. An intense gaze swept over his face, and after a short silence, Nathan opened his mouth.
"You... woke up. That's enough."

The hand that had been on his shoulder settled on the nape of his neck. The fingers gently rubbed the skin of his neck, then soon caressed his cheek. At the ticklish sensation creeping up, Alex slightly flinched. The warmth he'd felt while asleep must have felt exactly like this. It had been softer and smoother than this, but...
It was similar.

chapters.title: Chapter 103
paragraphs: Nathan held my cheek with his large hand, then stood up from the chair with a long sigh. Dozens of questions raced through my mind—what happened to the suspect? Did Amy escape? Where was Matthew?—but they faded as I watched Nathan get up. I couldn't believe what had just happened.
It felt strange. The touch, as if he were handling something precious, felt so good it gave me goosebumps.
"Can you breathe properly?"
Nathan examined Alex and then had him take deep breaths. Alex followed his instructions. His body was uncomfortable, but it wasn't a major problem. After observing this, Nathan spoke.
"I'll call the attending doctor, so stay put for a bit."
"Ah, okay."

My voice was trembling. Even after standing up, Nathan kept looking down at Alex. His hand, which had been about to leave my cheek, touched me again and stroked my face. Nathan looked at Alex for a long time with a pained expression. Alex, as if entranced, couldn't tear his eyes away from Nathan's gaze. I didn't know exactly why, but something felt different.

Was he worried about me? Probably. The fact that he was here meant he knew I'd been stabbed, right? Even when he disliked me, he helped me take the Neutralizer, so it made sense he'd be worried. Feeling apologetic, Alex avoided his gaze first. Then he said,
"Do you have to leave?"
The fingers resting on my cheek twitched and then fell away. Nathan, who had cleared his throat in a low voice, spoke.
"Sorry."

Nathan, who had let out a quiet sigh, turned his body. The hem of his white doctor's coat fluttered lightly and disappeared. Only after being left alone in the hospital room did Alex let out a tense breath.
I thought I was going to die from trembling.

Just now, the feeling was strange. Nathan had grabbed my chin or wrist a few times before, but this time it felt similar to when we met for the Neutralizer administration. Something felt overwhelming, and I sensed emotion in his caressing touch.
But I couldn't understand why. Was he that concerned about my injury?
I recalled the resolution I had made after our first counseling session. Even though my confession was rejected, I had resolved to tell him my honest feelings about the part that had hurt him.

In my life, Alex had never truly opened up to anyone about his family or his feelings. I couldn't remember ever trusting anyone, ever relying on them. Maybe, if I explained myself, Nathan's disappointment would lessen, even just a little.
And then I wanted to explain my actions, which Nathan didn't want to hear, and selfishly say what I truly wanted. I really liked you... no, I love you, and I want a chance.
And if I got rejected even after that, then I would truly have no choice but to get over my feelings. That part, I still wasn't confident about.

Just imagining being rejected twice made my heart feel heavy, unavoidable. For now, I wanted to think about something else. In a drowsy state from the painkillers, Alex looked around the room. To contact Matthew, I needed to find my clothes or phone. What I was most curious about was whether the suspect had been caught.

As I was looking around the room with a serious expression, the door opened. A doctor and nurse appeared. The doctor had the typical appearance of a United Kingdom middle-aged man with a slightly receding hairline on both sides of his forehead. Judging by his pheromones, he seemed to be an Omega. As soon as they entered, the nurse moved first. She came to Alex's side, raised the upper part of the bed, and positioned Alex in a semi-reclined posture. Like Nathan had done, she had him take deep breaths and also made him cough. My throat felt clogged.

The doctor, who had been watching this, began asking about my condition and pain level after the nurse stepped back. The doctor said the surgery went well, but since Alex hadn't fully regained consciousness, he had remained in the intensive care unit.
"You were in danger. If you hadn't received treatment quickly, it could have been serious."
"Was that so?"
Alex answered awkwardly.

"If the aorta had been cut a little deeper, even surgery would have been difficult. Fortunately, the emergency treatment and surgical preparations were done quickly, so you passed the critical point safely."
"Thank you."
The doctor wrote something on the chart and adjusted the painkiller dosage. Then he said he would prescribe a mucolytic agent.
"When can I be discharged?"

"We'll need to check your urine output and monitor your vital signs for a few days. If there are no issues on the chest and abdominal X-rays, we'll proceed with discharge then. Even after discharge, you'll need to manage yourself well. You'll have to disinfect the wound and change the dressing yourself until it heals."
"Then when can I return to the field?"
The doctor made a horrified face and then spoke firmly.
"You need to rest for at least two months. For a full recovery, we usually expect six months. If you move before it's fully healed, the wound site could rupture. Do you want that?"
Alex closed his mouth with an awkward smile. The doctor checked a few more things, told him to rest, and left the room. The door didn't close. As if taking the doctor's place, Matthew entered.
"Alex!"

At the shout, the nurse opened the door again and glared at him. When she said that no one except medical staff was allowed in the ICU, Matthew pleaded that he would only be a few seconds. Alex smiled at her as if to say it was okay and greeted Matthew.
"Hi, Matthew."
Matthew strode over as if angry. This guy, he who had made the sound lightly touched Alex's shoulder.
"You, I swear!.."
His voice was choked with emotion.
"I thought you were going to die, you idiot."
Letting out a sigh of relief, he plopped down into a chair and examined Alex's complexion. After scrutinizing his face meticulously, Matthew took off his glasses and rubbed his face dry.
"I have work to do, but I was worried sick about you. It was hell."
"You look like you've been through a lot."
He didn't look as bad as Nathan, but Matthew's complexion wasn't great either.
"The guy who got stabbed is the most carefree, huh?"
"It's the medication. Was the suspect caught? What about Wynings?"
When he immediately got to the point, Matthew frowned.
"He's caught and alive. But before that, let me say one thing."
"Say it."
Matthew took a deep breath and grabbed Alex's hand. Huh, I thought, and looked down at my hand.
"I'm sorry I didn't tell you about your father right away. Of all times, with that incident and you getting hurt, damn, I felt terrible."

Matthew confessed with a guilty look. Alex quietly watched him for a moment, then awkwardly patted his hand and spoke. Whether it was the painkillers or not, moving his body was difficult, so his movements were sluggish.
"I said it was okay back then. But, I'm sorry too."
"For what?"
"For not relying on you as much as you worry about me. You're a good partner and a friend, but on the day I found out about my father, I felt completely stuck and alone."
Talking a lot right after waking up took a little energy. Sleepiness was also creeping back in.
"Thank you."
So Alex offered a short but sincere word. Matthew quietly looked at him for a moment, then haha, laughed.
"Yeah."
"Mm."
As they exchanged brief replies, the hospital room door opened. It was Nathan. Both their gazes turned there simultaneously. Matthew, hey, said as he leaned forward.
"While you were unconscious, that doctor..."
"What's going on here?"
Nathan walked over with large strides and stood beside Alex. Nathan looked at Alex and Matthew's overlapping hands, then spoke coldly. His voice was much sharper than usual.
"He still needs a lot of rest, so visiting can happen later. He also needs to be moved to a different room."
"It hasn't even been a few minutes, you're being excessive."

Matthew grumbled but listened to him. Even as he got up, he slowly let go of his hand, and Nathan watched the whole time with a hardened expression, staring at Matthew. Hahaha! Matthew laughed. He said he was leaving and exited the room. As soon as Matthew left, Nathan's expression softened slightly, and then he approached Alex.
"Get some rest."

Just like when I first woke up, Nathan's hand gently swept across my forehead. Even though his body temperature was cool, it felt incredibly good. Alex stared intently at Nathan's face. It was amazing that I still liked Nathan this much even though he had rejected me. I just liked him so very much.

chapters.title: Chapter 104
paragraphs: But since he had no way of knowing what Nathan was thinking, Alex decided to just enjoy this kindness until his body got a little better. Even if it was pity, it was fine. It was that sweet.
"Yeah."
"Starting the day after tomorrow, we'll begin administering water or simple recovery nutrition. Get some more rest now."

He obediently said he understood. Even after saying that, Nathan didn't leave his spot. The drowsiness, which had been faint and wavering, began to surge in with surprising intensity as soon as he heard Nathan's words. As he slowly began to close his eyes, his body soon grew heavy. He wanted Nathan to stay by his side, and just before he completely fell asleep, he might have unconsciously grabbed the hem of Nathan's clothes.

When Alex had fully regained consciousness, he was moved from the ICU to a private room. It was incomparable to the private room where he'd first seen Amy Wainings. Everything, from the vase to the television, looked expensive, and the window was large and elegantly shaped. There was even a sofa.
It was clear that a subsidy wouldn't cover a room like this. When Alex asked if he couldn't be moved to a multi-bed ward, Nathan simply said there was no need to worry about it.

For three days after that, Matthew visited the room whenever he had time. Each time he came, his arms were full of flower baskets or gifts, so a corner of the unnecessarily spacious room became piled high with stuff. Some were sent by team members, and there was also an expensive-looking box sent by Inspector Janice. Besides that, many people from other departments had sent a lot. For Alex, it was a bewildering experience.
"Hey, that White guy, when exactly is he going to leave your side? Doesn't he have work?"
Nathan, who had been looking at Matthew with an annoyed expression, had left the room upon hearing it was work-related talk. Alex thought seriously about Matthew's question.
"I don't think he is."

At least, he wasn't while Alex was awake. The entire time Alex was bedridden, Nathan was in his room. Looking at his clothes, it seemed like he did work, but he spent all his other time with Alex. Alex noticed that he wasn't sleeping. Even if he did, it must have been for absurdly short periods.

Moreover, Nathan helped Alex with everything he needed right beside him. During embarrassing moments—like when he needed a caregiver's help to wash up even a little or measure his urine output—he would leave at Alex's desperate request, but everything else was done by Nathan. Even simple exercises like walking in the corridor started as soon as he was moved to the room, and Nathan watched over him then too.
He even spoon-fed him!

At first, Alex refused out of embarrassment, but Nathan was so firm that Alex had no choice but to surrender. His heart pounded every mealtime, feeling like these actions were better suited for lovers. He somehow managed to eat, but even after several days, he still hadn't adjusted to this behavior.

Even the food was delicious. The menu changed slightly each day, and even though it was simple nutritious food like porridge, it was incredibly good. Alex, who was starting to fear the hospital bill, asked if this amount was covered by support, and Matthew naturally said no. When the astonished Alex asked him to check the private room fee, he came back looking stunned. Instead of telling him the amount, he just said Nathan had taken care of it.
"Well, I guess that's possible if you're dating."
Matthew added.
"Who's dating?"
Alex asked, genuinely curious. Matthew frowned.
"What?"
The question was answered with another question. Alex couldn't understand Matthew's reaction.
"Why?"
"Haven't you two talked about it?"
"About what?"
"About how that guy was a mess the day you got hurt."
Being a mess. It was a scene impossible to imagine. When Alex remained silent, Matthew made a slight correction.

"Okay, not exactly crying... more like a total wreck. He just sat there while you were in surgery, couldn't do a thing. He was like that for over a day, so his family had to come. Seriously, is that family made up of only gorgeous guys? I heard two of them are like, actual nobles or something. Standing next to them made me feel so inferior."
Matthew seemed to be reminiscing about that day.
"Nathan did that?"
Unable to believe it, Alex opened his eyes wide and asked. Matthew looked at him as if to ask how he didn't even know that.
"It was him who gave you first aid at the scene and waited, wasn't it?"

It seemed Nathan had come to the scene after Amy arrived safely at Nathan's house. Alex responded, a little dazed by this unexpected revelation. A flutter started in his stomach. The more he thought about Nathan not leaving his side while he was in surgery, the more intense that flutter became.
"I didn't know. He didn't tell me."
"That seems like him. Anyway, you should talk about it soon."

Matthew changed the subject. Since Alex hadn't even been discharged yet, he naturally couldn't participate in the investigation, so Matthew, as the representative, visited daily to share updates on the investigation.

Yesterday, Anna, along with Sergeant Hayden and Inspector Janice, had visited. Anna looked like she was about to cry from the moment she entered, and later she actually started crying. It was quite amusing to see Sergeant Hayden flustered as he comforted her. For Sergeant Hayden, it was truly kind behavior. Matthew had whispered that his partner was amazing.
"Amy Wainings can't come to the hospital because she has to stay with the protection team, but she says she really wants to meet and apologize once you're discharged."
"Ahaha."

Alex laughed, picturing Amy's bold expression. Then he soon heard about the apprehended suspect. His name was Dwayne Carter, and as suspected, he was a former marine mercenary. He had no criminal record, but it seemed the things he had done were not normal; they just hadn't been recorded.
"Did you find out the reason for the attempted kidnapping?"
"Dwayne Carter isn't talking, but Patrick Shore is singing on his own."
Alex waited for his words with interest. Matthew continued.

"Looks like he was sort of a hostage too. Before you caught Dwayne Carter, Anna found Patrick Shore first, and when he heard he'd been caught, he expressed through his lawyer his willingness to negotiate for a lighter sentence."
Patrick Shore was the one who had made the threatening calls back then, and it seemed Anna, who was dispatched, had successfully found him in the vicinity.
"He was very afraid Dwayne Carter would kill him."
"That's a convincing reason."
Alex nodded. However, Matthew looked uncertain.

"But it seems Dwayne Carter is the one who knows the important stuff. Patrick Shore doesn't know exactly who gave the orders. He said he only heard the voices of other associates over the phone. He doesn't remember the name, but it was a man, and he said the voice was similar to some football player, so it stuck in his memory. He gave us information that there's something to get from Wainings. From what I've heard briefly, it seems Dwayne Carter was looking for some material."

At the mention of a football player, Alex flinched. It must have been his subconscious reacting, because it made him think of David Mac. He hadn't wanted to look for news, so he hadn't even heard his name since parting ways with Ian. He only knew he had made a splendid debut.
But the idea that a mere athlete was involved in something like this was absurd. Although David Mac's personality itself was creepy.
Recalling unpleasant memories dampened his mood. Alex returned to the conversation.
"Is it evidence related to the clinical trial? But Amy Wainings knows nothing at all."
"That's why we're trying to get her to think as much as possible. The situation isn't very good."

Matthew said that and then picked up the remote from the bedside table. He turned on the television. A building bearing the name of MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company came into view, and then the screen showed footage of police entering for a search warrant, being broadcast repeatedly.

"We somehow managed to get a warrant from a magistrate and went in for a search and seizure first, but the press caught on. Even though we tried to keep it secret, the case is big so they're quick. The situation is that criticism is pouring in on the CEO even before the circumstances are clarified, and there's talk internally too."
"Hmm."
Alex remembered what he had thought when Amy was nearly kidnapped again.
"What if the point they targeted Wainings again coincides with when we started digging into Sera Ots?"
Matthew looked at him for a moment, then soon spoke with a serious expression.
"You mean Sera Ots left something with Amy Wainings? Something even she doesn't know about?"

chapters.title: Chapter 105
paragraphs: "Let's find out in detail how close the two of them are, and things like that. There might be a reason he recommended him to the company."
"That sounds possible."
Matthew got up from his seat. He seemed to be in a hurry.
"I'm going. See, you're good at this."

Feeling awkward at the praise, Alex scrunched his eyes and smiled. Matthew, who had patted Alex on the shoulder, quickly left the hospital room. Alex looked at the empty seat where Matthew had been and the gifts crowding the room. He realized the loneliness that usually weighed on him felt lighter than usual.

So, I still had many problems. I still had no money, and the possibility of my father returning had vanished. When I'm discharged, this reality will be waiting for me. Not much will have changed, I guess. But my heart felt a little better.

Matthew was by my side, and there were many colleagues who unexpectedly worried about me. Alex had always thought he needed absolute love. The kind of love given by a being who would always be on my side and never leave me, like a normal mother or father. He believed he wouldn't be lonely only if he had that. Of course, even now, he wanted that kind of love.

But what he realized was that even if it wasn't necessarily that grand love, perhaps he'd feel less lonely if he leaned a little on the precious people around him who cared about him. Otherwise, he wouldn't be able to endure it.

While continuing his complicated thoughts, Nathan returned. The door opened without even the sound of a doorknob turning. It was Nathan's unique way of opening doors. Just by staying together for a few days, I had gotten used to such small actions. The reason I hadn't felt lonely all this time must have been because Nathan had been by my side the whole time.
"How are you feeling?"
Even though he'd only been away for about 30 minutes, Nathan asked that.
"I think I'm okay."
"Cold?"
"No."

Nathan walked over to the bed and, out of habit, gently touched Alex's forehead and brushed his hair aside. Even after experiencing it many times, I still tensed up whenever Nathan touched me. At the same time, Matthew's words came to mind. About how we were dating.

Objectively thinking, there was no reason for Nathan to do this for me, no matter how worried he was about me. Moreover, Nathan had rejected my confession. In such a situation, why would he do this much for me? Out of pity? Probably. My heart grew heavy thinking it was out of sympathy.
Alex looked into Nathan's eyes with a face that had lost its energy. Nathan, who had been looking at him for a moment, opened his mouth.
"Then I'll open the window for a bit."
"Yeah, okay."

Nathan walked over to the large window. Sunlight shining through the glass filled the room at a slant. It was a rare sunny day in winter London. Come to think of it, Christmas was coming soon. Quite some time had passed. It was almost two months since I met Nathan again, and many things had happened in that time.

Nathan, who had opened the window slightly, came back to his side. Alex could see his usual expressionless face. Matthew's words about Nathan crying came to mind. Alex superimposed the image of crying onto Nathan's indifferent face. But his imagination failed him. He just regretted missing a side of Nathan he'd never seen, especially if Nathan had really cried because of him...
"Nathan."

Without having sorted out what to say, Alex quietly called his name. Yet, Nathan looked straight at Alex's face with deep eyes, as if he had sensed something. A cold breeze subtly mixed into the quiet hospital room. The wind coming through the window crack mingled with the warm indoor air and tickled Alex's cheek coolly. It smelled of winter. Mixed with the scent of parched tree bark.
"I have something to ask you."
Nathan slowly perched on the edge of his bed. An expression surfaced on his pale face. It was unmistakable pain.
"What is it?"

With his pale lips moving slightly, Nathan lowered his gaze. His gaze passed over Alex's injured abdomen and headed towards his neatly placed wrist beside him. The left wrist with the scar. His fine eyelashes fluttered, and he asked in a tightly closed voice, "What's the scar on your wrist, Alex?"
Nathan's words didn't end. As if trying to continue speaking, he opened his mouth and let out a trembling breath. After steadying his breathing for a few seconds, Nathan asked.
"Did you try to die?"
Those words, that question, overlapped exactly with the situation of lying stabbed. Lying alone on the rainy ground, he thought he had been waiting for this moment for a long time.

Alex lowered his head and looked at his wrist that Nathan was looking at. He had often met people who gave him uneasy glances when they saw the scar whenever his wrist was exposed. Alex bitterly ruminated on whether he looked that precarious. Still, he was enduring, but it seemed he had unintentionally caused worry.
"This is from an injury at the scene. As you know, London has a lot of accidents involving weapons."
He had never directly decided to die. He didn't even consider his life tragic enough to decide on suicide.

However, he couldn't say he had an attachment to life. Returning to the empty, vacant house, eating alone in that place devoid of any warmth, Alex would sometimes ask himself when this pain would end.
He asked himself.
Did he want to die?
"I did sometimes think about whether I wanted to die."
Even with his eyes closed, Alex couldn't give a definitive answer. He had no strong desire to live. He had no regrets.
"Maybe because I'm not a fun person, life wasn't enjoyable."
But.

But, there was regret. He regretted a life lived without ever saying what he wanted, unable to rely on anyone. He had no memories of enjoying himself. He started soccer because his father wanted it, and he tried hard to satisfy his father. He couldn't do what he wanted to do, or say what he wanted to say. Because he was afraid. Of being abandoned. Even though the person who would abandon him had already abandoned him and left.
That held him back.

Alex ended his words there. Even though it was his own feelings, putting them into words was difficult. Only a shapeless, stifling feeling filled his chest. He slowly lifted his gaze from his wrist. He wanted to see Nathan's face. What Alex saw when he raised his head was Nathan, biting his lip with reddened eyes.
He looked tormented.

He was hurting, regretting, suffering. With bloodshot eyes, he couldn't take his eyes off Alex. It even felt like this space, where not even the sound of breathing could be heard, was being filled with his sorrow.
I was a fool for wanting to see him crying. Just seeing Nathan cry hurt Alex. Nathan was silent for a long time before opening his mouth. His voice trembled terribly.
"I've been thinking wrong all this time."
The question, 'about what?' didn't leave his lips. He felt like he knew what it was even without saying it.

"I declared our relationship wouldn't change without even trying to understand. I arbitrarily judged your feelings for me. Because I didn't want to get hurt again, I tried to dismiss everything you did for me as meaningless."
Nathan's hand carefully touched Alex's hand. The fingers touching the back of his hand were trembling minutely. Nathan's voice gradually choked up, and along with it...
"I loved you, just as you were."
Alex's eyes were also gradually reddening. He felt like he should say something, but no sound came out. His Adam's apple trembled and his mouth closed.
"I should have tried to understand why you had to act that way, not just dwell on why you hurt me."

His eyes hurt. In an instant, moisture welled up in his reddened eyes. Something hot and overwhelming tightly filled his chest, making his ribs ache. Flinching his hand, Alex just looked blankly at Nathan, not knowing what to do.
"I'm sorry, Alex."
The tears that had welled up to the limit finally fell with a plop. Biting his lip hard, Alex tried to steady his breath that was scattering messily.
"I'm sorry for not trying to hear what you wanted to say."
But he absolutely couldn't do it.

chapters.title: Chapter 106
paragraphs: "I'm sorry for acting as if I had forgiven you, without even giving you the chance."

With each of Nathan's words that followed, sorrow welled up, and Alex could no longer hold back his tears. They flowed uncontrollably. He rubbed his flushed cheek with the hand that wasn't being held. Gasping breaths escaped painfully through his lips.
"I'm sorry for leaving you alone."
Nathan, his hand gently holding Alex's, tightened his grip and reached out his other hand to wipe Alex's eyes. As he tenderly brushed away the unstoppable tears, he whispered.
Nathan's voice, as he spoke, was also trembling now.
"Thank you for trying to protect me."
