As if finally releasing long-pent-up emotions, Alex crumbled at those words of gratitude. His face completely flushed, he wept silently, unable to make a sound. It felt as though Nathan was touching his very heart. The words, which seemed to truly understand his wounded and torn insides, filled him with both joy and sorrow.
*In truth, I was never okay.*

*I hated myself for hurting Nathan, and I hated myself for making only wrong choices. Yet, sometimes, very rarely, I felt hurt by Nathan, who seemed to accept me while stubbornly refusing to hear my excuses.*
*You said you liked me. You said you'd forgive me even if I made mistakes. You said you'd grant me one wish. So, can't you just listen to me once?*
Even though I longed to make unreasonable demands, I held back. After all, I was the one who started everything.
But the moment I heard that single word of thanks, everything that had been hurting me melted away. It felt as though Nathan had acknowledged my heart that tried to protect him.
It truly felt like I was forgiven.
"Do you... understand... everything now?"
Alex asked, his voice a mess. Nathan, strengthening his grip on Alex's hand, replied.
"I understand everything."

He nodded. Alex wanted to ask how, or where Nathan had found out, but he realized it wasn't important. He wanted to stop dwelling on the past. For the past nine years, he had been so bound to the past that he felt like he was going crazy.
"From now on, I will listen to you, Alex. I'll listen to everything you want to say..."
With the hand that had been wiping away tears, Nathan cupped Alex's cheek. Moisture could be seen gathering in his distorted green eyes.
"Say what you want to say."
Choking up, Alex took a deep breath and nodded. His voice trembled violently. Thoughts of embarrassment about crying or needing to appear cool had no chance to intrude.
"I liked you from the moment I first saw you."
Alex brought out the words he had been accumulating for a very long time, one by one.
"What I said about briefly liking you before was also a lie. I've never stopped liking you. I don't know why, Nathan, but I really do like you... even though you pushed me away."
Nathan listened to his words while biting his lip. His insides gradually felt more relieved.
"You said you wouldn't change. I don't think that way. I believe people can change. I think they can change more for someone they care about. So..."
*I'll do well, I'll change a lot.*
*Such sentences were jumbled up in his head. I'll trust you. I'll get counseling and all that, I won't make such mistakes again, me...*
"Do you... still... like me?.."

Pushing aside the many jumbled sentences, Alex brought out the one question he most wanted to ask. He had wanted to ask all along. Even while thinking it was a delusion, he held onto that thought. *Maybe, Nathan might still like me.* Yet, he couldn't bring himself to say it out loud.

After spitting out the feelings that had been tied up inside for so long, he felt a sense of relief. Trembling but somehow not feeling anxious, Alex waited for Nathan's answer. It was different from the anxiety he had felt before.
"No."

Nathan said quietly. At the answer of denial, Alex opened his eyes wide and looked at Nathan. The moment tears that had been held back seemed to gather again hazily, Nathan pulled him in with strength in the hand cupping his cheek. Their faces drew close. He could see the incredibly beautiful eyelashes trembling, and the green eyes that seemed cold but were actually very warm staring only at him.
"I love you."

It was a wondrous thing. Alex was learning for the first time now that a single word could melt a person's heart in an instant. The joy young Alex Yeon felt upon hearing 'I like you,' or perhaps an even greater joy, enveloped his body like a tremor.
"Very, much."
He could see the affectionately curved eyebrows. The delicate, thin lips whispered words that were so beautiful that Alex smiled slightly, his eyes still tearful.

The distance was so close their noses could touch. Nathan was just looking at me quietly across that small gap. Then, for the first time, he felt certain about how to move. In his life, neither short nor long, this was the first moment he could be confident in his actions.

Alex leaned his upper body forward. He drew closer to Nathan, who was waiting for him. It smelled good. The faint scent of cold air seeping in, Nathan's scent that seemed dry and parched but upon closer sniff was incredibly fresh.

Slowly, he pressed his lips against Nathan's. Shyly, he rubbed his slightly dry lips. As if he had been waiting, Nathan pulled him in. He could feel his cheek being firmly held, as if grasping something he couldn't let go. Feeling Nathan's tongue gently probing his lips, Alex closed his eyes.
*Thinking that it seemed he had so much more to say,* Alex laughed inwardly.
*Today, just this is enough.*

Discharge happened three days later. The doctor said his recovery was remarkably excellent, adding his personal opinion that having a sturdy body was fortunate. He said that if Alex managed well to prevent the wound from worsening, he could move little by little like before in two months. He added that exercises which put strain on his abdomen would only be possible after another three months on top of that.
However, the doctor emphasized that until then, he absolutely must rest. Intimidated by the firm tone that sounded almost threatening, Alex repeated his agreement three times.

Nathan remained by his side, just as he had been for nearly ten days in the hospital. Even now, as they prepared for discharge, it was the same. Sneaking glances at Nathan packing his things for him while sitting on the bed, Alex wondered once again if this was reality. It was a thought that had persisted over the past three days.
Actually, he still wondered if maybe Nathan was looking after him out of pity. It was because it didn't feel real.

After receiving an unbelievable confession, initiating a kiss first, and embarrassingly crying even more, Alex fell asleep. It seemed his body was tired after expending so much emotional energy, as his strength hadn't fully returned yet. Beside him as he grew drowsy, Nathan kissed his forehead and watched over him as he fell asleep.
And even the next day after waking up, Nathan was by his side. Really, it was unbelievable!

Although he had resolved to slowly start trusting those around him from now on, Alex was someone accustomed to misfortune. Whenever something good happened, he always feared something bad would follow. In reality, misfortune did follow good fortune. While wondering if this was repayment for suffering a major injury, he tried hard to think differently, fearing that such an assumption itself might be underestimating Nathan's feelings.

His head believed it, but since his heart couldn't quite catch up yet, Alex still couldn't believe that Nathan loved him. Having been rejected and having seen Nathan suffer, it was more accurate to say it didn't feel real. Perhaps because of that, Alex realized only now that he had only confessed to liking Nathan, not to loving him.
Glancing sideways, their eyes met. Nathan was looking at him. Just their gazes intertwining, yet his face instantly flushed hot. Quickly lowering his eyes, Alex opened his mouth.
"Why, why?"
Nathan walked towards him without a word. Sitting on the bed in patient clothes, Alex held his breath watching the shoes approaching him. As he avoided looking, his chin was caught.
"You should change clothes."
Nathan said expressionlessly. As his chin was lifted, naturally making him look at Nathan's face, his earlobes grew even redder.
"Ah, right."
"Wear this."

chapters.title: Chapter 107
paragraphs: Nathan placed the large shopping bag from beside the bed onto it. Alex obediently took out the clothes. They were new, from a brand unfamiliar to him, but even someone as clueless about fashion as Alex could tell the material was exceptionally high quality. He looked up, flustered.
"These aren't my clothes?.."
"They're your size."
How did he know my size? With a bewildered expression, Alex spoke again.
"But they're new."
"I couldn't bring your clothes, so I bought them."
"I see. Then how much do I owe you?"

Nathan scrunched one eye, then turned Alex's face this way and that before speaking. His finger gently stroked and then moved away from Alex's cheekbone, which had been bruised from being hit by Dwayne Carter.
"You don't need to know. It's a gift."
Nathan was always particularly sensitive about his injuries, so Alex tensed slightly when Nathan touched the bruise. Watching his reaction carefully, Alex timidly insisted.
"But still..."
"Call it a discharge gift."
After saying that, Nathan closed his mouth. Alex could see his complexion worsening even more. Because Alex was always on high alert when it came to Nathan, he quickly asked.
"Are you okay?"

Leaning his upper body slightly forward, Nathan met his eye level. Staring straight into his eyes, Nathan spoke quietly. A faint look of weariness and distress appeared on his face. After sweeping his gaze over Alex's body once, he sighed and spoke.
"The moment I saw you hurt, I was..."
His fingers gripping Alex's chin tightened.
"...almost a mad person. Thinking that you might be in serious trouble... I couldn't do anything."
The adult Nathan had always seemed like a solid person who didn't need Alex's protection at all. Unlike Alex, who had been lost and wandering without direction, Nathan seemed unshakable.

But the Nathan before his eyes now was telling him about the vulnerable feelings hidden beneath his cool, expressionless face. Alex's chest tickled and his lower abdomen felt pleasantly warm. His feelings were strange.
"I couldn't do anything. Until you opened your eyes. So, Alex, don't get hurt."
Perhaps it was a reaction to the long years he had endured by force of will, but the corners of his eyes stung. Alex nodded with reddened eyes.
"Okay. I won't get hurt."
"I hate that you're a detective. The profession itself where you could get hurt."

Nathan spoke in a subdued voice. It was difficult to respond to those words. Alex fully understood Nathan's feelings. Conversely, if Nathan were a detective, Alex would have been worried the entire time he couldn't see him. When he was young, he just thought it was cool, but now that it was his own profession, he realized that wasn't the way to think.
"But you're a good detective. Like my father. I respect what you've accomplished."
Alex, who had been pondering how to lessen his worries, paused at that remark. Nathan straightened his back. He seemed to have reached a conclusion.
"So, it'll always be dangerous... but promise me you'll be careful."
Steadying his surging emotions, Alex spoke with sincerity.
"I'll definitely be careful."

Both the praise and the worry were firsts. Even when he got injured playing soccer, these were words he had never heard from his own father. He hadn't heard them from his mother either. The expression on Nathan's face as he looked at Alex, gently stroking him on the day Alex ran to him with his forehead split open, was exactly like now. Though now was more serious.
Listening to such admonitions, it really felt like they were in a relationship. Their faces were also excessively close.
*Wait, are we dating?* Alex thought with a serious expression. Meanwhile, Nathan, who had straightened up, released his chin. Then he spoke.
"I couldn't understand why my mother was afraid of me becoming a police officer before... but I think I get it now."
Seeing Nathan's complicated face as he muttered words closer to a soliloquy, Alex quickly added. Grabbing Nathan's retreating collar tightly, he spoke.
"I really won't get hurt, Nathan. So don't worry."

When Alex spoke with a resolute expression, Nathan's expression softened. A smile gradually formed on his face as he looked at Alex with his eyes still scrunched. Watching his delicate lips soften gently, Alex blinked. It felt like an eternity since he had seen him smile like that. It was that precious of a smile.
*We're really moving forward.*
Suddenly, that thought came to him.

When Alex expressed his desire to stop by the police station to briefly check on the investigation details and current situation, Nathan sighed and said he'd give him a ride. While thinking he should refuse because it felt like he was imposing, his heart yearned to be with Nathan.
While Alex was seriously agonizing, Nathan just grabbed his wrist and walked ahead. Alex, while flustered, obediently followed him.
In the quietly rolling car, Alex stole glances at Nathan driving. Nathan, who had been driving while looking ahead, opened his mouth.
"What?"
"Huh?"
"Do you have something to say?"
"Ah, no."
Then Alex changed his mind. There was something he hadn't been able to say.
"It's just..."
"Yeah."
Nathan waited for him. Alex spoke in a hushed voice.
"I, I, I think I couldn't say I love you."

Instantly, the car shook momentarily. The Mercedes, which had almost veered out of its lane, wobbled and returned to its place. Horns sounded aggressively from around them. Startled along with it, Alex hurriedly grabbed his seatbelt.

Nathan wasn't looking at Alex. He was holding the steering wheel tightly with his mouth closed. Just as Alex was about to ask what was wrong, he soon realized that Nathan's earlobes had turned slightly red. Upon discovering that, his own face flushed hotly as well.
Amidst the silence filled with tension, the car arrived at Scotland Yard. Around the time they showed their IDs at the entrance barrier and entered inside, Nathan broke the silence.
"Even though you've been discharged, until your wounds are fully healed, you need to do proper dressing and care. You also need to plan your meals properly. Can you do it alone?"
"Is it not possible?"
While Nathan skillfully parked the car, Alex replied in an unsure tone.
"It doesn't sound like it."
Even outside major cases, Alex's job as a detective often meant late nights and irregular meals. He could cook, but the time commitment was a problem. Nathan, having parked the car, cut to the chase.
"If you're not confident, stay at my house until you're fully recovered."
"What?"
"I'm not telling you to decide right now. Just think about it."
Nathan, who had undone his seatbelt, leaned toward him. A white hand stretched out and undid Alex's seatbelt for him.
"I'm saying this because I think I'll feel at ease if you are in front of my eyes."

Without realizing it, the distance was too close. They had just kissed the day before yesterday, and before that they had done even more, yet Alex froze, unable to even breathe. As he just stared with wide eyes, Nathan gently brushed back his hair. Then he spoke.
"And I love you too."
Without changing his expression at all, Nathan whispered in a voice that sounded somewhat dry. After nearly giving him a heart attack, Nathan acted as if nothing had happened.
"Let's go."
At the sound of the car door opening, Alex belatedly came to his senses. A sense of alarm formed like cold sweat that if he heard those words while sober one more time, he might die of sudden death.

Trying to somehow cool down his unsettled insides, Alex got out of the car. Nathan, who had already come and was standing by the passenger door, closed it for him. This kind of luxurious treatment was a first in his life.

Perhaps intending to see him inside before leaving, Nathan headed toward headquarters with Alex. Due to frequently coming and going recently because of the institute's work, Nathan also had a temporary visitor pass, so it wasn't a problem. As soon as they entered the lobby, Alex found Matthew, who had been waiting for him. There was one more person beside him.
"Detective Yeon!"

It was Amy Wainings. Perhaps she had suffered equally, she also seemed to have lost a lot of weight in the past few days. Amy, dressed in comfortable clothes, had her hair tied up high as before. Her face was always bold and lovely whenever he saw her.

chapters.title: Chapter 108
paragraphs: The moment she saw Alex, Amy ran over, grabbed his hand with a tearful face, and offered her apology.
"I'm so sorry you got hurt because of me. I couldn't move freely, so I couldn't come see you, but I kept praying. I'm sorry, Detective."
Matthew, who had walked over slowly, stood beside them. Amy continued in a voice full of guilt.

"When I heard my mother had passed away, I couldn't bear to wait for confirmation, so I did something crazy in the moment. I'd also been locked up for so long that I felt rebellious. But after getting on the train, I started to come to my senses a little. It was strange that a friend of mine delivered that kind of news.
After I got off at the station and was trying to go back, I noticed the man you showed me in the photo was following me. From then on..."
Amy took a deep breath and bowed deeply.
"I've apologized to the others too, but you, Detective, were especially in mortal danger because of me. Thank you for saving me. And I'm sorry."
It was a sincere apology. Alex grabbed Amy's arm and shook his head.
"I just did my job. Besides, you listened to me well, Ms. Wainings, so the situation didn't get more complicated. The bad ones are the people who tried to harm Ms. Wainings."
"Thank you for saying that."
Even after that, Amy apologized two more times, then this time she turned her body towards Nathan. A blush of a different meaning bloomed on her face, which had been full of tears.
"Nathan, do you have a moment?"
It was clear what she wanted to say, even without her saying it. Dread filled my stomach. She'd asked me to help her confess, so now that she was face-to-face with Nathan, she'd definitely try to.
*The matter.*
Alex hesitated, creating a little distance between himself and Nathan. At the same time, Matthew and Nathan both looked intently at Alex. Amy seemed puzzled, glancing between them.
"Oh, well, we'll be upstairs then. It's dangerous, so please don't go outside."

Alex gave the best answer he could. It was a matter between Nathan and Amy, and it was bound to happen sooner or later, regardless of time. It seemed right to vacate the spot quickly. They were so close, and she'd known Nathan throughout his twenties, a part of his life I'd missed. She knew him far longer than I did... It was unsettling, but there was nothing I could do.

After saying that and grabbing Matthew, Nathan's expression became frightening. At a glance, it seemed expressionless, but looking closely, you could see his eyes had hardened coldly. Was it because I was about to leave without saying goodbye?
"Have a good talk!"

So Alex waved at Nathan. Beside him, Matthew coughed as if something had caught in his throat. Nathan's expression didn't improve; on the contrary, it became even more terrifying, so Alex patted Matthew's back and just headed for the elevator. He didn't look back, afraid he might feel lingering regret.
"Hey, is it okay to leave them alone? No, never mind. Are you feeling a bit better? Everyone was waiting for you to be discharged."
Matthew whispered as he tapped his access card on the elevator.
"I can walk around."
Alex answered flatly about his condition, then belatedly questioned Matthew's first remark.
"Why wouldn't it be okay to leave them alone?"
"You're in love with each other, aren't you? You don't like Amy?"
Still not understanding the correlation, Alex blushed and averted his gaze.
"Y-yes, I like him."
Matthew made an uncomfortable expression, then coughed. The elevator doors opened.
"It's obvious Wainings is going to confess, I was asking if it's okay to just leave her to it."
"That's... something I can't do anything about."
Alex made a dejected face. Matthew let out a bewildered chuckle. It was incomprehensible. Meanwhile, they arrived on the 4th floor. Exiting the elevator, they walked down the corridor.
"Anyway, Alex, I'm glad you're back safe and sound."
Saying that, Matthew opened the door to the investigation unit.
"Welcome back, Alex!"
Anna's voice rang out first, followed by the sound of people clapping. With eyes wide open in surprise, Alex stopped. Matthew grabbed his shoulder and laughed.
"Everyone was really worried."
Sergeant Hayden came over with an awkward face, holding a small cake. On the square rectangular fresh cream cake, 'Congratulations on your discharge' was written.
"The case is still ongoing, so we can't celebrate too grandly... but well done, Alex. We almost ended up with more victims and letting the suspect get away."
Faced with the unexpected hospitality, Alex froze. He should say 'thank you,' but the words wouldn't leave his lips.

I became a detective almost by accident. It wasn't something I ever thought I'd enjoy. Surprisingly, I found I was good at it, and I was managing fine, but I never thought I was particularly outstanding.
Alex carefully looked around at the people surrounding him. He saw smiling faces. People he had suffered and rejoiced with for years.
"What are you doing frozen like that? Come on over and cut the cake."
Inspector Janice gestured and tapped the folding table. The cake was moved to a desk laden with muffins, sandwiches, coffee, juice, and the like.

Sergeant Hayden carried the cake to the center of the table. Looking at the words written in unappetizing green cream, Alex finally gave a small smile. He took the plastic knife and cut the cake cleanly in half.
"We're going easy on you because you're still a patient, Senior! From now on, you absolutely have to take Senior Matthew with you!"

Anna, saying that throwing cake in someone's face was the tradition, helped him cut the cake beside him. Cutting the cake into pieces for other team members besides his own team, a minute quickly passed. He stabbed a large forkful of the cake on the disposable tray. Pushing it into his mouth, it melted smoothly and, unlike its appearance, tasted good. The sponge was soft, and the cream wasn't greasy.
*I'm glad I became a police officer.*
Biting into the cake, Alex thought that. Perhaps, if he had become a soccer player, Alex wouldn't have felt this kind of joy or satisfaction.

After the brief celebration party, the department became busy with work again. Alex sat in the meeting room and received a proper investigation briefing. Sergeant Hayden explained the progress. He was on his third raisin muffin.

"First off, Patrick Shore is a splendid traitor. Contrary to what he did, he's quite cowardly. Dwayne Carter took care of all the abductions and murders, but as a possible insurance policy, he remembered where he conducted his work. He often had him bring necessary supplies nearby. Seems he mainly did odd jobs."
"He'll be a model prisoner."
Alex quickly jotted down the details he had missed. Anna chimed in with a laugh.

"It was really funny at the arrest scene. We didn't even grab him that hard, but he was overly dramatic. 'My arm's broken!' or something. Anyway, maybe he has some conscience, he spilled everything, saying he almost went crazy seeing the case blow up. Apparently, he didn't have that image at the language exchange meetups."
"Sales jobs are similar to acting."
Inspector Janice added.
"So, did a lot of evidence come out?"
The most important thing was evidence. Matthew answered Alex's question.

"We're combing through the abandoned factory and the surrounding area that Patrick Shore mentioned. Testimony alone isn't enough to link him to five murders. He's a skilled guy. We've been told there aren't many traces left at the scene either, just like the lack of evidence on the bodies."
Sergeant Hayden interjected.
"But Patrick Shore provided purchase records for the tools he used to mutilate the bodies, so it's not the worst-case scenario."
There was a lot to catch up on. After diligently recording the details, Alex asked what he was curious about.
"So, the remaining issue is MacMilan Pharmaceutical. How did the lab search and seizure go?"
Sergeant Hayden answered in a cynical voice.

"Identical Perrin was found at the research institute. Exactly the same as what was injected into the victims. Documents showing approval for clinical trials were also discovered, and the CEO, Edel MacMilan, denies knowing anything about it... well."

Matthew handed Alex a list they had compiled of the company's key executives and researchers. It was a thick list with photos, names, and brief career summaries. While Alex scanned the list, an exchange of opinions took place in the meeting room.
"So, do you really believe the CEO ordered it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 109
paragraphs: Sergeant Hayden answered Anna's question.
"There's responsibility in not knowing that something this big could happen even from behind the scenes. It's negligence in supervision and management."
"That's true, but. It hasn't made the news yet, but I hear there's internal strife happening recently."
Alex, flipping through the list, found the name Cameron Mac among the shareholders. It was a name unfamiliar to him, yet it nagged at him.
The man's face bore a resemblance to David Mac.

Frowning, Alex stared intently at the middle-aged man's face. According to the records, he was 58 years old and owned a highly successful company in the life sciences field. Muttering the surname Mac, Alex finally understood why it was bothering him.

From his time at the club, he had heard countless stories about David Mac's family being wealthy. He'd also frequently heard that he had connections with the club owner. David Mac himself was a talented striker, but jealous colleagues always added that his background probably played a significant role.

It felt too significant to be a mere coincidence, so Alex took the paper with Cameron Mac's personal details. This was truly intuition. Because the David Mac he had encountered, even at the tender age of seventeen, had shown no guilt whatsoever in manipulating people. Something felt amiss.
Moreover, Patrick Shore's testimony, relayed by Matthew, also unsettled him. If the voice resembled a football player, then perhaps really...

"If there's no evidence to overturn what came from the research institute, CEO Ethel MacMillan and the current chairman will bear the responsibility. So let's investigate thoroughly. The repercussions of corporate-led human experimentation will be immense."

Inspector Janice concluded the briefing. Before leaving, she informed Alex that while she understood the situation was unavoidable, he should stick with Matthew from now on and forbade him from field duties for a while.
Because of that, Matthew also ended up working at headquarters as much as possible. Consequently, two more detectives, who had just concluded other cases, were mobilized to the team.

After finishing the progress report meeting and coming out, Amy was there. Alex felt a sense of guilt for some reason and couldn't easily approach her as she sat in the chair. Unlike before, her face looked deflated, and her eyes were red. She had clearly been crying.
Had she confessed?
It seemed so, as Matthew had suggested. And the result was, most likely, rejection. Looking at her round face, which showed no signs of joy, Alex felt conflicting emotions: guilt and relief.

Even after hearing Nathan say he loved him twice, building confidence was a completely different hurdle. Moreover, Alex had too little experience trusting someone, so such trust wasn't formed instantly. Thus, unconsciously, he seemed to have assumed Nathan would accept Amy's confession.

As if waiting for something, she, who had been sitting in Alex's chair, raised her head, spotted Alex, and abruptly stood up. Amy, biting her lips hard, walked over quickly and suddenly extended her hand. Alex, flustered, quickly clasped her hand.
"Amy?"
"First, I apologize again, Detective. I didn't know you liked Nathan and made an impudent request."

Taken aback by the abrupt statement, Alex was instead surprised. He hurriedly scanned his surroundings and pulled Amy along. Holding her hand tightly, she followed meekly. After seating her in Matthew's chair, Alex asked,
"What happened?"
Amy said, her gaze intense.
"I confessed to Nathan, but I was rejected. He said he loves you, Detective."

Alex was once again flustered by the incredibly concise summary. The moment he heard the word 'love', he coughed. Amy made a sniffing sound, as if tears were welling up again, and wiped her eyes with her sleeve. He wanted to offer her a handkerchief or something, but he didn't carry such items. Amy stopped Alex, who was searching for tissues.
"I'm okay. Nathan rejected me so decisively that I'm disillusioned now, so I'll get over it quickly."
"Did Nathan not comfort you?"

Alex knew that Nathan had a reputation for being indifferent to his surroundings and, even when he was aware, for being emotionally reserved and cold. Having never dated anyone else, he didn't know for sure, but Nathan probably wouldn't be lauded as a warm person. However, at least in Alex's memory, Nathan often smiled at him and, at the same time, always comforted him when he cried.
"Yes. After saying sorry once, he told me to tell you he's leaving. Wow, he just left like that. That jerk."

Amy conveyed the situation in a clear, indignant voice. Sniffling a few more times, Amy let out a long sigh and stretched her body. Staring at Alex with reddened eyes, she shook the hand she was holding.

"What I wanted to say, Detective, is please look after Nathan. I mean, I'm still his friend, after all. I know this is presumptuous of me, but since I've loved him for so long, I wanted to say this: if it's someone as amazing as you, Detective, I can accept stepping aside... even though he rejected me."
Amy laughed through her tears. Alex silently held Amy's hand tightly.

"Anyway, the reason I came back up is because I remembered something I wanted to tell you before going to the safe house. I think I know why I became a target. After being pressured for days, something finally occurred to me."
After holding Alex's hand tightly, Amy let go and wiped her hand. Having gathered her emotions, she fixed her tied-up hair and opened her mouth.
"The day I went for the interview, Sera unnie asked me a favor."
With those words, Amy pulled out a lipstick from her pants pocket. In front of Alex, who was looking at her with puzzled eyes, Amy opened the lipstick.
"This is it."
*Click.*
As the lid opened, it was like the final piece of the puzzle snapping into place. In Amy's hand was a lipstick-shaped flash drive.
*Tsk.*

"As you can see, it's shaped like a lipstick, so I put it in my bag and forgot about it for quite a while. I met unnie at a cafe the day before the interview. Before we parted, unnie said she had something urgent and left, but she left this lipstick on the table. Then she texted asking if I could give her the lipstick she left behind at the company before my interview tomorrow. So I did. I didn't feel anything strange. Since it was unnie's, I didn't even think to open it."

The flash drive Amy gave was password-protected. Matthew rushed to where the tech team was to decrypt it. Anna suggested Sarah Ots might be one of the two unidentified corpses and went with Sergeant Hayden to pull the records of all researchers who had passed through MacMillan Pharmaceutical, stating they should have checked this sooner.

Their objective was to collect DNA samples from researchers who had been out of contact for a long time or had no family within two days and send them to the forensic science institute. A large number of personnel were deployed to assist them.

"We met briefly in the restroom and I handed the lipstick to unnie. Then unnie said she'd give me a company tour after the interview, so let's meet again briefly. Of course, I accepted, since it was a place I might work. So I had the interview, we met, had coffee at the company cafe, and then parted. The interview result was a pass, but I'd already decided I wanted to research Secondary Genders, so I declined anyway as it didn't seem like MacMillan was involved. Now I know they're involved, but MacMillan was known to be unrelated to Secondary Gender research. When I told her the result, unnie said I did well. That was a bit strange. As if she knew I would decline. Then she said she'd be busy for a while, so let's meet later."

The data Dwayne Carter had mentioned was most likely this. Anything was possible: recordings, research details, locations of documents, anything. If that were the case, Sarah Ots's possibility of being dead was also high, rather than having gone to Germany for training.

"But when I got home and changed bags a few days later, I found this lipstick inside. Unnie must have secretly put it in, I guess. I was curious and tried contacting her, but there was no reply. Unnie often goes completely off the grid, like going into seclusion, when she's busy or immersed in research, so I thought it was strange but soon forgot. The lipstick too. Then, a few days ago, it suddenly occurred to me. I opened it and it was a flash drive."

chapters.title: Chapter 110
paragraphs: After finishing her testimony, Amy asked Alex one last question.
"Will my senior be okay? She was such a good senior... I feel pathetic for only remembering this now, not even realizing she was caught up in something so dangerous."

Instead of resenting Sera Otsu for putting him in danger, Amy was blaming herself. Hearing the self-loathing in her voice, Alex couldn't help but hesitate, feeling it was no longer someone else's problem. To comfort Amy, he himself had lived for so long resenting his own victimhood. Hesitating, he gathered his thoughts piece by piece and opened his mouth.
"Don't think like that. Amy was already in enough danger and survived. That alone is enough."
Alex spoke words he had always told countless others but had never once said to himself.
Words filled with unspoken feelings.

"The guilt lies with the person who tried to hurt us. Don't think that we were stupid or made the wrong choices for getting caught up in such a bad thing. Because when people are in a desperate situation, they can't be perfectly rational."
You didn't do anything wrong, Amy. No one in this world is perfect. Saying that, Alex thought maybe, somehow, he could forgive himself a little too.

Since the immediate, direct danger was gone, Amy would stay in a safe house within London for the progress of the case. Only a few insiders knew the location, and more protection was added. Handing Amy over, Alex came out of the office with the materials on Cameron Mac. If the evidence was on the flash drive, the mastermind would be revealed anyway, but he still wanted to investigate thoroughly.

What he'd intended as a quick stop had turned into hours. The moment he stepped into the lobby, his tension eased. It was just a few hours of meetings, but it was true that it had taken a toll; he was already tired. The moment he thought he needed to change the gauze, disinfect, and eat properly, Alex felt the loneliness he had momentarily forgotten. Then, he started to miss Nathan. The words he'd said about staying at his place until he fully recovered came to mind.
"Alex."
As Alex was crossing the lobby to the exit, he stopped at the sound of his name with a 'Huh?'. It was Nathan's voice.
"Nathan?"
Nathan was leaning against the wall of the lobby, then walked towards him. At the unexpected meeting, the corners of his mouth lifted unbidden. He hadn't even realized it.
"Finished?"
"What are you doing here? I mean... Did you go and come back?"
He'd seen him earlier, but he looked handsome anew. He was wearing a thick, long grey coat and looked like a model.
"Yeah. Finished?"
"Yeah, finished."
"Let's go."

Nathan held out his hand. Alex's eyes widened as he looked at the offered hand, then, hesitating, he grabbed it tightly. It was as if the tiredness was a lie; he even felt a sudden surge of energy. He felt strong in an instant. It felt so good.

Nathan's hand was colder than usual, perhaps from being outside for quite a while. To warm it, Alex moved his fingers and rubbed the back of his hand. As they walked out of the police station towards the parking lot, Nathan spoke.
"Nothing to say to me?"
Alex thought carefully. Come to think of it, something had been bothering him since he was in the hospital. In fact, he'd been quite worried.
"Is it okay for you not to work, Nathan? You've been by my side for over a week..."

Nathan, who had stopped squarely in front of the car, looked down at him with a frown. Alex watched him carefully. After staring at Alex for a long while, Nathan pressed his index finger firmly between his eyebrows and spoke.
"I've told the hospital. I'll reduce my hours until next week."
"Is that really okay?.."
"Even if I get fired, I can get a job somewhere else, so don't worry."
Nathan really looked like he wasn't worried. That put Alex at ease.
"You don't like me being next to you?"
The question came back to him. Alex, startled, answered loudly.
"No!"
At that, Nathan's face softened a little.
"Good, I get that. Then why did you just let me go with Amy?"

The thing Alex should have asked about was probably this. Asking what was between Amy and Nathan, that sort of thing. Alex turned his head slightly with an uncertain look. Keeping his gaze on his feet, he spoke quietly.
"You two are close. And you said she's important to you, and it's not like I should interfere... I knew Mr. Wainings liked you. So I thought it'd be good if you resolved it well..."
"You knew?"
Nathan asked again with a serious face. In an even smaller voice, Alex said.
"A while ago, she asked me... to pass on a confession for her."

Hearing the answer, Nathan closed his mouth. As if holding something back, he closed and opened his eyes, then took out the car key, pressed the button, and opened the passenger door, gesturing for Alex to get in. Alex was about to say something, but thinking Nathan would be cold outside, he got in the car. To add, Nathan also looked quite angry.

As soon as he got in the car, Nathan started the engine, turned on the heater, and twisted his body to face him. Whether he'd calmed down in the short time or not, he looked straight at Alex and spoke quietly. His tone was calm, as if persuading him.
"Amy is a good friend, but not as precious as you. And you can interfere in my business as much as you want. We're dating."
The word 'dating' hit Alex like a jolt. It was what he'd been secretly hoping for, but dared not believe. Nathan and I are dating? Since when? It felt like a dream, too good to be true.
"We're dating?"
Nathan, who had seemed to regain his composure, hardened his mouth again at those words. Raising one hand to rub his face, he spoke clearly.
"I love you."
Hearing the words 'I love you,' his nape heated up reflexively. Shyly, Alex quickly responded to those words.
"I, I love you too, really."
At that, Nathan's expression softened a little. The tension between his brows loosened, and Nathan explained, like a teacher trying to let a student realize the answer for themselves.
"Right. So what kind of relationship are we in?"
Oh, so we're dating!..

Alex finally got the answer to the problem he'd been secretly worrying about in the hospital. Because of the memory of being rejected, he hadn't been able to ask on his own, but Nathan had brought it up first. Nathan spoke again.
"I want to date you. What about you, Alex?"

At those words, Alex remembered his seventeen-year-old self. The self who had wasted two days without saying anything right away on the day he received a confession. This time, he didn't want to do that. He couldn't create a romantic scene for Nathan like in movies or dramas, but giving this answer was more urgent.
"I want to."
In a desperate voice, Alex whispered.
"I want to do that."

chapters.title: Chapter 111
paragraphs: The words Alex probably should have said were likely something like asking what was going on between Amy and Nathan, or something along those lines. Alex turned his head slightly, his expression uncertain. Keeping his gaze on the floor, he spoke softly.

"You two are close. Besides, you said she's important to you, and it's not really my place to get involved... I knew Ms. Wainings liked you, so I thought it would be best if you two sorted things out..."
"You knew?"
Nathan asked again, his face serious. Alex's voice grew even smaller.
"A while ago... she asked me to... pass on her confession to you."

Upon hearing the answer, Nathan fell silent. He closed his eyes as if holding something back, then opened them, took out his car keys, pressed a button, and gestured for Alex to get in by opening the passenger door. Alex started to say something, but then, thinking Nathan would get cold standing outside, he got into the car. Besides, Nathan looked pretty angry.

As soon as he got into the car, Nathan started the engine and turned on the heater, then twisted his body to face Alex. Having perhaps calmed down in that short time, he looked directly at Alex and spoke quietly. His tone was calm, as if trying to persuade him.
"Amy is a good friend, but she's not as precious as you. And you can interfere in my affairs as much as you want. We're dating."

At the word 'dating,' Alex froze. The thought he'd barely dared to entertain, the possibility he'd dismissed as too presumptuous, had just been spoken aloud by Nathan. Dating Nathan? *Since when?* It felt unreal, like grasping at impossible luck.
"We're dating?"
Nathan, who had seemed to regain his composure, hardened his expression again at those words. He raised a hand to rub his face and spoke clearly.
"I love you."
Upon hearing the words 'I love you,' Alex's nape reflexively flushed. Feeling shy but also eager, Alex quickly responded.
"I, I really love you too."
At those words, Nathan's expression softened slightly. His furrowed brow relaxed, and Nathan explained, like a teacher trying to guide a student to the answer.
"Right. Then what kind of relationship do we have?"
*Ah, so we're dating!*

Alex finally got an answer to the problem he had been secretly agonizing over since the hospital. Because of the memory of being rejected, he hadn't been able to bring himself to ask, but Nathan had mentioned it first. Nathan spoke again.
"I want to date you. What about you, Alex?"

At those words, Alex recalled his seventeen-year-old self. The self who, on the day he received a confession, didn't say anything right away and wasted two days. This time, he didn't want to do that. He couldn't create a romantic situation for Nathan like in movies or dramas, but giving this answer felt more urgent.
"I want to."
In an earnest voice, Alex whispered.
"I'd like that."

But not now. As soon as he opened his eyes, Alex remembered the ghost-like image of Nathan he had seen, Matthew suppressing overwhelming emotions, and the people in the department who had been worried about him.

In the world, there must surely be an overflow of people loved by many, people who naturally receive love from their families. Judging by numbers alone, the people who truly love Alex might be pitifully few. But for Alex, this much was enough. Lately, he'd started to believe this was enough to keep him going. Love was addictive, and he'd quickly grown used to Nathan's devotion – guarding his side, barely sleeping since he'd woken. Even though Nathan wasn't a man of many words, remembering his quiet, watchful gaze brought a surge of loneliness.

Love. He had kept loneliness as his companion for far too long and had become easily vulnerable to solitude. Alex, who had always endured that feeling alone, hesitated and finally picked up his phone. Then he looked for Nathan's number. He hadn't saved it, but he knew what the number was.

Looking at the call list displaying only the number, Alex slowly moved his finger and entered the contacts. Staring at the blank space above the entered number, he pondered for a long time. Then he typed four letters.
Nate
A smile crept up. Looking at the four letters as if gazing at something precious, Alex pressed the message button. Then he sent a text to Nathan.

Even though Nathan wasn't right beside him at that moment, after sending those words, the loneliness eased considerably. In his memory, Nathan was slow to reply. He thought Nathan would be tired and asleep, but a reply came quickly.
"I miss you."
"Go to sleep quickly. So you can get better."
At Nathan's typically laconic reply, Alex smiled. He was just about to put his phone down when another text arrived.
"I'll pick you up tomorrow morning. I miss you too."

Reading that short sentence, his mood felt truly strange. The fact that there was someone to love in his daily life, it just, suddenly hit him. He felt loved and loving. As the counselor had said, it was something felt with the heart rather than the head.

Alex opened the shopping bag Nathan had brought. Inside were packaged nutritional meals with time markers attached. They didn't seem store-bought, but it was hard to believe Nathan had made them. Nathan was the antithesis of cooking.
Alex chewed and ate the savory-smelling food properly. Meanwhile, he began digging deeper into Cameron Mac. Information about his family was, of course, quickly found.
Seeing the names David Mac and Ian Mac that popped up as soon as he searched, Alex frowned. They were names he had deliberately avoided, and seeing them like this didn't feel good.

David Mac, who had been skyrocketing in value as a football player, transferred to a prestigious London club for a considerable transfer fee. However, after severely injuring his cruciate ligament in the Champions League, he retired at an early age. It was arguably right as a striker was reaching his prime, so it couldn't be seen as excessively early.

His team won the Champions League thanks to the penalty chance gained from his injury, and the phrase 'unlucky star' often appeared in articles. That was about a year and a half ago. Since then, it had been quiet. No articles could be found.

Alex began examining not only the executive list of MacMilan Pharmaceutical he had brought but also the list of operational staff beneath it. David Mac's name was listed as head of the sales department. Ian Mac was not seen.

If there was internal strife related to Edel MacMilan's corporate management, an external force holding shares in the company was clearly likely to be the problem. Looking at the situation where a former football player was placed as head of the sales department, perhaps...

While examining the corporate investigation report, Alex confirmed that Cameron Mac owned 33% of the shares as the second-largest shareholder. If the board members were divided into factions and David Mac was overstepping his authority within the company on behalf of Cameron Mac, it might be related to the internal strife, as Anna had said. Of course, this might just be a judgment colored by his own ill feelings, so Alex decided to refrain from speculation. Nevertheless, he spent several more hours investigating Cameron Mac's family before remembering Nathan's words and preparing for bed before it got any later. Before falling asleep, Alex suddenly wondered what it would be like if Nathan were by his side every night like this in his daily life. He recalled their childhood when they used to sleep together. Of course, that was nice too, but he wanted to feel the present Nathan. It would be nice if there were some kind of trace.

After staring at the 'I miss you' text for a long time, Alex opened the first drawer before getting into bed. Looking at the clearly faded Suppressant box, he took out a wristband that could no longer be worn. He held the old, worn-out, and dirty-looking band in his hand, then carefully placed it on the desk.
Then he felt at ease.

The next morning, Nathan announced his arrival earlier than promised. Looking forward to seeing Nathan, Alex had also woken up early, but he hadn't finished getting ready yet. While looking for clothes, his phone rang. Seeing the name 'Nate,' newly saved yesterday, a smile formed at the corner of his mouth.
"Nathan, hello!"
"Which floor?"
A straightforward question came through. Alex, momentarily not understanding the words, stammered his reply.
"Good morning?.."
"Good morning."
Then Nathan returned the greeting. His mood lifted. The corners of his mouth kept rising until his cheeks hurt slightly.

chapters.title: Chapter 112
paragraphs: "Yeah, sleep okay? What do you mean, 'which floor'?"
"Which floor and room number."
"Huh? Are you coming up? No! Like I said yesterday, I'm still cleaning..."
Alex desperately tried to stop Nathan. But Nathan wouldn't be dissuaded.
"Then I'll knock on every floor."
His tone convinced Alex that he would, so he quickly scanned the room. With a crestfallen face, he hurriedly tidied the bed and gave him the room number.
"It's room 807. Are you really coming up?"

The call ended. He'd coldly hung up before Alex could even try to persuade him otherwise. Nathan really was something else. With that thought, Alex hastily threw on some clothes. He put away the radiator he had scheduled to turn off that morning and cleared the dining table. Just as he was about to organize the documents, the doorbell rang.
"I'm coming out!"

Torn between cleaning more and letting Nathan in immediately, Alex naturally chose the latter. He couldn't leave Nathan outside in the cold. His abdomen ached from the sudden movement, so he walked carefully and opened the door.
"Did you rest well?"
Nathan came straight inside. Seeing Nathan first thing in the morning... His loosely swept-back platinum hair was dazzling.
"Yeah, I went to bed early like you said."
"What about a meal?"
"I ate what you gave me."
At that, Nathan's expression softened a little. He raised his hand and ruffled Alex's hair.
"Good job."

It felt strangely flattering, like being praised by a pet, but Alex dismissed it with a silent laugh. Anyway, he'd been praised. Forgetting that he hadn't wanted to show Nathan his place, he stuck close to him.
"My hands are cold, so I'll touch you in a bit."
After saying that, Nathan looked around the apartment. Since he was already inside, it felt awkward to just have him standing there, so Alex offered him tea.
"Want some black tea?"
"No, I'm fine. Is there anything I can help with?"
"No."

Nathan quickly saw through Alex's lie. Spotting the document bag placed near the desk, he walked over there. Following behind Nathan, Alex repeatedly said it was okay. Nathan didn't even pretend to listen, stopping squarely in front of the desk.
"Nathan?"

Nathan was looking not at the bag, but at the desk. Wondering what he was looking at, Alex peeked sideways and spotted the wristband he had taken out last night. He must have forgotten to put it back in the drawer.
"Ah, that's..."

Flustered, Alex quickly grabbed Nathan's hand. Was he going to think it was too creepy? Probably. It was the wristband Nathan had angrily snatched and stepped on, the one Alex had salvaged. His heart beat anxiously.
"Sorry. It's weird. I just, because I got it from you, I couldn't bring myself to throw it away..."
"You picked it up?"
His voice was strained. Nathan spoke while still looking down at the band. Afraid to see his face, Alex clenched his fist and answered.
"Yeah. Sorry."

Nathan didn't respond. He stood in the same position, staring at the band for several minutes. Just as Alex was about to find it unbearable, he turned his body. Nathan's face was filled with guilt. His eyebrows were drawn down long and his eyes were contorted.
"Come here."

Spreading his arms slightly, Nathan whispered to him. Alex quickly approached. As soon as he got close, Nathan carefully hugged Alex and buried his face in his neck. He could feel the bridge of Nathan's straight nose against his skin. And his hot breath.
"Leaving you alone like this..."
*It's driving me crazy.*
The hand holding his back crumpled his clothes. Nathan looked so sad that Alex hugged him back and spoke softly.
"I'm happy with you. I am when I'm by your side."

Nathan lifted his head. His reddened eyes were visible. Was it because of the wish I had made back in the hospital room? It pained his heart to see him cry twice, something he'd never seen in his whole life. Sincerely, Alex whispered.
"Don't cry, okay?"
"I wasn't crying."

Nathan stubbornly replied, then firmly closed his mouth and cupped Alex's cheeks. He softly pressed his lips to Alex's forehead and the bridge of his nose, and finally kissed him properly. From a distance where his pupils were clearly visible, Nathan said.
"I love you."
His cheeks flushed red in an instant. He was sure he was making a foolish face, but he couldn't look away. Still, he had to say it.
"I love you too."
*So much.*

When he unnecessarily added that, Nathan finally relaxed his expression. Letting go of his cheeks, Nathan picked up the document bag from under the desk. After kissing his forehead one more time, Nathan tightly held his hand.
"Let's go."
To that, he just nodded with a smile.

When they stepped outside, a grey wind blew chaotically. His face, under his fluttering hair, quickly grew cold. Nathan, who had parked his car at the entrance, was about to walk over but stopped and looked at Alex beside him. Alex looked at him quizzically.
Nathan unwound the grey cashmere scarf he was wearing around his neck. Then he wrapped it around Alex's neck, who was only wearing a coat. Instantly, his neck felt warm.
"I'm not cold, Nathan. You keep it, okay? You're the one who's cold."
Startled, Alex tried to take the scarf off, but Nathan went ahead and tied it properly.
"It's fine, since we're taking the car anyway."
Without even listening to the rest, Nathan turned around. When Alex saw him heading for the passenger seat this time, he cried out urgently. Every moment with Nathan was a whirlwind of emotions.
"N-Nathan, you don't have to open it for me every time..."
The door opened. Nathan gestured with his chin, his expression unchanged.
"Get in."

Since he couldn't close the already open door and open it again, Alex trudged over. It felt good to be taken care of, but nonetheless, he was a healthy Alpha. He didn't like making things hard for Nathan.
The inside of the car was warm. The air, filled with warmth, thawed his body that had grown cold. Starting the engine, Nathan spoke.
"Does the police station have no manpower? To the point of mobilizing an injured person?"

His voice sounded displeased. Even though he was discharged, Alex knew well that it was still a time for him to rest. Nevertheless, stopping by the police station for even a short while was Alex's own decision. Instead, since he couldn't overdo it, they had compromised on him going for just a few hours a day.
"But I still want to see the criminal get caught..."
When Alex spoke, gauging his reaction, Nathan closed his mouth. Making a troubled expression, he added.
"I'm not saying anything to you. It's just that if you can't rest when you need to, your recovery will slow down."
"But I really did rest well. I'll just go until lunchtime today and then come back."

He quickly added. Alex noticed that Nathan was trying to speak a little differently than before. He'd never really been hurt by Nathan's tone originally, but thinking that he was being treated specially made his heart race wildly. His fingertips tingled and felt itchy.
"Okay. I'll come pick you up then."
"Got it!"

When he replied cheerfully, Nathan chuckled. Seeing the corners of his mouth relax loosely made his body feel warm. He thought he'd built up a tolerance from seeing it so often lately, but Nathan was still ridiculously pretty. Having witnessed his smiling face, which he hadn't seen for so many years, several times just yesterday and today made it hard to calm down.

Not wanting to look any more foolish, Alex decided to do something else. At this rate, he'd just end up sitting there staring blankly at Nathan. He opened the document bag Nathan had brought for him and took out the files. He'd told himself to avoid conjecture, but Cameron Mac's actions were troubling him.
He thought he should look into the information that had come from inside the department once he arrived at headquarters. Speaking of which, what happened to the flash drive?
"Is that Cameron Mac's file?"
Nathan, who had been driving silently, spoke while looking ahead. Alex quickly turned his head.
"You know about it?"
"I know because of David Mac."

Nathan pronounced that name in a cold voice. After they had talked to each other in the hospital room, Alex hesitated for a moment about the past stories they hadn't mentioned. Even though Nathan said he understood everything, there was no good reason to bring up David Mac's story.
"Open the glove box."

When Alex hesitated, Nathan said that. Since he still hadn't figured out how to handle this kind of sensitive topic, Alex quickly followed Nathan's instruction. There were documents inside the glove box.
"They'll help you."

chapters.title: Chapter 113
paragraphs: Alex retrieved the meticulously organized documents with a dubious expression. The file contained an analysis of Cameron Mac's assets: real estate, liquid assets, everything he owned, along with personal details on David Mac and Ian Mac.

Several photographs of the house David Mac lived in were included. For Ian Mac, it was even noted that an illness he had suffered from since childhood had worsened. It appeared that abnormalities had been detected in his pheromone organs about two years ago, leading to a diagnosis of an incurable disease.
Alex closed his mouth, gazing at Ian's face, which was clearly sickly and older than he remembered.
*Could this also be one of the reasons?*
According to Amy, Sera Ots had been scouted for research related to incurable secondary gender illnesses. Of course, that wouldn't be the whole reason.

Reading the file, Cameron Mac had consistently advocated for expanding MacMilan's position within the secondary gender pharmaceutical sector. He had steadily sponsored football clubs for a long time, and there was probably no field as connected to Alphas as football. If he produced secondary gender-related drugs tied to Alphas, it would clearly align with his own interests.
Astonished by the terrifyingly neat file, Alex looked at Nathan. Sensing his gaze, Nathan spoke briefly.
"I looked into it privately for some business."
His tone was like a villain in a movie. Alex worried seriously.
"You're not planning to do anything strange, are you, Nathan?"
"Of course not."

Nathan looked at Alex with the faint smile he had shown earlier. Even though he should have been suspicious of the smile, Alex was captivated and found himself trusting Nathan implicitly. Besides, he reasoned, what could Nathan, just a civilian, really do?
To Alex, Nathan was still someone he had to protect.
Nathan handed the documents to Alex. After repeating that he would pick Alex up exactly at lunchtime and readjusting his scarf for him, he sent Alex on his way.

When Alex arrived at headquarters, the inside was bustling. Matthew looked a complete mess, as if he had spent the night there. Because of the noisy commotion, Alex couldn't even call out to him. People kept coming and going around him.

Those who belatedly noticed Alex told him evidence had been found. Alex quickly walked over to their shared desk. His stomach twinged a little. As Nathan had said, he grew a bit afraid his wound might burst. He resolved to truly rest after today.
"You're here? I was just about to call."
Matthew, who had been frantically clicking his mouse, stood up and spoke. The dark circles under his eyes were visible through his glasses.

"I cracked the flash drive password. It wasn't a program-installed password but a model with its own encryption, so it was a bit annoying, but Wainings remembered something else and sent me an email, so I solved it."
Matthew pointed at the monitor. There was an email there from a sender named Sera Young. Alex remembered that Young was Sera Ots's surname before adoption.

"The body text says she's alive and that she's sorry, and she had embedded the password in a combination within it. I guess the reason they suddenly started tracking Wainings was because of this email. Apparently, this email arrived around the time of the first attack."
"So Wainings only just checked it now?"
Alex sounded incredulous, and Matthew immediately jumped to Wainings' defense.
"It must be an email she doesn't use. It's a university email she hasn't used since her student days. She said she was thinking about Sera Ots, went in on a hunch, and the email was there."

Come to think of it, the day Alex met Nathan again in the hospital room, Nathan had also said Amy tended to be forgetful. Alex sat down and read the email from start to finish. Although it was an email with the password embedded, it contained a rather heartfelt apology.
"She nearly died because of Sera Ots, but will she be okay?"
She seemed to be, but once properly checked, feelings might change again.
"She didn't seem to mind. She said Sera Ots herself didn't keep people close. Among those she trusted, she was probably the only one in the medical field. Anyway, that's not important, Alex."
"It's all here."

With clicks that even seemed infused with a touch of madness, Matthew opened a folder. Inside were the research permits before they were forged, files recording clinical trial progress, preparation materials before the experiment started, photos, physical information of the test subjects, and audio files.
It was astonishing. There were short videos featuring the experimenters, which might be difficult to adopt as evidence. But their impact was undeniable.

"With evidence like this, it wouldn't be strange if she had died long ago. She was a smart woman. Looking at the records, the research team couldn't bring anything in or out. They underwent body searches too. That's why she used Wainings."

With those words, Matthew played an audio file. Sera Ots's voice could be heard. She argued that proceeding with trials was impossible with a drug rejected by the Institutional Review Board. Her angry voice echoed, saying much more time was needed for research. Someone cut off her words about the drug not being stabilized even in animal testing.
"To see definitive results, we ultimately have to test on people. It's a drug to be used on people, right? You said you were confident. Then there shouldn't be a problem."
It was a young man's voice. Without Matthew's explanation, Alex knew instantly who it was. His stomach sank.
"That's David Mac."
"Huh? How did you know?"
"There's a bit of a story."
Along with those words, Alex placed the documents Nathan had given him on Matthew's desk. Matthew quickly picked up the documents and scanned them voraciously.
"Whoever it is, this isn't the work of someone who's done this just once or twice."
"Right."
"It's a file you brought, why are you saying that?"
Alex shrugged. As the two were looking at the evidence, Sergeant Hayden rushed out of Inspector Janice's office. Inspector Janice followed him out, shouting with a fierce expression.
"Everyone, get up now! We've received a tip that Cameron Mac has left his residence. The travel ban review is still in progress. We must catch him!"
Matthew shot to his feet and looked down at Alex.
"You need to stay here."
"Are you serious?"
"You can't even run with that body."
Alex put on a pitiful expression. Matthew hesitated.
"I'll stay in the car. I swear. I'll be a hindrance if I tag along, so just let me stay inside. You can move with the other investigation vehicles, right?"
"No, but... that doctor gave me so much hell..."

Matthew trailed off with strange words, then ruffled his hair and grabbed the car keys and his coat. Alex picked up the document he had glanced at earlier, which recorded the location of the private jet owned by Cameron Mac. He remembered reading that he mainly used Stapleford Airfield at the edge of London. The deployment vehicles were divided among St Pancras Station (where one could catch the Eurostar), Heathrow, Gatwick, and Luton. The team already tracking Cameron Mac in the city reported that it hadn't been confirmed exactly which mode of transport he intended to use to leave the country. As Inspector Janice left to request a helicopter, Matthew and Alex also departed with the officers.
"Let's go here."
After entering Stapleford into the navigation, Matthew threatened Alex seriously.
"Don't get out of the car, no matter what. If you do, you'll have to make me lunch for three months."
"Got it."

"I'm serious. It's not because of what that doctor said, but even a little movement means a trip back to the hospital for you. I don't want to see you get hurt again. I'm still too young to lose my partner."

Matthew's voice revealed the extent of his recent hardship; pain seeped into every word. Alex swore he wouldn't get out unless Matthew was in mortal danger, a promise reinforced by the very real strain he could already feel on his body.

Alex checked the time. It had been just an hour since he parted with Nathan. He felt he had to inform Nathan, who was scheduled to pick him up in two hours, so he nervously took out his phone. He felt like he was going to get scolded.
*Nathan, evidence has surfaced. I just want to see the arrest scene. I'll stay in the car and absolutely won't move. I'll return home in Matthew's car, so don't wait for me.*

chapters.title: Chapter 114
paragraphs: Just as I was thinking he probably wouldn't read it right away, the 'Read' notification appeared. Alex held his breath, watching the speech bubble appear. A slight sweat broke out on his palms.
Okay.

Contrary to expectations, the answer was simple. Alex, feeling a pang of disappointment inwardly, relaxed his body. He didn't know why he felt this sense of regret. Still, getting permission was a relief.
"How do you know David Mac?"
It took 35 minutes to get to Stapleford even driving as fast as possible. Matthew was driving at a breakneck speed. The flashing lights only shortened the time a little.
It seemed Matthew had chosen David Mac as the conversation topic to fill the 35 minutes. Alex hesitated. He hadn't spoken about him out loud.
"We were on the same football team."
"What?!"
Matthew sped up sharply. Alex looked at him with a 'why' face.
"You played football?"
"It was a youth team. I quit before I could debut professionally."
"No wonder you were unbelievably fast. Wait, I'm just finding this out now?"
As Alex shrugged, Matthew spoke with a tone of annoyance.
"Sergeant Hayden should have used you as bait when he was recruiting for the team. He bet a Nintendo as a reward back then."
It seemed to be a story about the football team within the police department. Alex quietly tapped his knees with his fingers, then looked out the car window and said.
"David Mac is why Nathan and I broke up. David Mac wanted me to date his brother, Cameron Mac. I saw Cameron Mac's name and thought 'no way,' but it really was David Mac's father."
This was the first time he had been this honest with Matthew about this. Alex hesitated, then added one more thing.
"Do people not change, Matthew?"
Alex had told Nathan that people could change. But seeing David Mac, who hadn't changed a bit since childhood and had grown up to do even worse things, Alex couldn't be sure anymore.
"I think it depends on the person."
Matthew said, wrinkling his nose.
"People who genuinely want to change can change. Little by little. Criminals like David Mac just didn't have that will. They probably don't want to."
"Is that so."
"Look at you."
Matthew laughed.
"And here I thought I'd never see the day you'd tell me something like this."

Their eyes met briefly. Alex blinked and looked at him, then smiled faintly. After that, neither spoke. Watching the scenery flash by outside the car window, Alex wished Matthew's words were true. He didn't want to be lonely anymore.

Matthew abused his police authority a little and arrived at the airport in 30 minutes. It being lunchtime probably helped too. Following a small road that ran alongside a vast, spread-out pasture, a hidden airfield appeared. To the right of the thick woods, a hangar was visible. The support vehicles entered first. Matthew's car quietly followed behind. After showing their IDs at the checkpoint, they drove inside.
"Could that be it?"

A small plane beginning its takeoff was visible in the distance. *Damn it*, Matthew swore and drove the car in the direction the plane was heading. If Cameron Mac had the plane on standby, it was possible it had already left. If so, there was nothing they could do.

Matthew parked the car beside the control tower. After giving Alex a stern look, he told him to stay put and went inside with the officers. Not wanting to get in the way, Alex followed that instruction. But just in case, he only stepped out of the car and scanned the surroundings.
That's when he found something strange.
"No way?"

Alex discovered a familiar Mercedes parked in the lot. Even the license plate was the same. Recalling Nathan's face as he quietly said 'Yes,' Alex quickly looked around. Then, the hangar came into view. Alex picked up the radio and said to Matthew.
"Matthew, what's the situation? I think it's the hangar area. Come check it out."
He was anxious. Knowing that his limited mobility wouldn't help, Alex decided to survey the nearby area.

He tightly wrapped the scarf Nathan had given him around his neck and slowly headed toward the hangar. The individual hangars, divided into sections, weren't that large. As he got closer, Alex could hear a buzzing commotion. He picked out Nathan's voice from within.
"Where are you going alone!"
Matthew must have come down quickly, as he appeared from behind and firmly grabbed Alex's shoulder.
"I didn't go in. I was going to wait here."
"Now I see you're a good liar. You're my kitchen slave for 3 months."

With those words, Matthew took the lead. The door was open. Entering the hangar where a cold wind was swirling, they discovered an unexpected scene. Several people in suits were there. Alex spotted Nathan among them.

It wasn't just Nathan. Beside him, he spotted a man with hair color similar to Nathan's, but who looked more 'handsome' than 'pretty.' It was a face he remembered. It was the lawyer older brother Nathan adored so much. The hostility hiding in Alex's heart cautiously raised its head.
"Wow, that's one of the handsome aristocrats I saw at the hospital."

Matthew said in a truly bewildered voice, pointing. It was a black-haired man the same height as Nathan's brother, a face that exuded a sense of nobility even from a distance. He was even wearing a colder, more expressionless face than Nathan. He didn't know such a person existed. He was like a piece of ice.
And opposite them was David Mac. A relatively small number of bodyguards were surrounding David Mac and another person. Alex had a feeling he knew who that was. It was Ian.
"You stay right here and don't move."

With those words, Matthew and the officers began their entry. At the sound of 'police,' everyone's gaze turned that way. Alex only half-heard Matthew's words. He didn't enter with them, but he approached to a distance where he could see the events unfold.
"Get lost!"

Then a commotion broke out. As the police approached, the men in suits standing beside Nathan moved. They rushed not toward the police, but toward David's side, and in an instant, the inside of the hangar became a chaotic mess. Amid the scuffles, David Mac grabbed Ian Mac and turned his body toward the small plane. Matthew ran that way.
But someone moved faster than Matthew. Nathan glanced once in the direction where Alex was, then immediately blocked David's path.

Nathan easily grabbed David, who was trying to shove him aside with his body. He seized David's arm in a flash, and things happened in an instant. Nathan lifted David, who was of a similar build, slightly and slammed him onto the floor. A sickening *crack*, the unmistakable sound of bone on bone, echoed in the air.
Matthew, who had been running, halted. Ian Mac, who had been surrounded protectively by the bodyguards, screamed and ran forward.
"Brother!"

Ian was restrained by Matthew. Whether the report about him being in pain was true, he staggered and stopped even before Matthew grabbed him. Cameron Mac was nowhere to be seen. Alex reported into the radio without taking his eyes off the scene.
"This is Alex Yeon. Investigator Matthew Wayne has apprehended David Mac. Stapleford Airfield, 11:30."
A reply came. It was Anna.
"Anna Lionel here. Good work, senior! We also found Cameron Mac at Heathrow Airport. Maybe he knew he'd be caught, but he didn't resist on our end."
While the radio transmission was happening, Matthew approached David Mac to handcuff him. David, his face twisted fiercely as he tried to get up, was approached even faster by Nathan than by Matthew.

And this time, honestly, he punched him hard in the face with his fist. A solid *crack*, the unmistakable sound of bone breaking, resonated loudly in the air. Matthew looked utterly bewildered. A brief silence hung in the air. It was Nathan's brother who broke it.
"There was a disagreement while adjusting the flight schedule."
He shrugged his shoulders and smiled, then approached Matthew and handed him a business card.
"Let's discuss my brother's actions separately with me. Nicholas White."

chapters.title: Chapter 115
paragraphs: As Matthew, alternating his gaze between the unconscious David Mac and the business card, recited the Miranda rights, he accepted the card. The black-haired nobleman, who had been observing, added a comment.
"You've trained your son poorly, Nicholas."
"Carlyle, must you make such a remark in this situation?"
Nicholas grimaced at the man called Carlyle and complained. Instead of replying, Carlyle issued orders to the men in suits before speaking to Matthew.
"My apologies for the trouble. We will proceed to the station and wait, so please take your time."

Delivering his message in a cold, aristocratic tone, the man walked towards Alex with measured steps. He was an Alpha, yet his pheromones were almost imperceptible. Their eyes met briefly, icy gray eyes sweeping over Alex for a moment. However, he exited the hangar first, his face betraying no emotion.

Next were David Mac and Ian Mac. The officers supporting the collapsed David Mac passed by Alex. His neatly styled blond hair was disheveled, falling across his forehead. Alex, who had been quietly observing the face that had changed little since childhood, shifted his gaze forward. Ian was looking at him.
*He probably has nothing to do with this,* Alex thought. *It's clear that David or his father proceeded unilaterally, just as Alex had experienced.*
Eyes as green as Nathan's, yet in reality bearing no resemblance to Nathan's, looked up at him. Ian, who had been staring at Alex with a pale face, moved his lips slightly before bowing his head.

Then, matching Matthew's pace, he quietly passed by Alex. Alex offered no words to him either. He simply tasted bitterness in his mouth. The entity that had once caused him such trauma no longer occupied a significant space in his mind. That was right.
After everyone else had departed, Nicholas and Nathan approached him. Nicholas stood before Alex, a rueful smile gracing his lips as he spoke.
"Hello, Alex. Still as cute as ever."

Alex regarded him with a suspicious expression. Nicholas, whom he had met only once before, had boasted of his profession as a lawyer and had taken Nathan away from him. It had hardly been a pleasant first encounter. Following his initial animosity, a faint sense of wariness began to surface. Still, as Nathan's brother, he had to acknowledge him.
"Hello."
Just as Nicholas was about to continue, Nathan interjected. From beside Alex, Nathan addressed Nicholas.
"Stop with the pointless chatter and let's go, Brother."
Knowing that Nathan had deeply admired his brother in their youth, Alex looked at him with surprise. Alex had even harbored envy towards Nicholas.
"Nathan, you were quite adorable back then, too..."
Nicholas let out a sigh and told Alex they would meet again later. With Nicholas also gone, only the two of them remained in the hangar.
"Are you injured anywhere?"
Nathan spoke first, his gaze settling on the tightly wrapped scarf.
"I'm fine. Are you alright? Why did you come here so dangerously?"
"Since Dwayne Carter was apprehended, Cameron Mac had been preparing to facilitate his sons' escape. It's better to stop them here than let them slip away."
"Since when have you been investigating?"
Nathan fell silent. Raising a white hand, he smoothed Alex's hair before speaking slowly.
"While you were injured and lying down. I received help too. If anything were to happen to you, I..."
Nathan trailed off. Alex quietly observed Nathan for a moment before extending his hand.
"You did well. But from now on, let us, the police, handle it, okay?"

Nathan grasped the offered hand firmly. Alex knew there was likely still much to learn about Nathan, but he recognized this gesture as a sign of agreement. Whether it would be consistently honored, however, remained uncertain.
Instead of dwelling on his thoughts, Alex covered Nathan's cold, frozen hands with both of his own to warm them.
"Let's go."
Nathan said. Alex nodded. As they walked towards where the car was parked, Alex spoke as if recalling something.
"That was cool."
Nathan seemed to understand. Taking out the Mercedes car key, Nathan added a brief reply.
"I should have hit him one more time."
"Indeed."
He would rot in prison for life anyway, but perhaps that alternative wouldn't have been so bad either.

Alex stood still, quietly observing the police car that had begun to depart. A desolate wind blew, chillingly sweeping through his chest. He had once envisioned what he would do if he ever encountered David Mac again. The anger, buried beneath resignation, had never been truly resolved, often bubbling up like a simmering pot.
But now, witnessing David captured at his absolute worst, Alex felt no desire to dwell on him any longer. It was an unexpected form of retribution, but it was sufficient.

What mattered was that he and Nathan were now together. Just as David had once ruined Alex's life and yet continued to thrive, Alex resolved to no longer suffer over the remnants David had left behind.
He felt ready.
The Last Car of the Train

The new year was just around the corner. Having concluded the extensive investigation, the team was granted compensatory leave. Alex, who had sustained injuries, received an additional order to rest fully until the second week of January. Since the entire team had dedicated even Christmas Eve and Christmas Day to the investigation, everyone appeared to be returning to their hometowns for the year-end.
Only Alex had nowhere to go. Perhaps that would have been the case last year.

London's Christmas, unlike Christmas Eve, was rather desolate, leaving those without family with a profound sense of loneliness. For foreigners who had journeyed alone from various countries to spend Christmas, the holiday often felt more like a day of emptiness than a celebration. That lonely sentiment tended to linger well into the new year.

Alex set down the tea he was drinking at a restaurant where the news was playing. The meeting time was approaching. At Alex's request to see the outside, they had arranged to meet at Leicester Square. It was the location of their first date. To be precise, it had been a practice date, but a date nonetheless.

The news had been consistently reporting on the former soccer star who had spearheaded the human experiments at MacMilan Pharmaceutical Company. The Beta Tester Incident was a series of murders fabricated to conceal these human experiments. The experiments, conducted under David Mac's leadership, had been carried out in secrecy, without the company's knowledge.
