Cameron Mac, the second-largest shareholder, had facilitated this, and as suspected, Ian Mac's incurable illness had been the primary catalyst for the experiments. Naturally, various other interests were also intertwined. Sera Ots, who had participated in the experiments, had secretly passed evidence to Amy, and thanks to that evidence, David Mac and Cameron Mac were arrested. Patrick Shore, who had meticulously selected and handed over victims, cooperated splendidly for a reduced sentence. Through him, victim's hair was also discovered in Dwayne Carter's workshop. Dwayne Carter confessed only after his employer was arrested.

The biggest highlight was Sera Ots's return from hiding in Germany. The trial she attended as a witness became a daily topic of discussion. Two of the five Beta victims whose identities remained undisclosed were other researchers involved in the project, hired like Sera Ots under strict secrecy agreements.

Having realized the danger too late, they were killed first, without even a chance to flee. They too were the type who kept their associates at arm's length, so not even a missing person report was filed. Thus, it seemed clear that when David Mac initiated this, he had carefully selected individuals who were socially vulnerable and isolated, much like Alex. When it was revealed that he was the mastermind behind the horrific mutilation of corpses to destroy evidence, condemnation poured in from around the world. David's residence and the Mac family's private estates were vandalized by protesters.

The unrest flared up so violently, reminiscent of the riots that had once swept across the entire United Kingdom, that the police had to intervene to suppress it. The Betas' anger was immense. Even though he received the maximum sentence, extreme opinions calling for public execution rained down.

chapters.title: Chapter 116
paragraphs: Alex gathered his shopping bag and stood up. He had decided to accept Nathan's offer and stay at his house until he recovered. He felt a pang of guilt for being indebted, but his desire to see Nathan every day was far stronger. Besides, being alone in the house was, frankly, unbearably lonely.
He detested being alone.

He hadn't brought many clothes from home; the coat he was wearing was the only one. Nathan had told him not to bother packing more, assuring him they could simply buy anything else he needed. Since his heavy luggage had been moved yesterday, today all he had was a single shopping bag.

Checking the time, Alex slowly walked out of the restaurant. The lunchtime sky was exceptionally clear and bright. This winter had brought an unusual number of sunny days. Although rainy or cloudy days were overwhelmingly more frequent, having sunshine even just once or twice a week like this significantly lifted his spirits.

Feathery clouds drifted across the vast blue sky. Walking along the pavement, warmed by the gentle sunlight, Alex stopped in front of the subway station. Nathan was always punctual, so he would likely arrive within minutes.

As he checked the time again, Alex suddenly glanced down the stairs. Watching the constant stream of people ascending and descending, he made up his mind on a sudden impulse and straightened up. He descended the stairs slowly at first, then picked up speed, practically running to the subway station.

Alex hesitated. What he was about to do was akin to a fool's errand. There were many ways to travel from Shoreditch to Leicester Square. Nathan was most likely to come by car, and even if he took the subway, he might not have transferred to the Piccadilly line.
Still, Alex proceeded with what he wanted to do.
After tapping his Oyster card, Alex descended to the platform bound for Heathrow Airport. The circular tunnel carried the scent of stale dust.

He slowly made his way to the very end of the platform, in the direction the train would arrive. A display on the ceiling announced that a train was arriving in one minute. Squeezing through the crowd, Alex positioned himself on the yellow safety line.
*Mind the gap*

He stared down at the yellow lettering for a long time. He recalled the countless obstacles that had been placed before him. He recalled the self that believed he could never properly blend in among people.
Mixed-race, mediocre talent, an awkward personality—everything that constituted him.
Alex believed he would never be able to bridge the gap separating him from this cold and indifferent world.
Clearly, Alex alone could not eliminate this gap. It was innate, an intrinsic element that made up Alex himself.
While he was lost in thought, the subway train began to arrive. A lukewarm wind swept through the station. The people, as if accustomed to it, frowned and stepped back.

Alex slowly lifted his head. A red and blue subway train entered the platform with a clamorous rumble. Its rounded body filled the dark tracks and came to a smooth stop. The train's tail end, the last carriage door, stopped directly in front of him.
Alex spotted the green eyes watching him quietly from beyond that door.
The door slid open.
"Hi, Nathan."
Nathan stood at the doorway. Alex met his gaze, looking up at him with a shy smile. A smile slowly formed on Nathan's weary white face, and he extended his hand.
"Good lunch."

Alex took his hand. The dress shoe that had been on the yellow line moved. The shoe leaped over the gap separating the train and the tracks in a single stride. As soon as he stepped inside, landing on the train floor, Nathan pulled him closer. An arm wrapped around his waist. Simultaneously, laughter erupted. Nathan laughed softly, and Alex let out a light "haha," curling the corners of his mouth upward.
"We have to get off."
The door closed before his words had fully finished. The hand on his waist pulled Alex tightly. Nathan, who had lowered his head, whispered into Alex's ear.
"Let's go somewhere we haven't been."
*There are many places to go, Alex.*

A voice that might sound cold to others could only be sweet to Alex. Facing Nathan, Alex nodded. The scent of the cool winter wind mingled with Nathan's unique fragrance, creating an incredibly happy aroma. After a long journey that had circled back, the two stood again at their starting point. Two truly different people had met, and instead of eliminating the insurmountable gap between them, they chose to hold each other's hands and leap over it. It hadn't been easy and had taken a long time. There were many occasions when the pain made them want to give up.
But they had persevered.
All for this very moment.
*Please be considerate*

Buds began to sprout on the bare branches that had seemed devoid of life. It was spring. Vibrant colors slowly seeped into the buildings stained gray and lifeless, and the frozen ground thawed softly. Grass revealed its green appearance on the ground in parks hidden throughout London. The days were gradually lengthening, and even at 6 p.m. sunlight cast faint traces of warmth.
"You've been looking good lately, Doctor."

It was his colleague nurse, Susan Ray, who caught Nathan's step as he was leaving work. She had just put on a thin coat, as the weather was still chilly, and she straightened up slightly. With a smile on her face, as if something pleased her, she was a peer who had started working at the hospital a few months after Nathan. Her voluminous curly brown hair framed a face of modest beauty, and there were several Alpha doctors at the hospital who were fond of her, an Omega.
"In what way."

Nathan at the hospital was concise and clear. He listened to requests he needed to hear, rarely engaged in small talk, and otherwise solely focused on his work. He maintained the same distance from everyone. Greetings were exchanged, and questions were answered only. His life had always been this way. Except for a few close friends, he was equally businesslike with everyone.
There was only one exception.
"Isn't your lover so cute? Being an Alpha, you must have quite a possessive streak, I see."

The moment the topic of conversation shifted to Alex, a crack appeared on his impassive face. The first thing he felt was wariness. Susan's description of Alex as 'cute' triggered a flicker of defensiveness in Nathan. Needing to understand why she used that word for someone *his*, Nathan carefully composed his expression and asked.
"Well, I can't really sense that part."

That answer was also true. This was a separate realm from Alex blindly following him. He didn't know if it was because his personality was too docile, but he had never seen Alex show jealousy. He thought maybe Alex just didn't show it, but it certainly seemed that way.
"Ah, thinking about it, that would be the case. My apologies. You're a Beta, aren't you, Doctor White?"
Hoho, Susan laughed and leaned her upper body forward slightly with a playful expression. Then she whispered.

"I've been able to sense your lover's pheromones on you every day for the past few months. Everyone's happy, thinking you two are doing well. People were really surprised seeing you smile when you're with him."
This was unexpected.

Nathan paused for a moment at the answer that fell outside his expectations. The realm of pheromones was one Betas could absolutely never perceive, so it was only natural Nathan hadn't noticed. His chest tingling, Nathan raised his hand to cover his mouth to hide his troubled expression.
*Damn, he's doing cute things.*

Whether it was a result led by the unconscious or not, Nathan had chosen a profession studying Alphas to understand Alex's Secondary Gender. The reason he had moved from being an internist to trying to become a Secondary Gender specialist was likely that. He had tried to consciously avoid it too, but when considering his specialty, he had insisted at the time that it wasn't the reason for giving up surgery, but ultimately it was. Since Betas could only understand pheromones intellectually, this area was particularly difficult for them.

Still, he had researched for quite a long time. He studied hard and tried to learn a lot. Even though it was common sense that one could be marked with the pheromones of their loved one, whether Omega or Alpha, he couldn't feel it and thus hadn't even thought about it.
*That Alex's pheromones are on my body.*
The moment he thought that, an overwhelming scene came to mind. Nathan slightly furrowed his brow, concealing his embarrassment, and spoke to Susan.
"Thank you for your concern."
"Don't mention it. Have a good evening."
"Yes. You too, Ms. Ray."

chapters.title: Chapter 117
paragraphs: He gave a light nod and rose to his feet. Embarrassed by the crude fantasies that were beginning to surge uncontrollably, he instinctively tensed his lower abdomen to suppress the urge, and walked down towards the hospital entrance. The simmering heat that had been building up began to make his body unbearably warm.
It was no wonder. It had already been four months since he hadn't been able to touch Alex Yeon.
While Alex's injury was recovering, Nathan had brought him into his home. He thought it was the natural thing to do, and the satisfaction of getting what he wanted was beyond words.

Having Alex in his sight all day was even more fulfilling than he had anticipated. Because he worried Alex might get hurt or cause an accident if he was out of his sight, Nathan never took his eyes off him when he was home. Fortunately, Alex loved staying by his side. This was also something Nathan greatly cherished.

However, this mysterious and happy life had one drawback. Abstinence. He had no intention of laying a hand on Alex until his body was fully healthy. There were two reasons. It was obviously necessary for Alex's health, and the other was that he wasn't confident he could restrain himself. He recalled, without missing a single day, the first experience of seeing Alex's naked body after a shower. At that time, Nathan, unaware of why he was so desperately impatient, felt like he was going mad as he waited for Alex, who remained in the bathroom for over forty minutes, and finally lost his patience. When he opened the door and saw the skin peeking from the robe, he couldn't do anything for a moment. He could only stare at the scene like a madman.

Water had pooled on his straight, firm collarbones, and his chest, tracing a sleek curve and stretching tautly, was pale. He lost all self-control at the sight of Alex, to the point where his younger self, who never thought he'd lust after a man's body, seemed insignificant. The waist inside the revealed robe was unexpectedly slender. The smooth sides that stretched differently from his solid shoulders, and the straightly carved abs were inherently sensual.

The first experience of licking, biting, and nibbling on living flesh was so intense it was impossible to erase. The moment Alex touched his genitals with clumsy hands, Nathan truly felt his sanity flying away for the first time. Desire momentarily suppressed his reason. The moist heat with which Alex's mouth engulfed his fingers wasn't repulsive. It was just, simply, maddening.

Human sexual desire was an aspect Nathan couldn't quite understand. He even considered acts like kissing unclean, so when he kissed the lovers he had accepted and kept by his side after their confessions, he didn't feel any particular sensation. The act of mixing saliva and tongues was unpleasant and didn't feel hygienic.

Alex was an exception to all of Nathan's rules; a collection of wild variables in his otherwise ordered life. The sexual desire he thought was castrated for him surged explosively the moment it touched Alex.

Nathan now knew better than anyone what it felt like to be clenched so tightly. The lewd face making whimpering sounds as he was pierced, the trembling body, the sight of him reaching climax while tightening below, even the climax as he spilled copious semen...

*Haah.* Enduring the boiling heat, Nathan came down to the lobby. Brushing his hair back with a nervous expression, he gritted his teeth. Alex's recovery was much better than expected, and the test results were good. An injury that would have taken half a year for an ordinary person to recover from had already healed long ago, now four months later. If he managed it from here on and started exercising slowly, his body would fully return.
Nathan was enduring painfully to hold out until that moment. It was absurd how he was being tossed about by sexual desire like this.
"Nathan!"
As soon as he walked to the entrance, Alex spotted him. A bright smile instantly settled on his face, which had no particular expression, and it was a wondrous scene in itself.

The sharp eyes under his neat eyebrows didn't actually look that innocent. But when he smiled, his eyes, half-closed and curving downwards, couldn't be any more lovely. He even felt the illusion of a puppy's ears perking up. He knew comparing his lover to a dog wasn't a good thing, but he did it anyway.
Because he was lovely.
"Did work go well? Aren't you hungry?"
He was so lovely it was driving him crazy. Nathan realized his face was softening. It was an unstoppable phenomenon.
"Are you tired?"

Before he could even return the greeting, Alex, with an excited face, ran over and asked after his well-being. It was endearing to see him running around, proclaiming that he was fully recovered. At the question that gave him no room to answer, Nathan finally laughed. A languid smile formed on his cold face.
"Not tired. Were you waiting?"

Reaching out naturally, he touched Alex's cheek. He gently rubbed his cheek, ear, and forehead with his pale fingertips. The smooth texture winding around his fingertips made Nathan feel the desire he had just calmed trying to rise again. It was unavoidable. Alex, who was smaller than him, had not a single part that wasn't lovely. He had thought so in the past too, but now, every part of his body being a little small felt miraculous and pretty. How could such a body exist? Just as he was quietly enduring his soaring desire, Alex blushed.
"I just got here too."

Even though he had touched him every day for the past four months, Alex seemed like a person who simply couldn't get used to it. He met his eyes, not knowing what to do. *Do you know how you look like you're in trouble?*

Seeing him noticeably stiffen and become embarrassed just from skin touching skin made his lower abdomen harden. Swallowing his lips, he wanted to strip him and make him cry messily. The sight of his face crying sorrowfully, thinking he was urinating, suddenly overlapped, so Nathan let out a long sigh and pulled Alex into an embrace.

The width of his shoulders wasn't that different from his, but his waist, which fit perfectly and comfortably in his arms, was always amazing. It was considerably thinner than his. Rubbing his lips against the elastic skin, Nathan took a deep breath. As if trying to find Alex's pheromone, which he couldn't smell.
"N-Nathan, is it okay to do this outside?"

Twitching his body, Alex stiffened rigidly. It seemed he was quite embarrassed to be embraced in front of the hospital lobby, but as he spoke timidly, Nathan felt the arm embracing his back. Putting more strength into the arm holding him, Nathan buried his nose in the nape of his neck. chapters.title: Chapter 134
paragraphs: "What did I do wrong, huh?"

Then Alex was also surprised. After observing his expression for a moment, Alex timidly said.

"Sorry. I got carried away. I wanted to see your face, but you wouldn't show it, so I grabbed you like that without thinking."

Unlike his calm and seemingly bored pretty face, Nathan was very rough in bed. At first, they didn't feel much because they were both clumsy, but from the month they started properly mingling bodies, Nathan began to improve day by day.

Each time, he delivered a pleasure so intense it stole Alex's senses, revealing new facets of himself in the process. Pleas to stop were futile. Nathan's medical background gave him an almost preternatural understanding of Alex's physical limits.

Driven relentlessly, Alex was thrust into and shaken roughly, Nathan demanding words that made him cringe with shame. They were both sturdy, tall men, and Alex's life had been a constant struggle, so while their encounters pushed him to his limits, he was not overwhelmed.
But a situation like the one just now made him involuntarily a little surprised. No, actually, he was very surprised.
"That's not it, it's just, today... I had a nightmare..."

Alex made an excuse that was bound to sound ridiculous. He himself didn't know why he was so startled. It wasn't like he'd been hit; it was just his hair being grabbed. Nathan twisted his eyebrows crookedly, then, with a heartfelt sigh, pulled Alex even closer into his embrace.

"No, you are pretty. Maybe it's because you like sweet things, but your body scent is sweet too. You use the same shower gel and lotion as me, hmm? There's nothing about you that isn't pretty."

His opinion was not acknowledged by Nathan. He could feel Nathan sniffing his skin scent like a young animal, rubbing his nose against his neck. Startling at the stimulation on his sensitive skin, Alex still fumbled for Nathan's hand and intertwined their fingers. Then, after looking at Nathan for a moment, he lifted his arm and smelled it. It just smelled like the shower gel Nathan used.
"It's the same."

Instead of replying, Nathan kissed his cheek. His frantically beating heart gradually found its normal rhythm. Being held in Nathan's embrace made sleepiness wash over him again. He felt languid and wanted to stay like this. It was probably because he was startled that he felt this way more intensely.

Due to professional habits and a tendency to wake up early since his past, he didn't sleep much, but Alex was actually the type who needed a lot of sleep. Moreover, once he fell asleep, he slept deeply. As his body and mind became more comfortable being with Nathan, his sleep had increased lately.
"Sleepy?"

He blinked. Something he had forgotten surfaced in his drowsy mind.
"Aren't we late, Nate?"
He guessed over thirty minutes had passed. He was late too. Besides, the soccer uniform he had was currently the only one, so he had no practice clothes to wear right away.
"Should we not go?"
Nathan whispered suggestively. If he had animal ears, they would have perked right up; Alex immediately brightened up.
"Is that okay?"
"If you don't go, I'll take the day off too. I was just planning to go to the research lab today anyway."

His tone instantly softened. Stroking his hair affectionately, Nathan rubbed his lips against Alex's earlobe. Being the type to always keep promises, Alex was strongly tempted but also hesitated. Sergeant Hayden's face flickered in his mind. Seeing him look conflicted, Nathan whispered again.
"Do you absolutely have to go to practice?"
"That's not it..."
To be precise, it was members like Matthew and the others who needed to practice, while Alex's role was closer to checking their form.
"Then don't go."
"But the tournament isn't far off..."
"Stay with me."

That was very, extremely, immensely tempting. Alex genuinely pondered. He felt a pang of conscience, but spending the day off with Nathan was much more appealing. As he silently continued his internal conflict, Nathan tickled the nape of his neck playfully.
"Let's sleep in together and then go see a movie."
He even batted his eyes prettily and looked down at him. It was so cute it made his heart ache. Alex was momentarily mesmerized, just gazing at his face.
"Should we?"
How could he possibly resist someone this adorable? Alex declared his predetermined surrender. If Nathan asked, what couldn't he do?
"Okay."

Then Nathan swiftly moved into action. Reaching for the nightstand, he grabbed his phone and had Alex dial Sergeant Hayden's number. When Alex offered to make the call himself, Nathan firmly refused. While Alex clung tightly to Nathan's arm, feeling guilty about lying, Nathan expressionlessly and nonchalantly told Sergeant Hayden Alex's diagnosis.

He said Alex had come down with pseudomembranous colitis, was resting at the hospital, and should probably take the day off today, even offering the medical opinion that it would be best not to overwork him tomorrow either.
"What kind of illness is that?"
Hearing the disease name for the first time, Alex asked curiously. Nathan answered nonchalantly.
"It's a type of severe enteritis you can get while using antibiotics. It's not a major illness."

Perhaps because of the word 'pseudomembranous,' it sounded like a serious disease. Doctors are amazing. It's a very convenient profession for lying. Alex thought to himself. Or is Nathan just really good at it? It seemed like both.

Nathan stroked Alex's head again, then picked him up in his arms. As he slid his arms under Alex's knees and effortlessly lifted him, Alex hurriedly wrapped his arms around Nathan's neck. It was a gesture that seemed incongruous with Alex's physique, but Nathan did this so frequently that Alex had grown accustomed to it with a hint of resignation.

But he didn't forget to add that one comment. Because he really wasn't a light weight. He laid Alex down on the bed that was nominally there but hardly ever used. Nathan pulled up the thin blanket and closed the window curtains.
"Sleep, sleep."

Chatting idly, saying things like that to each other, at some point Nathan's hand covered Alex's eyes. Using the quiet sound of the air conditioner as a lullaby, the two fell asleep like that.

Alex woke up around 1 PM. Nathan, who had woken up first, had already stripped the bedroom sheets and dealt with the damp mattress. Nathan gifted Alex with several kisses as he stumbled out. After that, they took a bath together. They poured a bath bomb containing tea leaves into the tub, played in the water with their hands, and washed each other. As payback for getting water in Nathan's eyes, Alex was subjected to another stern matter in the bathtub. Dressed in short sleeves and cotton pants, they prepared a late lunch. Square-cut sunlight poured dazzlingly through the large glass window in the living room, and the air inside the house was pleasantly cool. The feel of the clothes on his well-dried skin and the cool air lifted his mood. It was excessively perfect.

Lunch was pizza. While Alex made the pizza dough and rolled it out into a circle, Nathan picked and washed the basil they had grown together. Pressing the center to make the edges puff up nicely, he spread the dough into a circle. chapters.title: Chapter 135
paragraphs: "It's delicious."

A soft laugh mingled with the chirping of birds outside the kitchen window. Through the window, which had been left open just while they cooked, the murmuring voices of families passing by on the street could be heard. He sprinkled finely grated mozzarella cheese evenly over the sauce. It was time to add the final toppings.
"What should we put on?"
"Canadian."
Nathan's tastes were definite. He liked things with mushrooms or vegetables, and if it was meat, it was finely chopped bacon pieces and pepperoni.
"Bacon, mushrooms, and pepperoni, right?"
"Yeah. You?"
"Then I'll have Hawaiian."

Nathan's expression turned strange. Come to think of it, Nathan had probably never seen what kind of pizza he ate. He wasn't a big eater, and whenever they ate pizza out, he usually just matched Nathan's style.
"I didn't know you liked hot pineapple."
"It's sweet, so I like it."
It was literally true. Among pizzas, the only thing that gave a sweet taste was the one with pineapple.
"I didn't know that."
Nathan squinted one eye and then gently bit Alex's nose. *Ack!* Alex let out a sound and burst out laughing.
"Your taste is weird."
As expected, it seemed Nathan was one of the many people who disliked pineapple on pizza. Alex stubbornly argued back.
"Pineapple is so tasty."
Alex was well-trained from countless reactions he'd received whenever he said he liked Hawaiian pizza. When he argued quite boldly that pineapple was delicious, Nathan let out a short laugh.
"You're the delicious one."
"Let's just put the toppings on quickly."

His face flushed instantly at the hard-to-handle words that suddenly changed the topic. Fortunately, the oven, preheated right on time, beeped. Nathan, who stopped Alex from reaching toward the ceiling, took out the pineapple can instead. Their fingers overlapped.
"I'm not joking. It's true."
"H-how can a person be delicious?"
"You are."

Grabbing the hand that tried to escape, Nathan kissed him. It was strange. He definitely didn't seem this skilled at first. By the time he came to his senses, Nathan had already become someone who could casually say such risqué things.

Not that he disliked it at all. His heart raced as if it might burst at the thought of him saying such things with that languid face and pleasant voice. It was just that he felt too immature compared to Nathan and was ashamed. He felt like he should also be able to say cool things like that.
It seemed forever impossible, given that his innate genetics were fundamentally different from Nathan's. Well, Nathan had dated many girlfriends since he was young.

Then the forgotten nightmare of Jessica Bundy and last night's woman came to mind. Shaking his head at the useless thoughts that kept surfacing, Alex clasped hands with him. Nathan smiled silently and opened the pineapple can.

The pizza, finished with a sprinkle of basil, was slowly baked and completed 15 minutes later. It was different from the frequently malfunctioning oven he'd used when living alone in his old apartment. Nathan's kitchen was full of nothing but expensive, nice things, so naturally, the fun of cooking had increased.

It was nice to have a bathtub to fill with warm water for a bath, and it was nice that the house stayed cool in summer without needing a fan. If he hadn't met Nathan, he probably would never have enjoyed his present life. Nathan was the first good thing to happen in Alex's life, a stroke of luck he'd never meet again.

Alex pretended not to know the complicated feelings that had been gnawing at him since yesterday. Whenever he was with Nathan, he was always just happy, but somewhere deep in his heart, he felt anxious, as if he'd returned to his childhood. Whether his efforts had an effect or not, the shallow unease gradually subsided as they sat together in the living room and started eating pizza.

While happily watching Nathan fold his pizza in half to eat it, he realized it was already well past 4 PM. While searching for the most harmless newly released movie, Nathan, upon hearing Alex say he'd never been to the BFI, booked tickets for an IMAX film. So they ended up having a date two days in a row.

South Bank on the weekend was crowded. He had almost no memory of coming to the Waterloo side. As he was looking around at the unfamiliar scenery despite having lived his whole life in London, Nathan approached.
"What do you want to drink?"
Nathan, who had naturally brought a bag of Maltesers chocolate, asked Alex. Alex, who had been curiously looking around at the people, answered quickly. A laugh escaped him without him realizing.
"Milkshake!"
His voice was a little loud. Nathan chuckled softly.
"Got it."

The cinema was extremely crowded. For Alex, who had often used movie money to cover living expenses, cultural activities were a truly long-unexperienced thing. No matter how well London's system was designed for poor students to enjoy cultural life, that was something only those with leisure could do.
Until the uninvited guest appeared.

Since neither he nor Nathan had fixed holidays and were busy on top of that, a weekend cinema visit was close to being a first-time experience. His mood, which had slightly sunk while making the pizza, reached its peak the moment Nathan returned with snacks for two.
"Oh my, aren't you Mr. White?"

A woman with long curly hair who suddenly appeared spoke to Nathan out of the blue. Alex, his smiling face frozen, blinked and stiffened. Déjà vu? Why do women know Nathan wherever we go? Alex thought blankly.

Nathan, who had been walking over, turned his head expressionlessly. The woman was much shorter than last night's model-like blonde woman, so much so that she would fit snugly into Nathan's embrace. Simultaneously, her figure was incredible.
"Ms. Loel."
"That's right! I never thought I'd see you outside, what's this all about? Did you come to see a movie too?"
The woman called Loel spoke to Nathan very happily. Alex, who had been frozen, took a deep breath. He carefully took one step forward. Like a dog guarding its owner against an interloper.
"Yes."

Nathan answered curtly. He didn't even smile. But the woman named Loel showed no sign of backing off. Alex's anxiety intensified even more. Alex had few female friends or Omegas in his life, while Nathan seemed to know countless women.

Come to think of it, weren't his doctor colleagues also overwhelmingly women? No, setting that aside, no matter how small London was, how did someone he knew appear every day? Alex began to suspect if Nathan had secretly debuted somewhere. He felt a surge of anxiety, a desperate urge to illegally search for information about Nathan.
"Wow, that's unexpected! I had the image that you wouldn't come to movies or theaters like this."

Loel even took a step closer to Nathan. He could see her friends behind her, eyes shining, asking who he was. Alex's wariness exploded. He anxiously took two steps forward. Nathan was right there within arm's reach.
"Is that so."

Nathan, who had spotted Alex, turned his head. Loel's gaze also landed on Alex. Unable to endure it any longer, Alex approached Nathan's side. Then, with wary eyes, he stood beside him, took the Maltesers, and stuck close.
"Hello."
Alex greeted her. The smile on the woman named Loel's face deepened.
"Oh my, there's a handsome gentleman here. Are you a friend?"

Alex, who was about to respond confidently, found himself momentarily speechless. The answer 'Yes!' didn't immediately jump out. As if overly tense words wouldn't come out, Alex froze. Would it be okay if I were Nathan's lover?
Well, of course it would be okay. Alex had loved Nathan for a long time and wished for it. The problem was the part where Nathan had only dated women until now.

With the perception that Betas typically meet the opposite sex still firmly entrenched in the world, he hesitated over whether it was okay to say such a thing immediately to a stranger he didn't know well. The people at the hospital learned through Nathan's mouth that they were in a relationship. Come to think of it, he had never once directly told Nathan's acquaintances that he was his lover.

chapters.title: Chapter 136
paragraphs: While Alex hesitated for these reasons, Laurel spoke up again.
"How about watching a movie and hanging out together, if that's okay?"

Nathan's gaze locked onto Alex. Alex snapped back to attention at Laurel's words. The situation had become a bit awkward for giving the 'lover' answer, but watching a movie together was truly out of the question. Alex tried to shake his head urgently. Nathan spoke up for him, who was trying to convey a refusal in a roundabout way.
"Sorry, but Alex is a bit shy in new situations. That probably won't work. Have a good time."

Having delivered a crisp reply, Nathan pulled Alex away before Alex could even glance at Laurel again with wary eyes. Even as he was being dragged away, Alex stubbornly kept staring in Laurel's direction.

Only when they reached the stairs below the theater entrance did Nathan stop. Standing in a secluded spot where few people passed by, Alex found himself trapped between Nathan and the wall. Looking up with wide eyes, Nathan spoke with a slight frown between his brows.
"What was that just now?"
Nathan seemed angry. Alex felt wronged. He was the one who kept running into women outside!
"What was what?"

It was usually true that Alex was in the wrong, and Nathan was always right! But today, he had no idea what he'd done wrong. Alex asked, revealing his aggrieved expression. Nathan let out a laugh that seemed incredulous.
"Why don't you say you're lovers when asked if you're friends?"

A brief silence descended. Alex hesitated. He needed time to organize the complex thoughts that had raced through his mind in that short moment into a single sentence. The reason for thinking the same thing as before was clearly because of yesterday's events and the content of the nightmare, but he didn't want to tell Nathan that.
He didn't want to seem petty.
"Well, it's true that we're friends too."
So Alex answered like that for the moment.
"You and me?"
We're lovers, but we're also friends. Didn't it start as friends? A very long time ago.
But it didn't seem like the right answer for this situation. Nathan wiped the expression from his face, making it look frightening. Then he let out a 'Hah' sound.
"Do you kiss, have sex, and live together with a friend? I don't. I don't have a hobby of getting horny and jumping on friends."
That's true. You don't do that with friends. Alex replied, feeling dejected.
"So from now on, don't hesitate and answer straight. I'm your lover. Not your friend."
"That's why... I..."
I did it because I didn't want you to get hurt from dating me, a guy, instead of a woman.

Alex said inwardly. It was true that Alex was completely clueless in this regard, but if he said even that, Nathan would definitely get even angrier. He'd probably get hurt too. So Alex just apologized.
"I'm sorry."

He bowed his head slightly. Normally, he would have checked Nathan's mood, held his hand, or added more words, but in the end, he didn't do anything. Since yesterday, women who knew Nathan kept appearing, and it made him uncomfortable. He hated that these negative thoughts kept surfacing. As he stared at the toes of his sneakers and kept his head down, Nathan grabbed his chin.
"Alex."

When Alex tried to avoid making eye contact, Nathan followed his gaze. With that pretty face right in front of his nose, there was no way to turn away. Having no choice but to look straight at him, Nathan frowned.
"I wasn't trying to push you. I just didn't like that you gave that kind of answer."
"Yeah."

An apologetic look appeared on his expressionless face. His flat voice became more affectionate than usual. However, the something that had started swelling since yesterday didn't easily disappear. Even Alex couldn't clearly identify the emotion. It clung to his heart like a leech, leaving a mark, and kept making him feel unpleasant and displeased.
Was it jealousy? But Nathan hadn't done anything in particular, had he?
When Alex remained silent, Nathan hugged him. Holding him tightly in his embrace, he spoke.
"I'm not angry. I'm sorry."

Alex nodded. Smelling Nathan's fragrant, clean scent, Alex thought that in times like these, he wished Nathan were an Alpha or Omega. Then Nathan would know that Alex was going around with his pheromones all over him, and there would probably be more Alphas or Omegas around Nathan than Betas.
Maybe they could have started dating a long, long time ago.
"Let's go, to see the movie."
"Yeah."

Linking their fingers together softly, Nathan spoke. Alex was about to ask who this 'Laurel' person was, but afraid of hearing an answer similar to yesterday's, he just kept his mouth shut. For him, the most frightening thing was causing problems by his own doing. There were no problems between them. Everything was peaceful. Really, nothing was wrong.

The movie was fun. It was a movie about animals infected with a plague attacking people, and the main character was a dog. To be precise, it was a dog and its owner. This strange film, a mix of zombie flick and moving drama, had surprisingly many viewers, enough to win an award at the BFI.

Each time a cheerful scene appeared, hearing the audience's laughter made his mood gradually improve as well. After all, from the start, as long as there were no incidents or money-related troubles, Alex was the kind of person who could be happy every day just with Nathan alone, so it was natural.

This was their first time visiting the BFI. The stairs were incredibly steep and high, and the huge screen was very close to the seats. The theater was so high that it was almost worrisome whether there might be an accident, making just entering it a sufficiently enjoyable experience. Nathan picked up some Maltesers and fed them to him, and also let Alex lick the chocolate off his fingers. Alex, in turn, fed Nathan popcorn. Honestly, this was more fun than the movie.

On the way back, they bought ice cream at McDonald's. He smiled happily at Nathan, who bought the chocolate-coated ice cream as if it were obvious and offered it to him. It was amazing how even just performing some trivial action made him feel happiness.

It was a satisfying day, albeit with some twists and turns. On the way home, he opened the car window while listening to the late-night radio flowing from inside the car. The lukewarm night breeze carried the scent of freshly sprouted green leaves and flowers from all around. The moon was big and high. Like the night road the first time they held hands.
The car stopped with a red signal. Nathan, who had been looking ahead, slowly turned his head and opened his mouth.
"Hm?"
"Alex."
"Don't keep what's inside your heart to yourself, tell me."
"Why suddenly?"
"You seemed like you had something to say earlier."

Alex blinked for a moment. Well, he did have something to say. But it was already past, and moreover, he didn't want to bring up an unpleasant topic. Precisely because he trusted Nathan, he felt that way.
Also, he was afraid of conflict arising.

To Alex, Nathan was his world. He didn't like anyone other than Nathan. Even when Nathan didn't listen to him, he had no memory of properly resenting him, so he especially didn't want to show that his mood was a bit soured over something as trivial as other people's matters.

In Alex's memory, conflict was always a path leading to the worst. Fights were connected to catastrophe. His mother and father's relationship was like that, and his relationship with David Mac was like that too. He didn't want to provide a pretext for conflict.

If he thought about it carefully, Alex had never had a close friend, and with close colleagues he met later in life, like Matthew, he had no memory of emotionally exhausting fights. He had virtually no memory of arguing with anyone.
In other words, Alex had never fought with someone in a precious relationship. For him, it was easier to endure and let things pass. Just like how he had never once talked back to his father.
"I'm fine. I guess I was just a bit startled since morning."
"Really?"
"Yeah!"

Alex nodded. Nathan narrowed his eyes and looked at him. The signal changed. As Alex whispered, "It's green," Nathan reached out his hand. After gently ruffling his hair, he gripped the steering wheel again.
"Still, if you want to say something, say it."
"I will."
"Promise me."
"Should we pinky promise?"
"When we get home."
At Nathan's answer, Alex laughed. He erased the thought that had briefly crossed his mind. No matter how much he thought about it, he couldn't imagine fighting with Nathan. Unless Nathan got angry.
Maybe it would never happen in his lifetime.
Naively, Alex thought that.

chapters.title: Chapter 137
paragraphs: The ominous omen brought by the nightmare properly revealed itself the next day. The start was ordinary. It was an extremely happy and peaceful morning.
"When are you getting your summer vacation?"

Alex asked, scooping blueberry jam and orange marmalade to spread on his toast. Since entering summer, Alex had been very much looking forward to Nathan's birthday in August and had previously suggested matching his vacation schedule to the birthday.

It was Nathan's birthday that I was properly celebrating for the first time. Nathan's birthday always fell during the vacation period, so even during high school, I had no memory of celebrating it directly. Since the last summer we had spent attached at the hip had been ruined by the David Mac incident, strictly speaking, this was Alex's first time celebrating Nathan's birthday.

Moreover, since I had always been on the receiving end, I wanted to do my absolute best and do a lot for Nathan's birthday this time. Thanks to no longer having to pay off debts, I had even saved up some money. I wanted to buy the plane tickets myself and book a nice place for accommodation to create wonderful memories for Nathan. I was still choosing a gift to give him on the trip.
"Early or mid-August. If you tell me the day you want, I'll match it."
"Really? Can you do that?"
"Yeah. What about you?"
"I think I'll be fine too."

There was the condition that we had to win the soccer tournament to enjoy it comfortably, but I was confident about that part. Nathan, brushing off his sleepy, languid face, stood behind Alex. Wrapping his arms around Alex from behind as if to embrace him, he reached for the toaster. In doing so, Alex found himself embraced. Nathan's dry yet faint scent spread. My body grew slightly warmer. Feeling strangely embarrassed, Alex lowered his gaze.
"What do you want to do this Wednesday?"
Nathan asked as he scooped the toast onto a plate. Alex tilted his head to the side. This Wednesday?
"Wednesday..."

Thinking about it, I remembered I had one plan. I recalled Matthew casually asking me last week, along with Anna. When I had said I had no particular plans for Wednesday, Matthew had suggested we all go to a pub together. Since Nathan was always at the hospital until late on weekdays like Wednesday, Alex had accepted the suggestion without much thought.
"I'll probably hang out with Matthew."
At that, Nathan's hand, which had been scooping the toast, stopped.
"You're going to hang out with Matthew Wayne on Wednesday?"
"Yeah."

Alex cautiously turned his head back. Sneaking a glance up, Nathan's green eyes were looking sharply at me. Alex blinked. The silence flowing thinly between us was thick with tension. Alex had no difficulty noticing that Nathan was angry. That was Alex's specialty. Whenever Nathan's mood became uncomfortable, I could sense it uncannily, even if I didn't know the reason. Maybe it was because I'd been scolded so much.
"Hey, are you mad?"

What made it even more frustrating was that Nathan was pretty and handsome even when he was angry. The sunlight pouring in from the kitchen window dyed Nathan's pale skin pearl-white, making Alex forget to look away and momentarily just admire his face. It was like a meticulously drawn painting.

My eyelashes, which seemed to have grown unusually light, looked faintly white. Nathan, blinking his long, curled lashes, twisted his lips. Alex rolled his eyes. I couldn't figure out the reason at all. "Yeah."
Nathan said curtly. Alex's eyes widened.
"Why?"
"Why?"
"Did I do something wrong?"

Alex retraced his actions. Nathan wasn't the type to bring up past matters, so he probably wasn't angry again about what happened at the movie theater yesterday. And I had even finished my shower quickly yesterday? It only took 15 minutes!
"Cancel the promise you made with Matthew Wayne for Wednesday."
Nathan said that. His voice was cold, so sharp it could cut. For a moment, Alex was speechless. My chest felt tight as if blocked, and then instantly, I felt aggrieved. Alex moved his lips.
"Do I have to?"

Actually, canceling the promise with Matthew wasn't a difficult thing. To begin with, Nathan's words were like law to Alex, and it wasn't like I desperately wanted to see Matthew either. To be clear, Alex Yeon cared deeply for Matthew Wayne.
But strangely, I didn't feel like obediently following along. Today, that simple word 'okay' felt grating. For one, it was upsetting to start fighting first thing in the morning. And besides...
"Isn't that obvious? Why would you see Matthew Wayne on Wednesday?"

Strangely, Nathan didn't really like Matthew. He wasn't outright rude, but he was always on guard whenever Alex was with Matthew. Before, Alex had somehow liked that Nathan seemed jealous, but today, that felt particularly hurtful. The images of the two women I had faced over the past two days flashed through Alex's mind.

Then, a sense of injustice surged. Clenching my mouth tightly, Alex furrowed his brows. Frankly speaking, there was no reason for Matthew to be persecuted. Matthew was the only person who had looked after Alex when Nathan wasn't around, and he was just a friend. But weren't there plenty of women around Nathan who weren't just friends?

If I were to nitpick, the doctor Nathan had watched a movie with was probably still at the hospital, and he had even gone on a date with Amy. To begin with, it was Nathan who had saved Amy, and we had even almost become *that* kind of relationship. Was that all? There could be dozens, or perhaps even hundreds, of women all over London that Alex couldn't even begin to guess about. It was only natural since Nathan was incredibly handsome, but still!
"But... I made the promise with Matthew first, so it doesn't seem right to cancel."

From Alex's mouth came an answer Nathan had never expected. This time, Nathan's eyes widened slightly. Alex closed his mouth tightly and slipped out of Nathan's embrace. Pulling my body away as if fleeing, I snatched the tray with toast and placed it on the dining table.
"You don't want to?"

Nathan immediately followed behind Alex. Looking down at Alex, who was pulling out a chair to sit, Nathan also pulled out a chair. Alex nodded. Because it was the first time I had rebelled against Nathan, a slight tremor ran deep in my heart. However, the weight of the inexplicable hurt was greater. I decided to prolong this rebellion a little more.
"Yeah, I don't want to. I'm going to see Matthew on Wednesday."
My heart almost stopped as I said it. Nathan asked back in a completely flat, dry voice.
"Do you mean that?"
The atmosphere suggested that if I said yes, big trouble would follow. But Alex bit his lips tightly and stubbornly insisted.
"Yeah, I mean it."

My voice, which had been quiet, gradually rose. The heightened atmosphere began to approach what people commonly call a 'fight.' Since I had never experienced this in my life, it felt awkward even as I spoke, but Alex didn't back down. Whenever I thought about backing down, Nathan's past women kept circling in my head. It felt like something was about to burst.
"Is that so?"
A nervous smile rose on Nathan's face. Alex saw Nathan laugh angrily for the first time. I held my breath for a moment. This was a bit scary.
"So, on your birthday, you want to hang out with a friend who's not your lover, is that it?"
And Alex finally realized the reason Nathan was angry. My heart sank for a moment.
Ah... Wednesday is my birthday.

I hadn't thought of it at all. Embarrassment washed over me. Since I had never celebrated my own birthday, I had completely forgotten it. To Alex, his birthday was merely the date his birth was registered and a number on paper.

So that's why Nathan was angry. He had every right to be angry. The confident, shameless feeling I'd had quickly crumbled. I should apologize. I was in the wrong. Just as Alex, having quickly changed his mind, was about to open his mouth, Nathan spoke lowly.
"Okay, fine. If you want to see me go out with someone else, then do that."

His tone was sharp. If I had thought about it just a little, I would have clearly realized that both I and Nathan were a bit more on edge than usual. But Alex was also not at ease. The moment I heard the words 'someone else,' I closed my mouth tightly.
*I've only had you, Nathan, my whole life.*

chapters.title: Chapter 138
paragraphs: Suddenly, Alex found himself thinking this: it was natural for people to meet. The times Nathan had disliked him, or when they had drifted apart due to Alex's own mistakes, were circumstances beyond his control.

But he didn't want to confront the remnants of those times directly. And amidst it all, resentment welled up towards Nathan, who was angry at him over Matthew—his only friend, and merely a friend at that. Unlike Alex, Nathan surely had plenty of people around him.
"If you want to be like that, fine. Unlike me, Nathan, you have plenty of people to meet. There's a girl who knows you wherever you go in London, right?"
That's why he had said it.
A remark that, for Alex Yeon, was excessively sharp and petty.
"What?"

Nathan stopped short. Alex closed his mouth, then pushed his chair back and stood up without even touching the toast prepared for breakfast. After giving voice to the substance of his resentment, he felt indescribably hurt.
"Unlike you, Nathan, you're the only person I've dated. And I don't understand why you're so hung up on my friend Matthew. I'm leaving first."
Yes, that was the problem.
The fact that, unlike Alex, who had known no one but Nathan his whole life, Nathan had a past. Apart from Nathan cherishing him the most, Alex childishly hated that they weren't the same.

It stung that Nathan's skillfulness came from others. Alex was jealous that he wasn't Nathan's first kiss. He hated that he wasn't the only one who knew Nathan's smiling face, and the assumption that they might have kissed Nathan was agonizing.
It was hard to accept that there was a Nathan he didn't know. That there were people who had claimed Nathan during the long blank period Alex himself had created.
And that Nathan didn't understand that.
"Alex, wait a minute. Why are you suddenly saying such things!.."
Nathan's expression rapidly crumbled. He, who rarely showed a startled look on his face, hurriedly followed Alex.
"I don't want to talk to you right now. Let's talk later."

Evading Nathan's attempt to grab his wrist, Alex quickly walked into the living room. He snatched up the bag and clothes he had prepared in advance and opened the front door just like that. Without even pretending to acknowledge Nathan chasing after him, Alex ran away. Like when he played soccer, at full speed.

It had been a while since he had used public transportation. He got confused about which bus to take from Shoreditch, so he had no choice but to take the Tube. Since the subway was a direct reminder of Nathan for Alex, his mood sank even further as he entered the station.

In stark contrast to his low spirits, the surroundings were overflowing with cheerful tourists enjoying the refreshing weather. Gazing gloomily at the tourists mingling with office workers, Alex took out his phone. It was to check if Nathan had contacted him, mere minutes after they had parted.
But as always on the Tube, there was no signal. Even if it connected, it would cut off quickly or the signal was weak.
*Stupid subway.*

Venting his unfounded anger on the subway, Alex arrived at the Police Station. Unlike when he lived deep in Zone 3, Shoreditch and the Police Station weren't far apart, so he arrived at headquarters incomparably faster than before.
However, it took longer than when Nathan used to drive him directly. Having stormed out of the house on his own, Alex was late.
"Oh, Alex."
In the elevator, Alex ran into Matthew. He looked gloomily at the main cause of the morning's discord. Matthew seemed unaware of anything. Of course, he wouldn't know anything.
"Hi."
"Seems like you really were sick."

At Alex's listless voice, Matthew expressed concern. Alex recalled the lie Nathan had told for him. He had said he had enteritis. Remembering his lover, who could even tell lies splendidly, Alex's heart quickly weakened. He wanted to go back right then and apologize. He turned his phone on again.
But there were no texts or calls.

Alex's face quickly darkened. His hand, which had opened the message window to send a text right away, hesitated. Nathan was the one who got angry first that morning. He could be the one to make up nicely. *What's so important about my birthday?* Alex thought as he asked Matthew a question.
"Matthew, did you know Wednesday is my birthday?"
"Yeah. July 7th, right? That's why I suggested hanging out."
"I see."
*It seems I was the only one who didn't know.* Since the Investigation Department knew each other's personal details, they celebrated each person's birthday briefly at the department level.

Alex's birthdays had always been like this. The last time he had celebrated his birthday properly was before his mother's separation. After that, he didn't bother celebrating his own birthday. Given that, there was no reason for him to attach meaning to his birthday. He knew Nathan's birthday but forgot his own. Occasionally, there were moments when the very act of being born and living felt overwhelming.
"You don't know your own birthday?"
Matthew sidled up next to him and asked probing questions. Alex shrugged his shoulders.
"It's February 14th."
"Then why don't you know your birthday?"
"It's not important."

Alex replied flatly. Matthew ruffled Alex's hair as if he found it ridiculous. The action that felt nice when Nathan did it felt quite unpleasant when Matthew did it. Alex weakly swatted Matthew's hand away.
"Why say that? Because your annoying boyfriend doesn't take care of it?"
Alex raised his head. *Annoying?* How could Matthew say that about someone as kind and soft-hearted as Nathan? Alex finally realized why Nathan wasn't fond of Matthew.
"Why is Nate annoying?"
"He's annoying because he glares at me like a ghost whenever he sees me."
"Don't say that. Nate is so soft-hearted."
Matthew twisted his mouth grotesquely and adjusted his glasses. Heaving a sigh, he changed the subject.
"Anyway, we're hanging out as planned on Wednesday, right?"

Alex blinked. His phone still hadn't rung, and Alex couldn't picture himself spending Wednesday, just two days away, happily with Nathan. He was confused. Moreover, he was the one who said he had to keep his prior promise. He couldn't take back his words.
"Yeah. I told him I was hanging out with you, and Nathan got mad. So I have no choice but to be with you."
"I swear I didn't do anything."
"I know."
The elevator doors opened. Alex listlessly stepped out into the corridor. The fluorescent lighting pouring down the corridor felt gloomy, unlike the summer sunlight.
His lackluster complexion made Sergeant Hayden believe Alex's lie without question. Insisting that Alex needed to recover his condition before the match, he assigned him to internal duties.

Maybe because he'd been smiling all the time since he and the department got along, his gloominess was very noticeable. Today, for some unknown reason, colleagues passing by bestowed chocolate upon Alex. Beside him, Anna made a compliment that sounded like an insult, saying he was like a dog receiving treats.
Even his favorite chocolate couldn't lift his mood, thanks to Nathan. On the contrary, as quitting time approached, Alex grew restless.
Because there had been no contact from Nathan whatsoever.

Now the situation had grown even more ambiguous. Unlike how he had behaved without any pride in front of Nathan, since he was the one who got angry first and Nathan truly hadn't contacted him, stubbornness had set in. A standoff had developed where neither side had done anything particularly wrong.
Alex decided to hold onto a sliver of hope anyway. That Nathan might contact him around quitting time.

But even as 6 o'clock passed, then 7 o'clock, Alex's phone remained silent. Nathan, who just three days ago had sent considerate texts saying he'd pick him up, said nothing. Matthew approached Alex, who was sitting there ready to leave work. He tapped Alex on the shoulder.
"You alive?"
"Not really."
"Damn, looks like you fought because of me."
Matthew scratched his head vigorously, then asked Alex again.
"What are you going to do?"
Looking up at Matthew from his seated position, Alex abruptly stood up and said.
"Let's go."
"Where?"
"Your place."
"Why my place?"
"I'm sleeping there tonight."

chapters.title: Chapter 139
paragraphs: At this point, Alex was truly afraid. Nathan seemed angrier than he could cope with. The bravado that had timidly shown his face until lunchtime had long since disappeared. He was afraid that if he went in like this, he'd end up fighting with Nathan again. More accurately, he was afraid of being scolded. He realized that being angry was exhausting, and Nathan had a lot more practice at it. Getting angry at Nathan was something Alex's mind couldn't handle. He didn't want to get angry ever again.
"That doesn't seem like a good idea."
Alex didn't answer. As he stubbornly held his bag and stared, Matthew made a strange sound and ruffled his own hair. He stared at the ceiling and spoke, his voice grave.
"Dinner is lasagna."
The contract was sealed. Alex nodded. Matthew picked up his car keys and went ahead as if he were doing something he didn't want to do.

Back in the present, Alex was slaving away in Matthew's kitchen, making lasagna. It was a dish that required a lot of effort, one he rarely made even for Nathan. The fact that he was making it for Matthew made him feel strangely sorry for himself.
"But did you really fight because of his birthday?"
Matthew approached Alex, who was spreading a generous amount of meat sauce between the layers of lasagna sheets. Leaning sideways against the kitchen counter with a beer can in hand, he asked.
"I don't really know either. I was just feeling a bit down."
"That's weird. You're always in a good mood when you're next to that guy. Has he cooled off already?"
"No!"
That was impossible. Alex answered, startled by the question. The question alone made him feel like he had to deny it. He felt like sprinkling holy water on Matthew.
"It's just... Nathan, unlike me, has dated a lot of people..."
"Because he's dated a lot?"
"I ran into someone he kept dating over the weekend."
"Wow, impressive."
When Alex stopped spreading the sauce with the spatula, Matthew closed his mouth.

“Seeing that stuff kept happening, I felt bad. I was the one who said I'd meet with you without even knowing it was my birthday, but then Nathan got angry first and suddenly I felt hurt... Honestly, I don't even know why I'm acting like this."
Matthew took a sip of his beer and then laughed this time. Wondering if this was a new way of teasing him, Alex watched quietly, and Matthew waved his hand dismissively.
"No, I was just amazed that a day would come when you'd say such things. It's clear you two are really well-matched."
"Why?"
"You're dating normally, aren't you? Feeling jealous, fighting..."

Matthew finished his beer in one gulp and placed the can on the counter. Leaning his elbows on the counter and bending his upper body, he smiled brightly while making eye contact. Since he had taken off his glasses at home, his eyes curved in a cool, sweeping arc.
"You used to keep everything bottled up, just enduring and accepting what your parents did... But now you're finally doing what *you* want, aren't you?"
"Even though we fought?"

"It's only natural that people can fight. No matter how well-matched you are, I think that can happen. Don't be afraid of that. Sometimes conflicts like this can be helpful. Instead of holding things in, you need to clash and resolve them together. Cases are like that too."
Alex quietly pondered Matthew's words. He, who had been meticulously spreading the sauce, nodded.
"Thank you."
"So don't be so gloomy. He'll probably come looking for you anyway."

The words that followed were a bit strange. The moment he opened his lips to ask what that meant, the doorbell rang. Matthew said, 'The time has come,' and shuffled out of the kitchen in his slippers like someone who had anticipated something. The doorbell rang once more. At the sound, which seemed to urge them, Alex also came out of the kitchen.

With a sigh and a gesture of reluctance, Matthew opened the door. As the door opened, a tall person came into view. Nathan was standing there, still wearing his white doctor's coat. His hair was disheveled as if he had been running, and his expression was intense. An icy silence settled between the three of them.
Matthew was the first to speak.
"For the record, I didn't do anything."
Nathan looked at Matthew with a displeased face for a moment, then opened his mouth with a sigh.
"Thank you for telling me."

Matthew looked at Nathan, taken aback. Alex was torn between the joy of seeing Nathan and the fear of being scolded, but the joy quickly overwhelmed the fear. After a day without calls or texts, just seeing Nathan's face brought tears to his eyes.
"Nate..."
When he called his name softly, Nathan strode into the entranceway. Matthew slowly backed away, retreating completely inside the house.
"How did you know I was here?"
"Where else would you run off to?"
Nathan looked down at Alex with an expression that said he was going crazy, let out a long sigh, and rubbed his face with his hands. He swept his hair back nervously, then closed and opened his eyes.
"Were you planning to sleep over here? Not coming home?"
"You... seemed angry..."
"You were the one who was angry."
Nathan bit his lip. His chest heaved heavily, and then he pulled Alex toward him. Enveloped in his arms in an instant, Alex quickly hugged Nathan back. Nathan spoke in a weary voice.
"If you were trying to drive me insane, congratulations. I got nothing done all day."
The palm holding his back pressed hard against Alex. His fingers dug into his skin through the thin fabric, squeezing tightly. Alex raised his head slightly and carefully examined Nathan's eyes.
"Why didn't you contact me?.."

Even though he hesitated, he asked what he was curious about. Nathan buried his face in his shoulder. Like someone who had found something lost, he didn't let go of Alex. From behind, they could hear Matthew muttering about them doing all sorts of things in someone else's house, but they both ignored it.
"You said you didn't want to talk to me."
"So you waited?"
"Yeah."

So that's what it was. His doubt was resolved. Then, the lump in his heart melted away instantly. Instead, another emotion welled up, and Alex rubbed his forehead against Nathan's chest and whispered. *My boyfriend is so thoughtful.*
"Sorry."
"No. I said harsh things. I'm the one who should apologize. Let's go first. Let's just get out of here."
He nodded his head eagerly. Nathan let out another sigh and then cupped Alex's cheeks with both hands. His deep green eyes stared intently at Alex. From behind, Matthew shouted.
"You have to finish my lasagna before you go!"
Finally recognizing Matthew's existence, Alex turned to look back. Nathan turned Alex's head back and imprisoned him in his embrace.
“Buy some to eat. I'll send you the money."
At those words, Matthew got annoyed.
"I told you, what Alex makes tastes better than store-bought!"
"That's exactly why I don't want to let you eat it."
Nathan said mercilessly. With an expression that seemed to say his foundation was crumbling, Matthew shouted at Alex.
"Alex, how can you not say he's annoying even after seeing that?"
With a face that asked why he would ask the obvious, Alex glanced at Matthew and said.
"Yeah. He's cute."

As if praising him, Nathan stroked his hair. This touch. It was best when Nathan, not someone else, was the one stroking it. A smile spread across his face, which had been wearing a gloomy expression all day.
Although they had made up, the way home was quiet. Alex sat stiffly upright in the passenger seat, stealing glances at Nathan and repeating the pattern of their eyes meeting.

His feelings were strange. Living together, there had been plenty of times when Nathan came home late or he was late, so they couldn't see each other all day. Yet, today in particular, it felt like they had been apart for a long time.
Matthew said fighting was okay too, but he still didn't want to do it. Having gotten angry at Nathan, it was an even more difficult thing for Alex himself.
Nathan didn't speak until they arrived home. He opened his mouth right after finishing parking in the garage.
"I know Matthew Wayne is your friend."
Turning off the ignition, he pulled out the car key and continued.
"That guy was by your side during the time I wasn't there."
In the tranquil silence, Nathan turned his head. Their eyes met.
"That's why I don't like it. Because it feels like you rely on him more than me."

chapters.title: Chapter 140
paragraphs: Nathan sighed, looking at Alex with a sunken face. He rubbed his forehead and apologized.
"Sorry for forcing you."
"No!"
As Nathan kept apologizing, Alex hurriedly grabbed his white hands with both of his. Clutching them tightly, Alex hastily continued.
"I'm similar too. It's something that happened because of me, but anyway, I haven't seen you for a long time, right? While I was seeing all the people you dated, that..."
Nathan drew closer. Stroking Alex's hands that were holding him, he asked.
"That?"
"Je, jealousy... I was jealous."

My cheeks burned hot. I felt heat rise all over my body and lowered my gaze. I never thought I'd say the word 'jealousy' out loud. Especially to Nathan. This way of being jealous didn't suit me and made me feel like a narrow-minded person, but my heart felt much lighter.
"You were jealous?"
"Uhm, yes."

Following Alex's lowered gaze, Nathan slightly bowed his head. The face looking up from below as he bent over looked exceptionally pretty, making my whole body feel even hotter. Nathan's eyes narrowed into crescents.
"You know how to be jealous now. Before, you didn't even seem interested."
His tone sounded like praise. Nathan looked pleased. Emboldened by his rarely seen smiling expression, Alex cautiously gained courage.
"No. I was always good at it."
To receive more praise, Alex appealed.
"You just let me send Amy off when she confessed?"
"Back then, I, I didn't know we were dating..."
"Really?"
Nathan's voice softened like melting. Alex nodded and gradually spoke the truth he had kept bottled up for a long time.
"I'm saying I was jealous of those Alphas who said you were pretty back in high school too."
"Full of personal feelings."
"But don't get me wrong. It's not because you seemed like an Omega, it's just that I like you!.."
The words didn't finish. My lips were blocked. The words hastily added, fearing he might get hurt if he was treated like an Omega, which he disliked, were swallowed into Nathan's mouth.
Squeezing the hands holding him, Alex tightly closed his eyes. His body had already begun to tremble.

Dry lips rubbed softly. Noses touched, and the faint sound of a small exhale resonated. As the rustling of their clothes filled the air, Nathan gradually moved closer. He deepened the kiss, clinging to Alex's lips, sucking gently. A stifled breath escaped, scattering into the space between them.

As if compensating for the time spent apart, even though they kissed countless times, this moment felt new to Alex every time. The purple night at the beach where the sunset had set always came to mind, and he was overwhelmed by the reality that Nathan, who had whispered 'I like you' over the quietly echoing waves, was right before his eyes. Haa, as he opened his mouth, a tongue slipped into the parted gap.

Tilting his head slightly, Nathan pushed his tongue in. As the tongue gently rubbed his palate, a *mmph* sound immediately leaked out. As Alex tried to writhe backward because it was ticklish, Nathan held him and tickled his palate even more.
Writhing his waist, Alex let out sounds like *uhng*, *ng*, flinching. A sensation akin to pleasure prickled up like goosebumps.

After tormenting him for quite a while, Nathan changed his objective. Leading Alex, who didn't know what to do and clumsily entangled his tongue, he deepened the kiss. The light kiss made a moist sound and gradually grew heated. Each time their tongues tangled, his lower abdomen grew warmer.
Around the time he finally clearly realized he was aroused, Nathan slowly pulled his lips away. The green gaze holding him was as dense as a wet forest.
"I love you, Alex."
"Me too, haa, I love you..."

His heart swelled up fluffy and grew in size. His insides felt so inflated that if pierced with a needle, it wouldn't be strange if they burst. As he whispered earnestly, Nathan wiped his moist, reddened lips with his thumb.
"You can be as jealous as you want, but don't make me lose my mind like you did today."
"I won't."
"If you do... I don't know what to do. You said I've met many people, but you're the only one I've cared about and loved. You're the most precious to me."
It had been a while since he saw Nathan's vulnerable side. Nathan saying he didn't know what to do looked genuinely perplexed, so Alex curiously observed that face.
"The only one I want to keep holding, the only one I feel like I'll go crazy wanting to hug every day... is just you."
Blushing at the last words, Alex smiled shyly. Hesitating, Alex firmly pulled Nathan's neck and hugged him.
"Me, me too. If it weren't for you, I would never have done th, that."

Alex softened the confession, implying that he wouldn't have let Nathan be the 'active' partner if it weren't for his feelings. Nathan, who laughed softly, gently stroked his back and held his waist tightly. Fingers rubbing over the thin t-shirt evoked a strange sensation.
"That's right."
As he unburdened himself one by one, his mood gradually lightened. Gaining courage, Alex continued.
"And my birthday, of course spending it with you is the best. I didn't even know Wednesday was my birthday. That's why I said okay to what Matthew said."
"You try to remember other people's birthdays, so why don't you know your own?"
"I've never celebrated it..."
Nathan let out a deep sigh and hugged Alex tightly. After staying silent for a while, he stroked Alex's head and made a suggestion.
"Then let's celebrate all together on Wednesday. As you said, it's a prior engagement too."
"No, it's fine."

He meant it. Of course, Matthew and Anna were precious too, but since it was his first birthday celebrating with Nathan, spending it just the two of them was much better. Nathan looked at him as if he was cute for a moment, then shook his head.
"Let's get celebrated a lot, Alex. And we'll spend the weekend just the two of us."
"You got the weekend off?"
"Yeah."
Alex's face brightened upon learning he could spend consecutive weekends with Nathan, following last weekend. It already felt like receiving a gift.
"Yeah, let's do that!"
"Shall we celebrate at home?"
"I'm fine with anything."
"What kind of answer is that."
Nathan gently bit his earlobe. Like a cat. Alex smiled slightly and hugged Nathan tightly. A faint scent spread distinctly.
"Just you taking care of it, I'm really fine with anything."
Nathan didn't respond to that. Putting strength into his embracing arms, he stroked Alex's back for a long time.

Tuesday arrived. The night before, the two looked into what to do for the birthday party. After washing up, snuggled in Nathan's arms, they searched together on a tablet. They'd gotten sidetracked on the sofa with a brief, heated moment after Alex accidentally brushed his hand against Nathan's thigh—or, more accurately, *his*—well, it was impossible to ignore! But anyway, the rest of the night was spent planning the party.
Nathan kept going into sites filled with cone hats and party supplies that seemed fit for children. He was aware that when he was with Nathan, he acted no differently from when he was in high school.

But no matter what, it didn't suit someone now in their late twenties to wear a cone hat. When Alex stubbornly insisted on his own opinion, Nathan temporarily changed the subject. Talk about food came up.
He briefly felt daunted by the talk of upper-class cuisine he couldn't relate to.

When Alex said he'd cook himself, Nathan said he didn't want to share his cooking with Matthew Wayne. Finding that cute, Alex laughed out loud. So it was decided that Nathan would ask his brother to bring a chef and a party planner. Alex would have absolutely no connection to it.

With neither cake nor cooking to handle, all that remained was indoor decoration. Since it was already Tuesday, they decided to go shopping together after work. Talking about plans for his own birthday party, of all things, made him feel strange. It was the first time since his distant childhood, which he couldn't even remember.

Nevertheless, because he liked how much Nathan cared for him, the unpleasant sentiments tied to his birthday lost their place. It felt like peeling off old, damp, moldy wallpaper and painting over it, finally shedding the old memories that clung to his life.
